title: Portrait and Figure Sculpture
Description: Sculpting the human form directly from the model.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Introduction to Ceramics
Description: Development of personal expression using the ceramic process.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Ceramics - Introductory Pottery
Description: An introductory course on pottery/vessel forms and aesthetics made on the potters wheel. Will include glazing and firing technology.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Jewelry and Metals: Design and Construction
Description: Introduces hands-on techniques and conceptual topics associated with the creation of jewelry and objects. Emphasizes the connection to traditional and contemporary craft and art practices/movements and frames these within the arena of current and historical material culture.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Textile Foundations
Description: Woven and non-woven textile techniques and the relation between process and material.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Surface Design
Description: Focus on basic design issues and color as they apply to continuous patterns.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Introduction to Digital Imaging
Description: An introduction into the digital means of image capturing, creation and research, and the broadcast and output of these files in art and design practice.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Hypermedia
Description: A combination of theory and practice in contemporary art and creative professions. As a studio course, the study of contemporary pop culture and its use of modern devices for creative expression will take place through both lecture and studio activity.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Hypermedia
Description: A combination of theory and practice in contemporary art and creative professions. As a studio course, the study of contemporary pop culture and its use of modern devices for creative expression will take place through both lecture and studio activity.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Drawing
Description: Advanced drawing stressing individual projects and experimental approaches.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Drawing: Drawing in Conceptual Space
Description: Practice using drawing to create and define conceptual spaces. Students are taught strategies for using conceptual space as co- informative to the pictorial space of drawing.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Transparent Watercolor
Description: Transparent watercolor including landscape, still life, and the human figure. Personal imagery and non-representational painting will also be explored.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Painting: Color and Application
Description: An intensive exploration of the mechanics and effect of color in the painted image. This course builds on basic color theory and Beginning Painting to give students tools for the sophisticated manipulation of color in their paintings and examines how color is perceived as a phenomenon and interpreted as content.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Aqueous Media
Description: Synthetic media (acrylics), casein, and water media other than transparent watercolor.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Painting: Strategies of Abstraction
Description: Introduction to acrylic paint and basic studio practice and theory in abstract painting. Students study the impulse toward abstraction in modernism and build upon various drawing and painting strategies and techniques to explore abstraction as an idea and artistic practice.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Introduction to Figure Painting
Description: Compositional, expressive, and anatomical aspects of painting the human figure from direct observation.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Painting Studio Concepts
Description: Inquiry into varied approaches in painting, both representational and non-representational. Experimental attitudes and personal ideas and solutions are encouraged.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Painting: Hybrids
Description: An interdisciplinary course that engages the history, mechanics, and language of painting as it manifests across medium and genre. Students will learn about contemporary artists who use painting in a hybrid way and will create works of art in the studio that address painting in a post-medium-specific time.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: The Figure as Subject and the Narrative Impulse
Description: Examines the figure as both subject and object in contemporary studio practice. Students develop and explore their own unique visual language and subjective figuration while examining the relationship between narrative ideas and pictorial structure.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Figure Painting
Description: Painting the human figure emphasizing structure and painting techniques. Media include oil and acrylic paints and grounds.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Painting Materials and Techniques
Description: Historical techniques such as egg tempera, fresco, encaustic, and Venetian mode oil painting as they apply to contemporary needs; modern materials such as alkyd and polymer resins are introduced. Consideration is given to the properties of pigments, binders, grounds, and supports.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Black and White Photography
Description: Camera skills and processing techniques for black and white negatives and prints with emphasis on visual concepts and articulation of ideas.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Video Concepts and Practice
Description: An introduction to time-based means of visual expression through video and other constructs. Students will develop technical skills using digital capture and editing, developing proficiency concerning the role of light, space, time, composition, editing, and sequencing, within a conceptual framework of ideas, expression, and communication.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Color Photography
Description: Color photography investigates color theory, lighting, utilizing color for conceptual concerns, digital printing, and workflows. Concepts are presented within the context of contemporary trends and practices.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Film and Camera
Description: Investigations into advanced camera practices with selected film formats, such as 35mm, medium format, and/or large format, plus digital. This course will cover techniques involving camera handling, lighting, film processing/printing, scanning, and the development of student projects. Past and present practices will be given equal consideration in their historical contexts.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Large Format Photography II
Description: Advanced Studio Practices in large format photography. Includes advanced techniques, historical and contemporary practices, with emphasis on portfolio development utilizing a large format camera.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Internship in Photography
Description: Practical experience with professionals including photographers, designers, and computer specialists. Independent projects and research with editors, curators, teachers, and historians. Assist photography faculty in creative work with emphasis on studio and lab production.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Constructed Image in Photography
Description: Exploration of photographing constructed scenes both in the studio and on location. Students will investigate the conceptual expression of an idea through a constructed situation with emphasis on artificial lighting techniques. Discussion of historic and contemporary works as well as individual portfolio development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Printmaking: Relief
Description: Various relief printmaking techniques with concentrated work in the processes of woodcut, wood engraving, and linoleum cut.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Printmaking: Etching
Description: Various printmaking techniques with concentrated work on intaglio.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Printmaking: Lithography
Description: Various printmaking techniques with concentrated work on lithography.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Printmaking: Screen Printing
Description: Exploration of a variety of techniques for creating limited edition screen prints.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Digital Printmaking
Description: The use of software such as Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator to create imagery. Students will learn to print images on large format printers to make ink jet prints. Students will also combine digital printing with traditional printmaking methods. Technical mastery will be emphasized along with conceptual development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Construction in Metal
Description: Beginning welding techniques and the use of metal in sculptural composition.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Intermediate Constuction in Metal
Description: Advanced welding techniques and the use of mixed media.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Sculpture: The Subtractive Process I
Description: Direct carving in wood or stone.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Sculpture in Spatial Context I
Description: Students will be encouraged to expand their studio practice to encompass sculptural object-making, installation art, environmental art, and performance. Instruction includes studio work, lectures, and discussions on topics in contemporary art.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Sculpture: The Subtractive Process II
Description: Carving wood and stone, both representational and non-representational, with emphasis on aesthetic development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Fundamentals of Casting Metal Sculpture
Description: Fundamental techniques for producing metal sculpture using refractory molds and sand casting.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Intermediate Casting in Metal
Description: Production of sculpture in refractory molds and sand casting, both representational and non-representational, with emphasis on aesthetic development and mixed media.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Intermediate Portrait and Figure Sculpture
Description: Sculpting the human form based on the live model. Anatomy, composition, and sculptural techniques are emphasized as means for creative expression.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Wood as a Sculptural Medium
Description: Processes include carving with hand, pneumatic, and electric tools. Stationary machine tools will also be incorporated.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Performance Art
Description: Explores performance art’s utilization of the body as a site for meaning and tool for expression. In addition to traditional performances, students will have the opportunity to design and implement interventions, collaborations, and participatory works.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Installation
Description: Investigates the complexities of installation, the decentralized viewer, the utilization of space, and context. Students will research the history of installation art and its influence on sculpture, photography, authorship, and spectatorship.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: The Object
Description: Examines the complex identities of objects. Objects have stories that define memory, identity, and technology. Students will produce projects that explore the importance of objects in contemporary life, their layered compositions, and the implications for artists.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Intermediate Ceramics
Description: Sculptural and functional ceramic forms with an emphasis on personal expression and individual style.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Intermediate Pottery
Description: An intermediate course on pottery/vessel forms and aesthetics made on the potters wheel. Will include glazing and firing technology.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Jewelry: Movement
Description: Students will develop and refine technical and conceptual abilities by making mechanisms for jewelry. Fundamental tools and techniques will be introduced over the course of the semester. Students will investigate movement by making chains, hinges, and findings with an awareness to body as site.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Jewelry: Fabrication and Setting
Description: Students will develop and refine technical and conceptual abilities through fabricating with sheet metal and stone setting. Fundamental tools and techniques will be introduced over the course of the semester. Students will work toward refining technical abilities and solving design challenges in innovative ways.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Jewelry: The Multiple
Description: An introduction to the techniques utilized to make multiples for jewelry and small scale objects. The course will consist of a number of exercises and assignments to familiarize students and enable them to become proficient with lost wax casting, carving wax, modeling wax, stone setting in wax, and mold making for the purpose of making multiples and/or repetitive elements.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Jewelry: Historical and Traditional Techniques
Description: Utilizing the rich 3,000-year-plus history of the field as a springboard, students will learn ancient techniques such as granulation, kuemboo, chasing, repousse, and filigree. Students will then use these techniques in a contemporary manner.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Moving Metal: Cups, Spoons, and Objects
Description: The various metal-forming processes, which include forging, raising, and fabrication as they relate to hollowware, flatware, and functional objects. Technical expertise and the understanding of the properties of metal will be developed while exploring form and function.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: CAD/CAM for Objects and Jewelry
Description: Introduces students to digital tools used in visual art practices. Emphasis will be on computer-aided 2D and 3D design, modeling, and manufacturing using the latest software available. Students will leave with a foundation to pursue further production, prototyping, and modeling goals to design and create objects and/or jewelry.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: CAD/CAM for Objects and Jewelry
Description: Introduces students to digital tools used in visual art practices. Emphasis will be on computer-aided 2D and 3D design, modeling, and manufacturing using the latest software available. Students will leave with a foundation to pursue further production, prototyping, and modeling goals to design and create objects and/or jewelry.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Fusing Glass to Metal for Jewelry and Objects
Description: An introduction to hands-on techniques of enameling, fusing glass to metal under high heat conditions. Techniques include sifting, cloisonné, basse taille, champleve, grisaille, sgraffito, and stenciling. Techniques will be applied to create jewelry and small objects. The course will emphasize the connection to traditional and contemporary craft and art practices and will frame these within the arena of current and historical material culture.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Jewelry and Objects: Surface/Color/Solid
Description: An introduction to the theoretical and technical use of color to create jewelry and small objects using nontraditional materials such as casting plastics and powder coating, as well as traditional color applications such as chemical patinas. Emphasis will be placed on the understanding of color as it applies to surface and form in historical and contemporary practice.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Weaving I
Description: Utilization of the floor loom to study basic weaves and their application to hand-crafted and industrial textiles.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Screen-Printing
Description: Utilization of screen printing for fabric printing, including simple stencils and photographic processes.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Studio Practices
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of a faculty member.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Design for Industry
Description: In-depth study and insight into various textile companies within the fabric industry.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Material Futures
Description: Production of new and innovative modern textiles through use of under-utilized, often overlooked textile techniques.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Transmedia
Description: Conceptual methods of visual thinking found in New Media, focusing on time-based media, performance, installation, and computer generated imaging. This course encourages the thoughtful engagement in complex ideas through visual application, not limited to any single configuration or vocabulary of art.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: CAD and Fabrication I
Description: The first part of a comprehensive exploration of computer-aided design and fabrication from concept development and digital modeling through rapid prototyping processes. Using CAD software and state-of-the-art CNC machining, students are able to build detailed models and fabricate finished objects out of a variety of materials.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Digital Video I
Description: This is a basic production course in video as a medium for artistic expression. Students learn the skills working with digital video equipment and non-linear editing systems. Strategies for using video as an art-making tool are explored. Contemporary video artists are viewed and discussed.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interdisciplinary Art I
Description: Exploration and research of various topics using interdisciplinary methods. Encourages the thoughtful engagement of complex ideas through visual application, not limited to any single configuration or vocabulary of art. Collaborative teaching, visiting lecturers, and field trips create the dynamic learning environment.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interdisciplinary Art I
Description: Exploration and research of various topics using interdisciplinary methods. Encourages the thoughtful engagement of complex ideas through visual application, not limited to any single configuration or vocabulary of art. Collaborative teaching and visiting lecturers create the dynamic learning environment.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interactive Art I
Description: Exploration of realtime interactive audio-visual/mechanical systems in the service of art. Students create, control, effect, and transform digital media in realtime using custom hardware and software.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: E-Gadgets for Experimental Media
Description: Students learn the basic principles of electronics along with hands-on techniques for incorporating it into their work. An introduction to electronic components, circuits, motors, and actuators available for integration into art projects. A look at various forms of motor control, and the necessary means to power these devices.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Directed Study in Drawing
Description: Independent projects for advanced drawing and painting majors.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Figure Drawing/Anatomy
Description: Figure drawing with consideration of the human skeletal and muscular systems, surface anatomy, and bio-mechanical concerns.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Drawing
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Senior Exit in Drawing
Description: Projects in drawing towards the presentation of a BFA exhibition. The course includes preparation for professional activity and/or application to graduate school, and should be taken during last semester of studio course work.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Directed Study in Painting
Description: Advanced independent study for drawing and painting majors. Studio meetings arranged.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Senior Exit in Painting
Description: Projects in painting towards the presentation of a BFA exhibition. The course includes preparation for professional activity and/or application to graduate school, and should be taken during last quarter of studio course work.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Studio Concepts
Description: Advanced inquiry into varied approaches in generating and developing images, both representational and non- representational. Modern and contemporary techniques as well as mixed media approaches. Experimental attitudes, ideas and solutions are encouraged. Students will expand their awareness of social, historical and critical issues, with an emphasis on contemporary art and criticism.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Contemporary Applications of Historic Painting Materials
Description: Introduction to historical methods: egg tempera, fresco, encaustic, casein and Venetian oil painting in combination with modern materials: acrylic polymers and alkyd resins. Consideration is given to the properties of pigments, binders, grounds, and supports and how they inform contemporary studio practice.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Painting
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Workshop in Photography and Expanded Media
Description: Advanced studio applications of lens, time-based, and expanded media practices. Students will develop intensive, individualized research practices within a conceptual framework. Regular critiques will support portfolio development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Workshop in Photography and Expanded Media II
Description: Advanced studio applications of lens, time-based, and expanded media practices. Students will extend and enhance individualized research practices within a conceptual framework. Regular critiques will support portfolio development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Photography in Time
Description: Exploration of the evolution of photography into the moving picture. Working primarily with digital video, the course will cover the techniques of shooting and editing video, focusing on the conceptual expression of time-based photography.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Special Topics in Photography
Description: Major historical movements in photography including comparative studies of contemporary trends and criticism with an emphasis on research and the development of library archives.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Sound in Art
Description: Exploration of artists who use sound in their art or as their art. Sound is a medium to be explored in its creation and installation. This course will introduce sound as an expressive and exploratory tool for studio research practice.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Senior Exhibition and Portfolio
Description: Creation and presentation of a finished body of original work in photography for BFA degree, with a written statement concerning the work.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Photography Practice and Theory
Description: Studies on the practices and theories of selected movements in photography, considering the dual nature of image function and concept, from original analog invention to digital forms of expanded media. Topics include documentary, fictional, experimental, and conceptual roles with photographers on practice, scholars, and critics on theory.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: External Internship in Photography
Description: Practical experience with professionals, including photographers, designers, curators, computer specialists, and other art-related professions. Assist professionals in practical and creative projects with emphasis on work experience outside the academic environment.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Constructed Image in Photography
Description: Exploration of photographing constructed scenes both in the studio and on location. Investigation of the conceptual expression of an idea through a constructed situation with emphasis on artificial lighting techniques. Discussion of historic and contemporary works as well as individual portfolio development.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Constructed Image in Photograpy II
Description: Advanced studio practices in constructed photographic scenes both in the studio and on location. Includes advanced techniques, historical and contemporary practices, with emphasis on portfolio development utilizing the methods of constructed situations with emphasis on artificial lighting techniques.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Techniques in Photography
Description: Techniques for advanced handling of equipment and materials in photographic processing. Advanced techniques in film exposure and processing, darkroom printing, and digital image processing and printing.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Social Documentary Photography and Video
Description: Storytelling through documentary photography and video research. Introduction to the history and practice of documentary work as well as studio practice. Students will develop projects engaging social documentary work through photo essays, documentary videos, and digital storytelling.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Photography
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Alternative Photography
Description: Alternative photographic processes in printing and presentation. These include non-traditional cameras, historic printing processes such as cyanotype, salt prints, van dyke and platinum/palladium printing, as well as contemporary non-traditional presentation materials and methods.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Landscape Photography
Description: The practice of landscape photography and the recording of place. Includes an overview of the history and practice of landscape photography. Students will develop studio projects that engage both natural and urban landscapes, considering the social, political, and personal engagements with the earth.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Printmaking: Internship
Description: Practical experiences with related professions in the field of print, paper and book collections, and print shops; work with printmaking faculty in the studio or print facility.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Senior Exit in Printmaking
Description: Individual research, creation, and presentation of a finished body of original work in printmaking for senior exhibition or portfolio with written statement and visual documentation.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Introduction to Book Arts
Description: Introduction to hand bookbinding and artist's books as a form of artistic expression. Examination of the book as art with a focus on the book as a carefully designed object with an emphasis on design, planning, content development, construction, and the application of allied fields into book processes.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Introduction to Book Arts: Papermaking
Description: Introduction to the use of handmade paper as a versatile and sustainable medium for creative expression in two- and three-dimensional applications. Survey of traditional and contemporary hand papermaking processes, the introduction of the tools and techniques, and the exploration of the materiality and science of paper.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Printmaking: Special Topics I
Description: Special projects for advanced students.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Print Studio
Description: Advanced lithography, etching, screenprinting, relief, or monoprints stressing aesthetic development and technical achievement.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Letterpress
Description: Letterpress printing and book arts as they relate to the creative synthesis of text and image in book and broadside form.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Book Studio
Description: This course will focus on the book as an art form and/or letterpress projects for advanced students. Aesthetic development and technical achievement will be stressed.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Printmaking
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Casting in Metal
Description: Continued exploration of cast metal and mixed media in the creation of sculpture.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Portrait and Figure Sculpture
Description: Refinement of technical and expressive skills in sculpting the human form.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Sculpture and Spatial Context II
Description: Production of a fully realized three-dimensional maquette or full scale sculpture beginning with drawing of objects, landscape, architecture, and the human figure.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Sculpture: The Subtractive Process III
Description: Refinement of technical and expressive skills in carving stone.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Contruction in Metal
Description: Refinement of technical and expressive skills in construction in metal and mixed media.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Studio Art Capstone
Description: Curatorial practices leading to the presentation of a B.F.A. exhibition, including preparation, curation, and installation of work in gallery exhibitions.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Sculpture
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Ceramics
Description: This advanced ceramics course will combine studio practice and a seminar format. The studio component will provide ample time to concentrate on specific projects agreed upon by faculty and student. The seminar component of this course is designed to engage the group in dialog concerning different pertinent subjects chosen to disseminate information and exercise creative and critical thinking skills.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Kiln Design and Construction
Description: This course is designed for ceramics majors and will cover the history, design, and construction of a variety of kilns.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Ceramics
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Senior Exit Show in Ceramics
Description: Independent study directed towards the presentation of a BFA exhibition, including preparation for a career and/or application to graduate school.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Jewelry
Description: Exploration of advanced skills and techniques in jewelry. Emphasis will be on research and concept development while enhancing technical and problem solving skills. Material studies and thematic explorations will drive the assignments. Discussions on historical and contemporary metalsmiths will advance skills in critical thinking.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: History and Theory of Modern Objects in Visual and Material Culture
Description: The examination of forms, uses, and meanings of objects, images, and environments in everyday life. The study and practice of visual and material culture with bridges between studio craft, design, and art.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Metalwork
Description: Exploration of advanced skills and techniques as they relate to metalsmithing. Emphasis will be on research, concept development, and material investigation while enhancing technical skills and developing skills in critical thinking. Exploration of material and process to advance personal expression is encouraged.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: BFA Project in Jewelry or Metalwork
Description: The purpose of this class is to create a cohesive body of work that supports the continued development of a student's professional portfolio. There will be an emphasis on research analysis and evaluation of aesthetic and conceptual decisions.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Jewelry/Metal
Description: Individual research projects under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: CAD for Textiles
Description: Computer-aided design using various computer programs for textile designs.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: BFA Project in Fabric Design
Description: Directed independent study towards the presentation of a BFA exhibition, including preparation for professional activity and/or application to graduate school.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Advanced Weaving
Description: Woven structures on multi-harness looms.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Fabric Design in Japan
Description: Study program in Japan incorporating intensive studio work and field trips to collections and sites.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Fabric Design
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Special Topics in Art and Technology
Description: For upper-level undergraduate and graduate students who are working within expanded forms of installation, video, sound, performance, and interactive electronic arts. Students are expected to work independently setting their own projects and goals. The class combines theory, studio, critique, and discussion.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: CAD and Fabrication
Description: Aspects of computer aided design and CNC fabricating. Utilization of state-of-the-art fabrication facilities: haptic sensible technology, 3D stereo thermojet lithographic printing, and our 3-axis CNC router.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Exit Studio
Description: This studio course facilitates the development of a cohesive body of work for an exit exhibition. Research, creation, and presentation of an exhibition will be required for graduation. Students will also work on a portfolio with a written statement and visual documentation as preparation for professional activities and/or graduate school.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Digital Video II
Description: Introduction to more sophisticated processes in video production and post production. Further refinement of digital editing techniques and visual effects are covered. Storyboards, scripting, and content are emphasized. The class views, reads, and discusses significant contemporary works and related critical writings.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interdisciplinary Art II
Description: An advanced course exploring and researching various topics in art through interdisciplinary methods.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interdisciplinary Art II
Description: An advanced course exploring and researching various topics in art through interdisciplinary methods.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Interactive Art II
Description: An advanced course in realtime interactive audio-visual/mechanical systems.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Video Installation
Description: Combination of studio practice and research with critiques of student work to examine the vernacular and practices of video installation. Students experiment with single and multi-channel video as monitor displays, projections, and/or part of larger scale projects. Site specific concerns of private/public space, narrative, identity, reception, and aesthetics will be the basis for discussion.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Internet Art Studio
Description: Examination of the current state of artistic practice on the Internet and facilitation of the production of new works for networked audiences. The course consists of concurrent research and studio components joined by critical theory.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Web Site Design for Artists
Description: Web site design for professional artists, reviewing historic and contemporary models. Addresses site creation from the ground up, examining best practices and strategies for successful design and management for portfolio and works created specifically for the internet.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Digital Media
Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Technical Problems
Description: For students qualified to carry out individual projects in studio areas.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 15 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Thematic Inquiry in Contemporary Art
Description: Advanced cross-media research and studio production on a topical theme in contemporary art. Readings, guest lectures, and field research will guide discussions on the topical theme of the course. Students will develop studio work addressing the theme utilizing the media of their expertise.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Thematic Inquiry: Public Art
Description: Advanced interdisciplinary research and studio production in designing, funding, and executing a community-engaged public project through the arts. Readings, guest lectures, and field research in partnership with local communities will guide collaborative work in implementing public art projects.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: IDEA Seminar: Innovation, Design, Entrepreneurship, and Art
Description: Focuses on planning for production. Students will research process, creating a variety of tools used for planning, including budgets, timelines, contracts, case studies, SWOT analysis, user scenarios, schematics, and narrative summaries. Students will leave the course able to create methodologies and plans for innovative project implementation.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 3-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6-12 hours lab per week.
title: Innovative Project Studio
Description: A design studio environment designed to allow students to rapidly develop and test innovative ideas into cultural objects whether they are works of art, new business ventures, or products.

Description: Supervised experience in a professional environment such as cooperative programs, agencies, or artists' studios.

Description: Individual studio projects investigating specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 2-12 hours lab per week.
title: Art and Design Charrettes
Description: Provides students with an opportunity to work side by side with faculty and visiting artists/designers to engage in intensive, often collaborative, project development and on a single topic, vision, or shared theme, often resulting in creative production as well as ideation.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Professional Practices in Art and Design
Description: This cross-media course develops students’ professional skills for the field, building tools and knowledge for careers in art, design, and related fields. The course includes career path development and the constructs of vision, research practice, websites, branding, resumes, business plans, client relationships, contracts, interview skills, and other career development tools.

Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Capstone Exhibition and Professional Practices
Description: This cross-media course develops students’ professional skills for the field including exhibition curation and installation, as well as tools and knowledge for careers in art, design, and related fields. The course includes career path development and the constructs of vision, branding, business practices, and other professional tools.

Description: Figure drawing with consideration of the human skeletal and muscular systems, surface anatomy, and bio-mechanical concerns.

Description: Historical techniques such as egg tempera, fresco, encaustic, and Venetian mode oil painting as they apply to contemporary needs; modern materials such as alkyd and polymer resins are introduced. Consideration is given to the properties of pigments, binders, grounds, and supports.

title: Drawing and Composition
Description: Projects in drawing including individual and group critiques.

Description: A continuation of Drawing and Composition. Projects in drawing, including individual and group critiques.

title: Drawing and Composition
Description: Studio work in drawing, with consideration of relationship of principles to picture structure. Readings in art history and criticism.

credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.

Description: Individual studio projects and investigation of specific problems under the direction of faculty members.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Painting
Description: Projects in painting, including individual and group critiques.

title: Painting
Description: A continuation of Painting. Projects in painting, individual and group critiques.

subject: ARST - Art Studio Art
title: Painting
Description: Studio work in painting with consideration of theoretical issues. Readings in art criticism and aesthetics.

credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Graduate Astronomy Seminar
Description: Professional skills such as writing and reviewing research and observing proposals, writing and refereeing research papers, making oral presentations of research and of journal articles, and writing brief newspaper and magazine summaries.

subject: ASTR - Astronomy
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Seminar on Special Topics in Astronomy
Description: Discussion of contemporary topics in astronomy.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
Description: Atmospheric composition and structure, clouds, precipitation, and atmospheric motion and winds. Organized weather systems, including air masses, fronts, and severe weather. Discussion of global climates includes circulation, wind systems, climate classification, and climate change.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Laboratory
Description: Optional laboratory for Introduction to Weather and Climate.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
Description: Atmospheric composition and structure, clouds, precipitation, and atmospheric motion and winds. Organized weather systems, including air masses, fronts, and severe weather. Discussion of global climates includes circulation, wind systems, climate classification, and climate change.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Climatology
Description: Climatology from local to global scales. Topics include radiation/heat exchanges, the hydrologic cycle, global climate patterns, climate change, measurement and data sources, relationships of climate with ecosystem processes, and human activities, and climate forecasting.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Weather Analysis and Forecasting
Description: The collection, display, and application of weather data. The use of meteorological instruments, codes, maps, atmospheric soundings, and thermodynamics diagrams. Interpretation of weather maps using basic meteorological principles.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Atmospheric Hazards
Description: The causes, impacts and policies regarding hazards due to atmospheric phenomena, including hurricanes, tornadoes, windstorms, extreme temperature and precipitation events, and climate change.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Atmospheric Hazards
Description: The causes, impacts, and policies regarding hazards due to atmospheric phenomena, including hurricanes, tornadoes, windstorms, extreme temperature and precipitation events, and climate change.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Hidden Figures in the Atmospheric Sciences
Description: Critical examination of the history of the atmospheric sciences in the U.S. with a focus on the foundational contributions of African-American, Asian-American, Hispanic-American, and Native American scientists. In addition, the key roles of women, the LGBTQ community, people with physical disabilities, and neurodiverse people in the atmospheric sciences are highlighted.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Global Climate Change: Causes and Consequences
Description: Provides students with the opportunity to critically evaluate the climatic and environmental changes currently facing our planet. Students will gain knowledge of the mechanisms that force climate and the human activities that affect the magnitude and direction of these forcing mechanisms and the impacts associated with these changes.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Internship in Atmospheric Sciences
Description: Placement of students in employment and/or training environment where they will utilize atmospheric sciences and related techniques in approaching practical problems relevant to the organization’s mission. An initial orientation and a post-internship evaluation with the internship committee are required.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Programming for Atmospheric Scientists
Description: An introduction to computer programming for atmospheric scientists. Students will learn to navigate the scientific computing environment and work with several computing languages. A study of applications of scientific computing for modeling atmospheric processes and data analysis. The course will be hands- on and focused around several practical programming assignments.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Atmospheric Thermodynamics
Description: An introduction to atmospheric thermodynamics with emphasis on the first and second laws of thermodynamics, equation of state for gases, moisture variables, adiabatic and diabatic processes of dry and moist air, phase changes of water, and atmospheric statics.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Atmospheric Dynamics
Description: A quantitative investigation of large-scale atmospheric motion. Equations of motion are derived from basic physical laws. Concepts of vorticity, quasi-geostrophic theory, and general circulation are addressed.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
Description: A quantitative investigation of atmospheric phenomena, including boundary-layer dynamics; balanced dynamics theory; atmospheric waves; geostrophic adjustment theories; atmospheric instabilities and cyclogenesis theories; frontogenesis theories; jet stream dynamics; introduction to finite difference methods; survey of tropical dynamics and middle atmosphere dynamics.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 3 hours lecture and 3 hours lab per week.
title: Introduction to Data Assimilation
Description: Introduction to the concepts, theory, and computational methods of data assimilation in the atmospheric and related sciences. Topics include the history of data assimilation, the “rejection problem,” adjustment to balance, balance constraints, nonlinear normal mode initialization, variational data assimilation, Kalman filter methods and applications to different disciplines and data types.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Synoptic Meteorology and Climatology
Description: Theory and observations to understand mid-latitude weather systems. Focus is on application of quasi-geostrophic theory in weather forecasting. Analysis and interpretation of weather maps and numerical models. Development and life cycle of cyclones, fronts, and jet streams.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Weather Forecasting Seminar
Description: A weather forecasting practicum that provides an opportunity for students to obtain real-time, real-world experience forecasting conventional weather parameters at selected cities in the United States.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Tropical Meteorology and Climatology
Description: An investigation of the weather and climate of the tropics, including its interactions with the tropical oceans and the extratropical atmosphere. Topics include the Hadley Cell, the ITCZ, monsoons, equatorial waves, tropical oscillations, and climate change, with particular emphasis on the theory, observations, modeling, and forecasting of tropical cyclones.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Tropical Meteorology and Climatology
Description: An investigation of the weather and climate of the tropics, including its interactions with the tropical oceans and the extratropical atmosphere. Topics include the Hadley Cell, the ITCZ, monsoons, equatorial waves, tropical oscillations, and climate change, with particular emphasis on the theory, observations, modeling, and forecasting of tropical cyclones.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 3 hours lab per week.
title: Introductory Atmospheric Physics
Description: An introduction to the physics of the atmosphere with emphasis on the laws of radiation, solar and terrestrial radiation, surface and atmospheric energy balances, cloud physics, precipitation formation, and atmospheric optical and electrical phenomena.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Satellite Meteorology and Climatology
Description: Application of satellite remote sensing in meteorology and climatology. Applications include clouds, atmospheric water vapor and precipitation, the Earth's radiation budget, sea and land surface temperatures.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Physical Climatology
Description: Advanced, quantitative study of Earth's physical climate. Includes global energy balance, surface-atmosphere energy exchanges, surface hydrology and water budget at various temporal and spatial scales. Methods of measuring and modeling are discussed. Case studies are used to illustrate how the physical processes govern the climate system.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Hydrometeorology
Description: Hydrometeorology bridges atmospheric sciences and hydrology, including formation and distribution of liquid and solid precipitation, floods, and drought, and impacts on water resources. Topics address the observing, modeling, and forecasting of fluxes, flow, and storage of liquid water, ice, and water vapor, including interactions between the land surface and atmosphere.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Applied Climatology in the Urban Environment
Description: Do cities create their own thunderstorms? Will pollution from emerging mega-cities change climate? Exploration of fundamental concepts of the urban-climate system, observational and modeling strategies for studying the urban-climate system, and context for how human activity in the built environment is changing Earth's weather and hydro-climate.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 3 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Environmental Microclimatology
Description: An introduction to the interactions between the biosphere and atmosphere. Energy, moisture, and carbon exchange in the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum with applications to managed and natural environments. The impact of weather and climate on humans and domesticated animals. Elementary turbulent exchange theory will be introduced.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Mesoscale and Radar Meteorology/Climatology
Description: Fundamental theory, analysis, and exercises on mesoscale weather phenomena and principles of radar meteorology. A major topical focus will be thunderstorms, mesoscale convective systems, and tornadic supercells. Other topics will include mesoscale classification, observing systems, the boundary layer, circulations, flooding, mesoscale tropical systems, mesoscale modeling, short-range forecasting/nowcasting, and mesoscale climatology.

subject: ATSC - Atmospheric Sciences
title: Capstone in Atmospheric Sciences
Description: The capstone allows B.S. Atmospheric Sciences majors to synthesize knowledge within the atmospheric sciences or between the atmospheric sciences and other disciplines while enhancing students’ appreciation of the discipline and connecting their education with future goals. This course allows the department to assess the learning outcomes of this major.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Anatomy for Athletic Training I
Description: This course will complete advanced study to include gross and surface anatomy, biomechanical principles, and functional anatomy of the spine and upper extremities.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Anatomy for Athletic Training II
Description: This course will complete advanced study to include human gross and surface anatomy, biomechanical principles, and functional anatomy of the lower extremities, brain, spinal cord, and internal organs.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Introduction to Athletic Training Clinical Practice
Description: Students will learn foundational clinical skills needed for the prevention, evaluation, and treatment of orthopedic and non-orthopedic conditions.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Medicine I
Description: The first course in a series designed to introduce students to the pathophysiology, evaluation, treatment, and relevant pharmacology for non-orthopedic conditions in Athletic Training.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Medicine II
Description: The second course in a series designed to introduce students to the pathophysiology, evaluation, treatment, and relevant pharmacology for non-orthopedic conditions in Athletic Training.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Therapeutic Interventions I
Description: Students will be introduced to the foundations, theories, and techniques regarding treatment interventions. Interventions include pain modulation, pharmacology, and therapeutic modalities.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Therapeutic Interventions II
Description: Students will be introduced to the foundations, theories, and techniques regarding treatment interventions to include therapeutic exercise and therapeutic modalities.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Therapeutic Interventions III
Description: Students will be introduced to the foundations, theories, and techniques regarding treatment interventions to include therapeutic modalities, complementary and alternative medicine therapies, and joint stabilization.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Evaluation and Treatment: Emergent Conditions
Description: Students will learn skills and techniques required to recognize, examine, diagnose, and manage acute and emergent life or limb threatening conditions.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Evaluation and Treatment: Spine and Trunk
Description: Designed to teach students pathomechanics, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and therapeutic interventions of conditions found in the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine, pelvis, trunk, and temporomandibular joint.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Evaluation and Treatment: Brain
Description: Focuses on integrative study of the brain. Topics of this course include anatomy, neuroscience, and neuroplasticity, and the recognition, evaluation, treatment, and interventions of acute, chronic, and degenerative conditions.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to teach students pathomechanics, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and therapeutic interventions of conditions found in the lower extremity.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to teach students pathomechanics, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and therapeutic interventions of conditions found in the knee and hip.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to teach students biomechanics, pathomechanics, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and therapeutic interventions of conditions found in the shoulder.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to teach students biomechanics, pathomechanics, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and therapeutic interventions of conditions found in the elbow, wrist, and hand.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Introduces the athletic training student to research methods to facilitate translation of scientific inquiry to clinical practice.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Evidence-Based Practice II

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Evidence-Based Practice III
Description: Teaches students clinically-applicable statistical analysis in order to critically evaluate research and determine the impact on clinical practice.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Evidence-Based Practice IV
Description: Prepares students to disseminate scientific research.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Prepares students to undertake independent research by introducing advanced literature review skills, scientific writing techniques, and methodology design and implementation. Additionally, students will gain an advanced understanding of statistical analyses related to common clinical sports medicine research designs.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Psychological and Social Considerations in Healthcare
Description: Students will be prepared to identify, support, and refer patients with psychological disorders or concerns. Students will learn to embed empathy into their practice with respect to cultures, values, and the socioeconomic status of patients.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Clinical Imaging and Diagnostic Procedures
Description: Provides students with fundamental clinical knowledge of commonly utilized diagnostic procedures in sports medicine.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Special Populations and Disabilities
Description: Designed to introduce athletic training students to the evaluation, treatment, and medical considerations of those with developmental and physical disabilities as they participate in physical activity and sport.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training
title: Injury Prevention, Performance Enhancement, and Wellness
Description: Provides students with advanced theories and policies of public health, prevention and treatment programs in the communities, evaluation and integration of epidemiological data, and injury prevention techniques, as well as theories, concepts, and techniques regarding return to activity progression and training.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Introduces students to the business and administrative responsibilities of athletic training.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to prepare students for advanced clinical practice through selected topics related to theory, research, or athletic training clinical practice.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to integrate didactic knowledge and clinical practice through collaboration, problem-solving, and critical thinking. The primary focus of this course will be the evaluation and treatment of emergent conditions, neurological conditions, or spinal injuries.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

Description: Designed to integrate didactic knowledge and clinical practice through collaboration, problem-solving, and critical thinking. The focus of this course will be the evaluation and treatment of orthopedic and non-orthopedic conditions.

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

subject: ATTR - Athletic Training

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering

Description: Introduction to biochemical engineering processes, types of process units, process flow sheets, mass and energy balance calculations, process simulation, and basics of plant design economics.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering

Description: Equilibrium thermodynamics and its application to chemical processes.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering

Description: Engineering principles of heat, mass, and energy systems through experiential learning with focus on chemical/biochemical processes.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Kinetics and Reactor Design
Description: The fundamentals of engineering science and design related to chemical, environmental, and biocatalytic homogeneous reactions. An introduction to chemical and enzymatic kinetics, collection and analysis of rate data, isothermal reactor design, bioreactor design, energy balance, and runaway reactions.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Mass Transport and Rate Phenomena
Description: Mass transport and rate phenomena in the analysis of engineering problems in biological systems.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 3 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Biochemical Engineering Laboratory
Description: Principles and applications of biochemical engineering processes and unit operations through experiential learning.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Biochemical Process Control
Description: Theories and knowledge of chemical/biochemical process control systems focusing on dynamic behavior of processes, feedback control, and applications to biological systems.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Biorefinery Engineering
Description: Various aspects of biomass conversion to energy, chemical, and bioproducts. The presentations are linked to introduce the student to opportunities in the emerging bio-economy. Topics include biomass types and characteristics, technologies, systems analysis, economics, and environmental aspects of biorefineries.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Environmental Engineering Remediation Design
Description: Engineering science and design related to environmental modeling, solid waste management, and hazardous waste management. Concepts of risk assessment will also be introduced.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Biochemical Engineering
Description: Design and analysis of enzymatic and microbial biological reaction systems.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Design of Biochemical Separations Processes
Description: Unit operations used for biological processing including filtration, centrifugation, cell disruption, isolation, purification, and polishing.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Bioprocess Design and Simulation
Description: Design and modeling of chemical/bioprocess systems, including unit operations and reactor design principles. Process simulation and process economics applied to chemical/bioprocessing systems. Plant layout and process safety of bio/chemical plants will be included.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Animal Cell Biomanufacturing
Description: Biochemical engineering concepts related to large-scale animal cell biotechnology and scalable manufacturing of cellular products, such as recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, viral vaccines, therapeutic cells, and gene therapy vectors. Working in small groups, students will address a range of contemporary problems.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 3 hours lab per week.
title: Metabolic Engineering and Synthetic Biology
Description: Theories and applications of cellular metabolism, genetic engineering, protein engineering, and metabolic engineering through experiential learning.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering
title: Bioelectrochemical Engineering
Description: The study of electron transfer interaction in biological systems. Topics include redox biochemistry, bio-energetics and thermodynamics, kinetics, transport processes in bio-electrochemical systems, and engineering of bio- electrochemical systems.

Description: Kinetics and reactor design of heterogeneous reactions; i.e., reactions in which the substrate (reactant) and bio/catalyst are initially in two separate phases. Simulation of processes using heterogeneous catalysis. The course will briefly introduce homogenous kinetics and methods of chemical catalyst characterization, preparation, and mechanisms of action.

Description: Advanced fermentation principles through the development of mathematical models, design of experiments, and interpretation of results.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering

Description: Advanced concepts and techniques of metabolic engineering and synthetic biology that enable the fast development of microbial cell factories.

subject: BCHE - Biochemical Engineering

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

Description: The structure and function of biological molecules, enzymology, metabolism and bioenergetics, and molecular biology. For honors students who have completed prerequisite introductory biology and chemistry coursework.

Description: Seminars, readings, and discussions of topics related to biochemistry, biotechnology, and molecular biology. Scientific writing will be emphasized, and visits to laboratories may be scheduled.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Biology for Medicine
Description: Selected topics in biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, and biotechnology involved in modern medicine. Includes cloning, stem cells, endocrinology, human genetics, gene testing, and human population genetics. Bioethical issues will also be discussed. Both formal lectures and discussion sessions will be utilized and students will write short essays on selected topics.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
Description: A focus on the remarkable impact that genome sequencing projects is having on virtually all aspects of biochemistry, as well as on medicine and biotechnology. An introduction to a broad range of 'omic' topics, including functional genomics, microarrays, proteomics, physiological genomics, and bioinformatics.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Methods in Biotechnology
Description: Laboratory instruction in the methods for manipulation of plants, microbes, and animals for biotechnological purposes.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

Description: The most essential computing skills for modern biologists, such as MySQL, R, and AWK, as well as how to access and use High Performance Computer clusters and construct reusable data analysis workflows in RCC and the Galaxy system. Emphasis will be on hands-on work on computer work and problem solving.

title: Graduate Professional Development

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Fermentation Technology
Description: Introduces concepts in fermentation to students already familiar with industrial microbiology. The course will have a lecture and lab component, with students getting hands-on experience with fermentors and cell culture equipment.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Downstream Processing
Description: Techniques used in downstream processing of material produced in fermentation or cell culture. Students will get hands-on experience with real-life problems in downstream processing.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Advanced Biochemistry and Molecular Biology I
Description: Advanced biochemistry and molecular biology stressing thermodynamic principles in biochemistry, structural biology, enzymology, and aspects of metabolism and bioenergetics.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Advanced Biochemistry and Molecular Biology II
Description: Advanced biochemistry and molecular biology stressing metabolism and bioenergetics, replication, transcription, RNA processing, genetic codes, translation, membrane transport, and signal transduction.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Introduction to Research in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Description: Overview of current departmental research and introduction to research facilities. Training and practical experience in oral presentation, scientific writing, and grant preparation.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 3-9 hours lab per week.
title: Laboratory Rotation
Description: Exploratory laboratory research for first year biochemistry graduate students.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
title: Advanced Physical Biochemistry
Description: Principles in physical chemistry and biophysics to biological macromolecules, including structural biology, hydrodynamics, electronic and magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and crystallography.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 5 hours credit.
title: Cellular and Molecular Biochemistry
Description: Advanced molecular and cellular biochemistry, including structure, biosynthesis, and assembly of cell proteins and nucleic acids.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

Description: Seminar dealing with various topics in current biochemistry and molecular biology.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

Description: Research discussion focused on current research in biochemistry and molecular biology.

subject: BCMB - Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
