Description: Students will study key concepts and institutions of our system of government, as well as the practical and political realities impacting law and policy-making in Washington. Students will consider and hear directly from senior government officials, lawmakers, and policy leaders regarding their actual work on the ground. Students will apply this practical understanding to analyze issues of national importance including, for example, the immigration crisis and President Trump's "Travel Ban." Class also will expose students to the wide range of professional opportunities available to them in Washington.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lawyers, Kings, Despots, and Revolutionaries: How Lawyers Create and Destroy Political Freedom
Description: Examines the role that lawyers across time and space have played in creating and defending democratic government that respects the rule of law. We will examine the role that lawyers played in insulating the rule of law from the arbitrary exercise of monarchical power, the role lawyers have played since 1900 in defending democracy and the rule of law from authoritarian governments, and evaluate the performance of lawyers in defending these institutions in the United States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Business Law Practicum
Description: Students will work with a licensed attorney to produce carefully researched, jurisdiction-specific, tailored informational guidance addressing common legal needs in the entrepreneurial and nonprofit community. A weekly seminar will provide an introductory overview of major topics in business law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Foundations of American Law
Description: An introduction to legal reasoning, fundamental law and policy argumentative tools, the various types of legal institutions, the administrative state, and the interpretation of statutes and the Constitution. Foundational study will lead to legally sophisticated analyses and discussion concerning recently argued or decided Supreme Court cases.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Foundations of American Law
Description: An introduction to legal reasoning, fundamental law and policy argumentative tools, the various types of legal institutions, the administrative state, and the interpretation of statutes and the Constitution. Foundational study will lead to legally sophisticated analyses and discussion concerning recently argued or decided Supreme Court cases.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Practicum in Animal Welfare Skills
Description: Students will work with law enforcement and animal welfare professionals to identify, investigate, and work to resolve animal welfare issues, including crimes and ordinance violations in Athens-Clarke County.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Criminal Procedure
Description: A study of criminal process rights that apply during the interaction between law enforcement and individual suspects. More specifically, the course will examine the relationship (and tension) that exists between the law enforcement investigative function and the constitutional guarantees that are designed to safeguard our individual liberties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Criminal Procedure
Description: A study of criminal process rights that apply during the interaction between law enforcement and individual suspects. More specifically, the course will examine the relationship (and tension) that exists between the law enforcement investigative function and the constitutional guarantees that are designed to safeguard our individual liberties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Learning from Wrongful Convictions
Description: Exploration of some of the main factors that have led to wrongful convictions across the United States. Using actual cases in which the accused has been exonerated, students will develop an understanding of how forensic science, social science, police officers, prosecutors, and defense attorneys have all contributed to various cases of wrongful convictions. Students will then examine what the criminal justice system can do to prevent wrongful convictions in the future and present a paper detailing a proposed solution to one of the issues discussed. Learning will come from readings, class discussions, and guest speakers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Learning from Wrongful Convictions
Description: Exploration of some of the main factors that have led to wrongful convictions across the United States. Using actual cases in which the accused has been exonerated, students will develop an understanding of how forensic science, social science, police officers, prosecutors, and defense attorneys have all contributed to various cases of wrongful convictions. Students will then examine what the criminal justice system can do to prevent wrongful convictions in the future and present a paper detailing a proposed solution to one of the issues discussed. Learning will come from readings, class discussions, and guest speakers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Legal System Through Crime Books
Description: Books about crime often grab the public’s attention, but how much truth do they convey? This course will explore the stories that both crime novels and true crime books tell and the reality of the criminal legal system behind those stories.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Death Penalty in America
Description: Examination of legal, social, and political issues surrounding the death penalty. History, race, mental health, and geographical disparities are a few of the issues to be addressed. Capital punishment also affects individuals, perpetrators, and victims whose lives are forever altered. Individual cases illustrate issues raised by the death penalty.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Death Penalty in America
Description: Examination of legal, social, and political issues surrounding the death penalty. History, race, mental health, and geographical disparities are a few of the issues to be addressed. Capital punishment also affects individuals, perpetrators, and victims whose lives are forever altered. Individual cases illustrate issues raised by the death penalty.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Introduction to Global Governance
Description: In a globalizing world, the range of issues with cross-border implications only expands, from finance to trade, terrorism to food safety, climate change to sports. This upper-level, interdisciplinary course examines how and why different legal regimes have developed to govern these issues, when and why they succeed, and when and why they fail or generate backlash.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Undergraduate Mock Trial
Description: Students will earn credit through participation as members of the University of Georgia Mock Trial Team. Participants in the course will assume roles as lawyers, witnesses, and/or student coaches preparing for and competing in tournaments sponsored by the American Mock Trial Association.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Exploring the Intersection of Law and Technology in the Information Age
Description: Exploration of the intersection of law, policy, and the modern connective technologies that many use daily. To this end, the course will look at copyright, fair use, and the changing concept of IP ownership.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Ideas and Expressions: The Fundamentals of Copyright Law
Description: With its roots in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, copyright is an essential part of U.S. Law. This course will explore the fundamentals of U.S. copyright law, from securing protection, to copyright duration, fair use, and the tension between copyright and First Amendment freedom of expression.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Information Literacy and the Law
Description: Teaches students to research effectively and introduces them to information literacy concepts like verifying news, online resources, and other publications. Civics concepts needed to understand American government and legal documents and how to find those documents for free or at low cost.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Directed Readings
Description: Individual study, reading, or projects for undergraduates under the direction of a law professor.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Studies in Law in Other Times and Places
Description: A special issue or topic not otherwise offered in the Law School curriculum. Topics, methodology, and instructors will vary from semester to semester. An example class is "Tales of Asylum, Border Crossings, and International Refugee Law.”

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Studies in Law in Other Times and Places
Description: A special issue or topic not otherwise offered in the Law School curriculum. Topics, methodology, and instructors will vary from semester to semester. An example class is "Tales of Asylum, Border Crossings, and International Refugee Law.”

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Aspects of Entrepreneurship
Description: Exploration of the law related to developing and launching a small business. Topics include selecting the structure of and forming a corporation; protecting a business’s copyrights, trademarks, patents, and/or trade secrets; and complying with employment and consumer protection laws and regulations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Mental Health Law
Description: The legal issues relating to mental health and illness, including competency, disability, confidentiality (HIPAA), duty to warn, civil commitment, criminal defenses, discrimination, and similar issues. Recommended for students planning careers in the helping professions, including social work, therapy, psychology, education, and criminal justice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Antimonopoly and American Democracy: Case Studies in American Capitalism
Description: Teaches students about antitrust law by placing it within the broader scope of the American antimonopoly tradition. Enables students to engage in the ongoing debate and answer the perennial question of our time: how should we regulate market competition in a liberal democracy?

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Race and Law
Description: An examination of the effects of race on the structure and practice of law, on thinking about law, and on legal education.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Institutions of the European Union
Description: History of the European Union, law-making and administrative institutions and processes, economic sectoral policies, including competition and state aids, transport and agriculture; internal market, freedoms (movement of goods, workers, capital, services); harmonization of national laws; external economic trade policy; impact of Single European Act and Treaty on European Union.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Capital Punishment
Description: Legal and social issues surrounding capital punishment. Surveys legal issues in areas of criminal law and procedure, constitutional law and ethics which confront attorneys in capital cases. Encourages students to synthesize social and legal facets to objectively evaluate complex issues involved in capital punishment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Patent Prosecution and Procedure
Description: Study of how to write and prosecute a United States patent application. Introduces students to common issues arising during patent prosecution and equips students with basic strategies to deal with those issues. Explores patent infringement analysis and opinion letter work in which patent lawyers routinely engage.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Mediation Practicum
Description: In-class, simulation-based training, including interactive training on the mediation process, the role and competencies of the mediator, ethical and regulatory rules governing mediation, and a series of specific topics of mediation practice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: How to Sue Your School
Description: Introduces students to students' and teachers' constitutional rights and obligations in the education context.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: How to Sue Your School
Description: Introduces students to students' and teachers' constitutional rights and obligations in the educational context.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Disability and Education Law
Description: Students with disabilities are entitled to specific educational services and accommodations in public schools in the United States. This course will introduce undergraduate and graduate students to federal and state laws and regulations that apply to the provision of educational services for students with disabilities from birth through age 21.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: LLCs and Partnerships
Description: Limited liability companies (LLCs) and partnerships are the most common legal entity forms used by U.S. businesses today. Focuses on the legal, financial, tax, and other practical matters relating to LLCs and partnerships and the terms of their governing documents. Class attendance and participation are required.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Oxford Law Tutorial
Description: In-depth research and written analysis of a legal issue under the tutoring and supervision of law faculty from Oxford University. It requires significant legal research, original thinking and analysis, and must result in a paper, over thirty pages in length, similar in quality to a law review article.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Civil Procedure
Description: The process of adjudication by which America's courts resolve civil controversies brought to them as lawsuits. Topics covered in this half of an academic year-long course include personal jurisdiction, subject matter jurisdiction, supplemental jurisdiction, additional claims, multiple parties, and the Erie doctrine (choice of law).

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: EU Economic Law
Description: The bases for the common market, free trade area, customs union, and common external trade policy will be described and discussed. Focus on the "four freedoms" which are essential elements of the common market and their expanded scope since the Treaty of Maastricht. Discussion of the common agricultural and transport policies.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Comparative Intellectual Property Law
Description: Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) Agreement governing intellectual property as administered by World Trade Organization (WTO). Topics include provisions on patent, trademark, copyright, geographical indications, trade secret law. Enforcement and dispute resolution issues will be covered, along with considerations of effect of intellectual property protection on foreign direct investment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: UK Constitutional Law in Comparative Perspective
Description: How lawmakers and courts in the United States and United Kingdom deal with written and unwritten constitutions, common law, and precedent through the lens of the British election and debate over immigration reform and whether the United Kingdom needs a written Constitution. The legislative process and judicial decisions in both nations will be studied.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Real Property Law in Comparative Perspective
Description: Property concepts and institutions that are important for global economic development and international trade. A large part of the course will be comparative; we will focus on the United States and a number of approaches from other major legal systems.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: European Union Business Law
Description: An introduction to selected aspects of European Union business law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Comparative United States - European Union Law
Description: This course compares the allocation of decision-making under the United States Constitution with that of the European Union.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: International Trade Law Practice under the WTO
Description: Legal issues and trade practices under the World Trade Organization (WTO).

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Human Rights in a Comparative Perspective
Description: Examination of how different legal systems balance the judicial protection of civil rights and liberties with the power of legislative majorities to govern. It does so by considering how different constitutional texts, governmental structures, and social and legal traditions shape juridical responses to common questions about rights.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Contracts
Description: Contracts provides an introduction to the law of legally enforceable promises under Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code and the common law. Among other topics, the course considers offers and their acceptance; consideration, formalities, and promissory estoppel; the parole evidence rule and the statute of frauds; third-party enforcement; material breach of contract; and damages. Students are expected to be able to explain in writing how these and additional legal issues under the UCC and the common law apply to various complex factual scenarios.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lawyering I
Description: “Lawyering” covers various strategies and issues that are relevant to a long-term, healthy, and satisfying career in a dynamic profession. Topics may include the business of lawyering, professional-identity formation, cross-cultural competency, legal technology, wellness strategies, and professional communication skills.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lawyering II
Description: A continuation of Lawyering I, covering various strategies and issues that are relevant to a long-term, healthy, and satisfying career in a dynamic profession. Topics may include the business of lawyering, professional identity formation, cross-cultural competency, legal technology, wellness strategies, and professional communication skills.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Law
Description: The historical development of criminal law as well as analysis of necessary elements of crimes, and consideration of the principal classes of crimes, including homicide, attempt, and conspiracy.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Writing I
Description: Introduces the process of legal analysis and reasoning and teaches students to produce written documents in the style and format appropriate for the audience and purpose, with an emphasis on objective analysis and writing. It also covers legal research sources and methodologies for print and digital resources.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 0.5-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Legal Research I
Description: Introduction to sources and strategies for basic legal research, including finding cases, statutes, regulations, and secondary authorities.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Writing II
Description: Advanced skills of legal analysis, reasoning, and research within the context of legal argument. Students produce written documents in the style and format appropriate for the audience and purpose, with an emphasis on persuasive writing. Also covered are basic concepts, conventions, and formats for drafting legal documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

title: Legal Research II

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: This course will build upon research skills acquired in first- year Legal Research and Writing classes by offering students an advanced exploration of legal research tools. The course will cover primary and secondary legal sources, advanced searching skills, topical research, internet resources, and non-law resources.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Technology Skills for Legal Practice
Description: A focused, hands-on exploration of the use of technology in the practice of law. The course will cover the impact of technology on law and practice and the specific technology understanding and skills required of the modern lawyer. Students will complete hands-on projects using practice management, document assembly, presentation, and office productivity software.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

The course will cover the impact of technology on law and practice and the specific technology understanding and skills required of the modern lawyer. Students will complete hands-on projects using practice management, document assembly, presentation, and office productivity software.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Law Research
Description: Gives students experience in researching a variety of business law topics focusing on primary, secondary, and transactional materials. Provides an in-depth look at primary and secondary tax law resources and how to find them using a variety of print and electronic sources.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Writing for Judicial Clerkships
Description: Introduces students to the workings of judicial chambers and provides experience in writing the types of documents commonly required of judicial clerks, such as jury instructions, trial court opinions, appellate court opinions, and bench memoranda.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Georgia Legal Research
Description: A hands-on exploration of Georgia legal research resources. The course will cover primary and secondary sources, advanced searching skills, topical research, and cost saving strategies. Students will complete research for simulated client matters: preparing civil and criminal cases for trial, completing a business transaction, and representing a client in an administrative hearing.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: A hands-on exploration of Georgia legal research resources. The course will cover primary and secondary sources, advanced searching skills, topical research, and cost saving strategies. Students will complete research for simulated client matters: preparing civil and criminal cases for trial, completing a business transaction, and representing a client in an administrative hearing.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Property
Description: The recognition, development, and regulation of rights in real property and personal property, including the nature and function of possession and title, shared ownership, private and public rights, and transfers of property.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Property
Description: The recognition, development, and regulation of rights in real property and personal property, including the nature and function of possession and title, shared ownership, private and public rights, and transfers of property.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Democracy and the Constitution
Description: An exploration of the concepts of democracy and equal citizenship through the prism of the U.S. Constitution. Students will examine the rights and responsibilities of membership in the American civic community and how those rights and responsibilities have changed over time. Examination of each of these conflicts will center on their relationship to the rights and duties embodied in the U.S. Constitution.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
