Description: An exploration of the concepts of democracy and equal citizenship through the prism of the U.S. Constitution. Students will examine the rights and responsibilities of membership in the American civic community and how those rights and responsibilities have changed over time. Examination of each of these conflicts will center on their relationship to the rights and duties embodied in the U.S. Constitution.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Torts
Description: Covers intentional torts, which may include battery, assault, and possibly false imprisonment, trespass to land, and others. Certain defenses to intentional tort, such as consent and self defense, may also be covered. The bulk of the course is devoted to the tort of negligence, including the content of the duty of reasonable care, issues bearing on whether the defendant has breached that duty, the requirement that the plaintiff establish a causal connection between the breach and the plaintiff's harm, and proximate cause limits on liability.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Economic Law, Energy, and Climate
Description: Energy scarcity, and the scarcity of natural resources more generally, is one of the key international challenges of the twenty-first century. This course examines the relationship between international economic law (the WTO, investment law), energy governance institutions, such as the Organization of Petroleum Exporting States and the International Energy Agency, and climate change.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Torts II
Description: Advanced topics in tort law, building on the coverage in the first-year Torts I course. Topics may include products liability, defamation, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, interference with contractual relations, recovery for pure economic harm, interference with intellectual property rights, nuisance, trespass to chattels, and conversion. In addition, the roles of mass tort litigation, insurance, and tort reform may be considered.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Economic Torts
Description: Examination of economic tort claims and other remedies that may be available for commercial disputes. The seminar also considers damages, litigation concerns, and professionalism issues that may be a part of such disputes.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Mass Tort Litigation
Description: The legal problems and issues associated with the unique, growing phenomenon of mass torts, e.g., the B.P. Oil Spill, the 9/11 litigation, tobacco, Agent Orange, Dalkon Shield, breast implants, asbestos personal injury litigation, Holocaust litigation, etc.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Torts and Terrorism
Description: Exploration of the liability and compensation issues arising from terrorists' acts. Topics include: potential liability of public and private non-terrorist defendants such as government agencies and officials, airlines, security companies, and building owners; liability of terrorists and their supporters; insurance and compensation programs; liability of officials for acts taken against suspected terrorists.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Appellate Advocacy
Description: Designed to help students to become successful appellate advocates. Students prepare a brief and oral argument. Grades based on evaluations of appellate brief, videotaped argument, competition argument, and writing exercises.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Appellate Advocacy
Description: Designed to help students to become successful appellate advocates. Students prepare a brief and oral argument. Grades based on evaluations of an appellate brief, videotaped argument, competition argument, and writing exercises.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Appellate Litigation Clinic Seminar
Description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral arguments if scheduled. This portion includes a seminar component.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Appellate Litigation Clinic I
Description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral argument if scheduled.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Appellate Litigation Clinic II
Description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral argument if scheduled.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Appellate Litigation Clinic Summer
Description: Under supervision, students will assist in preparing briefs and other documents submitted to the United States Circuit Courts of Appeals, the Board of Immigration Appeals, the United States Supreme Court, or the Office of the United States Pardon Attorney.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Legal Writing Seminar
Description: Advanced instruction in legal research and legal writing. Focuses on both training and experience in the practical skills of researching and writing as well as explicitly exploring the purposes for writing a particular document and being sure to effectively reach the intended audience. Class material will cover general writing principles, guidance on legal writing style, grammar, organization, editing, and citation form. Course consists of extensive practice, feedback, peer review, and review of excerpts from actual briefs and other documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Legal Writing Seminar
Description: Advanced instruction in legal research and legal writing. Focuses on both training and experience in the practical skills of researching and writing as well as explicitly exploring the purposes for writing a particular document and being sure to effectively reach the intended audience. Class material will cover general writing principles, guidance on legal writing style, grammar, organization, editing, and citation form. Course consists of extensive practice, feedback, peer review, and review of excerpts from actual briefs and other documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Payment Systems
Description: Articles 3 and 4 of the Uniform Commercial Code which deal with checks and promissory notes. Other payment systems, such as credit cards, debit cards, and electronic fund transfers also will be examined.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sale and Lease of Goods
Description: This is an advanced course that focuses primarily on those portions of UCC Article 2 and Article 2A that are not studied in depth in the Contracts course. The warranty, risk of loss, breach, and damage provisions of the UCC will be emphasized.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Consumer Law
Description: Legal issues concerning consumers' commercial transactions, including the following key topics: disclosure of information to consumers, consumer credit, predatory-lending prohibitions, consumer-credit reporting, privacy related to consumer transactions (both online and offline), consumer-product warranties, debt collection, and dispute-resolution methods.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Law I
Description: The meaning and impact of the Constitution of the United States, particularly with regard to the subjects of federalism, separation of powers, the judicial function, and due process of law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Law I
Description: The meaning and impact of the Constitution of the United States, particularly with regard to the subjects of federalism, separation of powers, the judicial function, and due process of law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Comparative Constitutional Rights
Description: Examination of how different legal systems balance the judicial protection of civil rights and liberties with the power of legislative majorities to govern. It does so by considering how different constitutional texts, governmental structures, and social and legal traditions shape juridical responses to common questions about rights.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: British Government and the British Constitutional Tradition
Description: An introduction to basic concepts of British public law. An examination of the structure of British government and British constitutionalism; the relationship between the United Kingdom and its member countries; and the regulation within British law of political parties, political participation, and interest groups.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Law II
Description: An in-depth examination of the individual rights protected in the Fourteenth and First Amendments (substantive due process, equal protection, freedom of speech and association, and religious freedoms).

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Law II
Description: An in-depth examination of the individual rights protected in the Fourteenth and First Amendments (substantive due process, equal protection, freedom of speech and association, and religious freedoms).

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law of Constitutional Structure
Description: Exploration of the Constitution’s structuring of American government. Of particular importance are two key concepts, federalism (that is, the division of power between the central government and the states) and the separation of powers among the three branches of the central government.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Identity Seminar
Description: Examination of how the Constitution defines national community through citizenship practices. Constitutional and other rules relating to acceptance, rejection, and expulsion of individual members as citizens; special problems of dual nationality; historical racial and gender aspects of American citizenship; and constitutional meaning of state citizenship will also be examined.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Theory
Description: Exploration of the theory that lies behind the American Constitution and its interpretation in judicial decisions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Press and the Constitution
Description: This seminar will take an in-depth look at the constitutional rights of the “press.” Topics of discussion will include the history of the Press Clause, the relationship between the Speech Clause and the Press Clause, the definition of the “press” under the Constitution, and the rights available to the press.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Constitutional Law Seminar
Description: This seminar will focus on Constitutional Law at a greater level of depth than occurs in two basic courses. Student efforts will center on researching discrete subjects within constitutional law. There may, in particular, be opportunities to work on such subjects as religious displays, affirmative action, presidential immunities, etc.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Modern American Legal Theory
Description: This is a study in the theories that animate modern legal scholarship and practice. The course surveys classic articles and book excerpts and reviews to provide a basic understanding of the dominant theoretical movements and their development.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Modern American Legal Theory
Description: This is an online class which studies the theories that animate modern legal scholarship and practice. The course surveys classic articles and book excerpts and reviews to provide a basic understanding of the dominant theoretical movements and their development.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: First Amendment Clinic Seminar
Description: UGA’s First Amendment Clinic defends and advances the rights of free speech, press, petition, and assembly. The Clinic provides direct client services to individuals or organizations in need of counsel with First Amendment expertise and serves as an educational resource regarding free expression, open access, and protection of newsgathering and reporting.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: First Amendment Clinic Hours
Description: UGA’s First Amendment Clinic defends and advances the rights of free speech, press, petition, and assembly. The Clinic provides direct client services to individuals or organizations in need of counsel with First Amendment expertise and serves as an educational resource regarding free expression, open access, and protection of news gathering and reporting.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporations
Description: Problems in organization and functioning of corporations, including such matters as disregard of corporate entity, management and control, federal regulation of insider trading, proxy solicitation and shareholder voting, derivative actions, and special problems of the closed corporation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Negotiations
Description: Basic negotiation skills and transactional problems commonly confronted in a general business law practice. Deals with cover bilateral, multilateral, and repeated negotiations in addition to principal-agent problems. Timing and desirability of disclosure of information, misrepresentation, and legal ethics are also discussed.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Negotiations
Description: Basic negotiation skills and transactional problems commonly confronted in general business law practice. Deals with cover bilateral, multilateral, and repeated negotiations in addition to principal-agent problems. Timing and desirability of disclosure of information, misrepresentation, and legal ethics are also discussed.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Drafting for Transactional Practice
Description: A guide for beginning drafters and an advanced focus on avoiding the three types of ambiguity in legal documents. Using dozens of real-life examples of typical contract provisions, the course introduces techniques applicable to virtually all drafting projects for making better word choices and improving sentence structure.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Drafting for Transactional Practice
Description: A guide for beginning drafters and an advanced focus on avoiding the three types of ambiguity in legal documents. Using dozens of real life examples of typical contract provisions, the course introduces techniques applicable to virtually all drafting projects for making better word choices and improving sentence structure.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Negotiation and Settlement
Description: Negotiation theory, practical skills training, and an examination of settlement issues combine to give students confidence that they can negotiate legal disputes effectively and with integrity. Students participate in class discussions and negotiation simulations, complete written assignments, and submit a paper.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Negotiation and Settlement
Description: Negotiation theory, practical skills training, and an examination of settlement issues combine to give students confidence that they can negotiate legal disputes effectively and with integrity. Students participate in class discussions and negotiation simulations, complete written assignments, and submit a paper.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Fundamentals of Mergers and Acquisitions
Description: Designed to give the student working familiarity with how a merger or acquisition transaction is negotiated and structured, from inception to post-closing, with a heavy emphasis on how the major deal documents allocate risks between the parties through pricing structure, representations, covenants, and conditions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Anatomy of a Mergers and Aquisition Deal
Description: Provides overview of typical asset sale transaction and attorney's role in it. Students will assume role of counsel for one party, as well as that of legal specialist, and will follow transaction from confidentiality agreement through closing.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Business Law Practicum
Description: Supervised students will represent entrepreneurs, small business owners, and not-for-profit organizations that cannot otherwise afford legal services. In the practicum seminar, students will learn how to interview, counsel, draft, and negotiate, and will develop problem-solving, analytical, and editorial skills.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Business Law Practicum Clinic Hours
Description: Essential lawyering skills in a professional, interactive, live- client environment. Services provided by students will relate to such matters as entity formation, corporate governance, employment, and contracts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Landmark Cases in Corporate Law
Description: Mergers and transfers of control, hostile acquisitions, tender offers, and defensive tactics. Each student will choose between writing a paper and taking an exam.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Bankruptcy Litigation
Description: Provide students with practical, direct, and realistic experience with the procedural rules applicable to the resolution of disputes that commonly occur in contested chapter 11 reorganization and chapter 7 bankruptcy cases. Students will individually and as part of teams draft petitions, draft and argue Contested Matter applications, motions, objections, and an Adversary Proceeding complaint and answer.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Selected Topics in Jurisprudence
Description: An examination of natural law theories, both those based on revealed religion and those without religion. Guidelines for understanding how law actually develops and is related to society, and its consequences.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Leadership and the Foundations of American Law
Description: Students will serve as discussants and mentors for undergraduates in a course concerning basic legal reasoning and institutions and culminating in discussion and analysis of pending and recently decided Supreme Court cases. Students will be responsible for teaching and evaluating undergraduate learners, including leading and participating in discussion sessions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Leadership and the Foundations of American Law
Description: Students will serve as discussants and mentors for undergraduates in a course concerning basic legal reasoning and institutions and culminating in discussion and analysis of pending and recently decided Supreme Court cases. Students will be responsible for teaching and evaluating undergraduate learners, including leading and participating in discussion sessions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Perspectives on the Legal Process
Description: A survey of 20th-century perspectives on the nature of law and the legal process. Historical and philosophical approach, focusing on key writers and "schools," including Holmes, Cardozo, legal Realism, H.L.A. Hart, Dworkin, law and economics, public choice, critical legal studies, feminist jurisprudence, and critical race theory.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Jurisprudence Seminar
Description: Examination of modes of thinking about law. Focus upon particular jurisprudential systems and points of view as they bear upon contemporary legal problems and lines of cases, including administrative law and environmental regulation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Evidence
Description: Provides a detailed exploration of the Federal Rules of Evidence and other sources of law governing the admission of evidence in civil and criminal trials. The rules in Georgia are substantially similar to the federal rules, so this class also will give a good grounding in the Georgia rules.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Evidence
Description: Provides a detailed exploration of the Federal Rules of Evidence and other sources of law governing the admission of evidence in civil and criminal trials. The rules in Georgia are substantially similar to the federal rules, so this class also will give a good grounding in the Georgia rules.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sentencing (Minicourse)
Description: An examination of the overarching goals of sentencing in the criminal justice system, policy considerations driving sentencing, constitutional and statutory limitations on sentencing schemes, and the basics of sentencing practice in state and federal courts in this country.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Sentencing
Description: Examination of various aspects of the state sentencing process as it pertains to criminal charges and convictions. Includes an overview of the legal and societal objectives underlying the imposition of sentences.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Problems in Intellectual Property Seminar
Description: Advanced issues in the law of unfair competition, trademark, false advertising and publicity rights, with special focus on questions of pre-emption of state law, antitrust, secured transactions, and international law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Intellectual Property Seminar
Description: Primary focus on the WTO-administered Treaty on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Law (TRIPS). Secondary focus on Paris Convention, Berne Convention, Madrid Protocol, bio-piracy and gray market goods. Comparative focus on the intellectual property law of various nations encouraged in student presentations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Criminal Law
Description: Examination of the development of international criminal law. Exploration of the history of international criminal justice, the “core crimes” of international criminal law, theories of liability, and available defenses. Other topics will include the war on terrorism, United States opposition to the International Criminal Court, and transitional justice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Transnational Criminal Law
Description: This course concerns crimes that, though ordinarily domestic, become “transnational” when some aspect crosses national borders. To be studied: extraterritorial jurisdiction; obligations of law enforcement officers operating overseas; substantive law of crimes like trafficking, public corruption, money laundering, and terrorism; and procedural matters like extradition, rendition, evidence gathering, and judgment enforcement.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Crime and Criminal Behavior
Description: Course explores documented connections between certain underlying variables and criminal behavior. These variables include the motivation of the offender, victim behavior, social variables, and situational contexts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Landmark Cases in Criminal Procedure
Description: Examination of an array of notable Supreme Court criminal procedure cases by deeply delving into the litigation and surrounding stories that accompany each case. Ten to fourteen landmark cases commonly reviewed in Criminal Procedure I and II (Katz, Miranda, Terry, Batson, and Powell, to name a few) will be covered.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Justice Reform
Description: Exploration of contemporary criminal justice reform efforts with an emphasis on the role of race in criminal justice policy and practice. Likely areas of focus include policing, bail, and sentencing. Each student will complete a final research project evaluating or proposing a specific reform initiative.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Law Drafting
Description: The fundamentals of document drafting in the context of criminal law. Students will prepare documents that arise in a criminal law setting, including charging documents, notices, motions, bench briefs, and orders. Students will examine the function of these documents within the criminal justice system, including applicable statutory and case law. This course will require students to produce various graded documents of increasing complexity. Students will receive feedback from the professor on all graded assignments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Law Drafting
Description: The fundamentals of document drafting in the context of criminal law. Students will prepare documents that arise in a criminal law setting, including charging documents, notices, motions, bench briefs, and orders. Students will examine the function of these documents within the criminal justice system, including applicable statutory and case law. This course will require students to produce various graded documents of increasing complexity. Students will receive feedback from the professor on all graded assignments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Litigation
Description: Focuses on aspects of criminal litigation beginning in the immediate period following arrest up to trial from the perspective of both the prosecution and the defense. Coursework involves preparing for and conducting committal hearings, bond hearings, and various motions and other hearings commonly encountered in a criminal litigation practice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Trusts and Estates I
Description: Substantive and procedural rules concerning disposition of wealth, including intestate succession, wills, will substitutes and inter vivos and testamentary trusts; law of express and charitable trusts; remedies for wrongs relating to disposition of wealth; fiduciary powers, duties, and liabilities; construction problems relating to future interests and powers of appointment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Trusts and Estates II
Description: Continuation of study of procedural rules concerning disposition of wealth, including intestate succession, wills, will substitutes and inter vivos and testamentary trusts; express and charitable trusts; remedies for wrongs relating to disposition of wealth; fiduciary powers, duties, and liabilities; construction problems relating to future interests and powers of appointment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law and Ethics of Lawyering
Description: The organization of the profession and its standards of professional conduct as set forth in the rules of professional responsibility promulgated by the American Bar Association and the State Bar of Georgia.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law and Ethics of Lawyering
Description: The organization of the profession and its standards of professional conduct as set forth in the rules of professional responsibility promulgated by the American Bar Association and the State Bar of Georgia.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Common Law Jurisprudence
Description: Through a survey of the historical development of the common law, courts, and the legal profession on both sides of the Atlantic, this course will explore the goals, structure, values, and regulations of the legal profession and its members.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Administrative Law
Description: Focuses on law controlling federal and state administrative action. Along with constitutional restraints, student is asked to consider statutory and judicially formulated rules for administrative process. Control over administrative discretion and enforced accountability are major themes. Attention is devoted to federal and state Administrative Procedure Acts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Administrative Law
Description: Focuses on law controlling federal and state administrative action. Along with constitutional restraints, student is asked to consider statutory and judicially formulated rules for administrative process. Control over administrative discretion and enforced accountability are major themes. Attention is devoted to federal and state Administrative Procedure Acts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Admiralty
Description: Admiralty jurisdiction and selected topics in the maritime law, including maritime liens, injuries to seamen and other maritime workers, carriage of goods, charter parties, salvage, general average, collision, limitation of liability, and the relation of maritime law to local law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Antitrust Law
Description: Federal antitrust law with emphasis on leading cases decided by the United States Supreme Court under Sherman and Clayton Acts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Antitrust Law and Policy Seminar
Description: Examination of the legal structures aimed at promoting a competitive market economy. Covers both public enforcement by agencies and private suits that have advanced changes in the law. While the course will pay special attention to developments in case law, it will also consider pertinent policy-making decisions by Congress and the agencies.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Bankruptcy
Description: Survey of insolvency legislation; jurisdiction of U.S. Bankruptcy Court and concurrent state jurisdiction; administrative officials; petition and petitioners; individual debtor's discharge; assets of estate; claims, priorities, and distribution; and, if time permits, overview of Chapter 13, debts of an individual with regular income.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Bankruptcy Practice Seminar
Description: Exploration of the lifecycle of a corporate bankruptcy from the perspective of multiple stakeholders, including debtors, lenders, and creditors. Through simulated negotiations, hearings, and meetings that would occur during the restructuring process, students will develop critical strategy and practice skills while increasing their understanding of bankruptcy law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Contemporary Issues in Business Law
Description: This seminar examines contemporary issues that are prevalent in the regulation of business organizations and activities.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Problems Seminar
Description: Review of economic, social, and management science theories applicable to law firm organization, operation, and evolution. Analysis of economic consequences of specific law firm activities associated with the recruitment, training, and promotion of attorneys, execution of specific practice development strategies, and servicing of particular client categories and practice areas.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Fundamentals Mini Boot Camp
Description: An introduction to basic business and financial concepts. All law students should consider taking this course, particularly students who do not have extensive knowledge of or experience in business. Topics will include an overview of various common business entities, corporate governance, types of investors, securities, securities markets, insurance, and banking.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Economic Analysis of Law
Description: Application of economic principles to analysis of legal issues and institutions. Focus upon law's determination of fundamental market context governing economic exchange (torts, contracts, crime control) and discrimination prohibitions as definers and protectors of property rights upon effects of government intervention and performance of law enforcement agencies and judiciary.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Accounting and Finance for Lawyers
Description: The general foundation of accounting and finance for law students planning to manage a private law firm.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Military Law
Description: A study of criminal, civil, and administrative law as it applies to the United States military with focus on military justice including historical and constitutional bases of military courts, rights of accused under the military justice code, criminal procedure, and trials by court martial.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Civil-Military Relations: The Role of the Military in the United States
Description: This course is narrowly focused on the proper role of the military under the United States Constitution and other laws as well as cultural and societal norms that have been inculcated and fostered since the founding of the nation. It is complementary to other courses that deal with broader subjects under our domestic and applicable international law, such as Constitutional Law and the Law of War.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Comparative Corporate Law
Description: Examination of corporate law and the corporate form from a comparative perspective, with particular emphasis placed on how large publicly traded companies are governed and regulated in some of the world’s leading commercial and financial jurisdictions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Conflict of Laws
Description: Jurisdiction over persons and things; domicile as basis of personal jurisdiction; law governing creation of personal and property rights; recognition and enforcement by one state of rights created by laws of another state, including questions arising from capacity, marriage, legitimacy, and inheritance; nature and effect of judgments and decrees, and enforcement outside rendering jurisdiction; choice of law; impact of Constitution on conflict issues.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Theory of Conflict
Description: Introduces students to important theoretical perspectives on our understanding of conflict and conflict responses through discussion of popular literature within each discipline.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Constitutional Litigation Seminar
Description: Addresses issues in damage actions under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983, authorizing cause of action against constitutional violations under color of state law. Topics include distinction between common law and constitutional torts, scope of governmental liability, official immunity, damages, causation, state court suits, procedural defenses, attorney's fees, and meaning of "under color of."

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Foreign Affairs and National Security Law
Description: An examination of how United States law both constrains and is constrained by United States foreign relations and the foreign policy-making process. The course covers issues relating to separation of powers, federalism, individual rights, and the influence of international norms on United States constitutional development.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Copyright Law
Description: Focus is upon various methods to protect literary, musical, and artistic work under law of copyright. Copyright is a statutory subject based upon Copyright Act of 1909 and its amendments and Copyright Act of 1976. The course deals with what can be copyrighted, infringement actions, rights enjoyed by the copyright proprietor, jurisdiction, and various remedies.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Resolution of Corporate Financial Distress
Description: Examines financial reorganization of financially distressed companies. Follows restructuring attempt of the firm and examines legal and economic aspects of attempting to restructure operations and obtain financing in an out-of-court workout and exchange offer as well as reorganizing under Chapter 11 of Bankruptcy Code.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Finance
Description: Corporate financing, including short-term and long-term debt, preferred stock, common stock, hybrid securities, how to protect from value appropriation by another class of corporate creditor/owner. Capital structure and duties of directors to various claimant classes will be examined using decisions about dividend policy and dissidents appraisal rights.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lending and Commercial Finance - Legal Fundamentals and Drafting Exercises
Description: This course will help an attorney be prepared when a client needs help with a new loan transaction. Focus on debt finance transactions and the legal considerations that shape those transactions. There will also be several writing and drafting exercises.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Venture Capital and Entrepreneurial Financing
Description: The financing needs of private companies, particularly high-growth entrepreneurial companies. Course readings and discussion will concentrate on legal and business aspects of entrepreneurial financing transactions involving such companies.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Procedure I
Description: Criminal process from pre-arrest investigation to trial, including guilty pleas. Emphasis on pre-trial rights of persons suspected of crime, including privilege against self-incrimination, right to be free from unreasonable search and seizure, and due process and other rights attaching to pre-trial confrontation between accused and witnesses.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Procedure II
Description: Criminal process from bringing of formal charges to adjudication of guilt or innocence. Emphasis on prosecutorial discretion; preliminary hearing and grand jury procedures; joinder and severance; plea bargaining; criminal discovery; right to speedy trial, assistance of counsel, confrontation, and trial by jury; double jeopardy; and sentencing.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Procedure II
Description: The criminal process from bringing formal charges to adjudication of guilt or innocence. Emphasis on prosecutorial discretion; preliminary hearing and grand jury procedures; joinder and severance; plea bargaining; criminal discovery; right to a speedy trial, the assistance of counsel, confrontation, and trial by jury; double jeopardy; and sentencing.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Post Conviction Relief
Description: Analysis of judicial relief in federal and state systems for persons detained pursuant to conviction, who assert unlawful detention. Habeas corpus, statutory motions to vacate or set aside, and other modes of relief, including coram nobis. Consideration will be given to proposals to alter or abolish present procedures.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Federal Habeas Corpus
Description: Examination of the history and development of the writ of habeas corpus in the courts of the United States. Habeas corpus, known as the Great Writ, traces its history from the Magna Carta through the current term in the Supreme Court.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Crime and Punishment: Understanding the Carceral State
Description: The carceral state is a term used to speak about one particular mode of organizing, distributing, and justifying government power in American society. We will examine the carceral state in detail and start by looking at the history of policing and prisons.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Criminal Defense Practicum II - Service Learning
Description: Students will assist attorneys in Legal Aid and Defender Clinic in handling defense of criminal cases and receive intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture, and actual representation of clients. Clinic also handles juvenile cases.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 4-6 hours lab per week.
title: Criminal Defense Practicum II
Description: Students will assist attorneys in Legal Aid and Defender Clinic in handling defense of criminal cases and receive intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture, and actual representation of clients. Clinic also handles juvenile cases.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 4-6 hours lab per week.
title: Criminal Defense Practicum II Hours
Description: Intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture and representation of clients by students licensed to practice under the Law School Legal Aid Agency Act.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: First Amendment Seminar
Description: Study of the legal aspects of First Amendment law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Equitable Remedies
Description: Study of injunction and specific performance decree. Attention given to injunction and its availability at temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction stages, and after trial upon merits. Restitution at law studied at length. Course focuses on choice of remedies and emphasizes "election of remedies" opportunities and implications of each choice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Estate Planning Seminar
Description: Typical problems involved in planning effective and economical gift distribution of property interests. Attention given to preparation of estate plans and drafting of appropriate instruments to accomplish goals. Focus on restrictions imposed by law of trusts, wills, future interests, and federal taxation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Document Drafting: Special Topics in Estate Planning
Description: The fundamentals of document drafting focusing on selected topics in estate planning. Among other things, the course will require students to produce successive drafts of documents and provisions that incorporate feedback from the professor.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Document Drafting: Special Topics in Estate Planning
Description: The fundamentals of document drafting focusing on selected topics in estate planning. Among other things, the course will require students to produce successive drafts of documents and provisions that incorporate feedback from the professor.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Federal Courts
Description: Nature, source, and extent of federal judicial power. Original, removal, and appellate jurisdiction and procedure in federal courts. Study of state law as rule of decision.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Federalist Papers
Description: Focuses on the framing and ratification of the United States Constitution and the role of The Federalist Papers in that process.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Federal Power and the States
Description: Focuses on the authority of the federal government and federal courts over states and state courts. Coverage will include: federal authority and state courts, the power/duty of state courts to hear federal claims, state law, and the enforcement of federal rights.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Judicial Process
Description: Focuses on process of judging, professionalism in court system, specialized courts, comparison of English and American judicial systems, judicial reform, and similar topics. Designed particularly for those who will become judicial clerks upon graduation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 0.5-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Select Topics in Judicature
Description: Selected areas of judicial administration and judging that are too narrow for a full-semester course. Topics may include judicial case management, the judicial role in criminal and civil matters, the role of judges or courts in society and literature, comparative approaches to judging in different legal systems, etc.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Supreme Court
Description: The Supreme Court of the United States is a unique institution with its own history, personalities and appellate practice. This course examines the Court, including an in-depth look at the current nine justices. Students then argue cases from the Court's current docket and write an opinion in a case.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Supreme Court in the Political Process
Description: Examination of the role the Supreme Court actually plays in our self-governing process. In furtherance of this, we will study the Court less as a law maker and more as an actor and re-actor in the political system. Course materials will include various books and political science papers examining the interplay of court decisions, elected officials, and social movements. We also will discuss the political aspects of Supreme Court decision making and the justice selection process.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Freedom of Information Law Seminar
Description: Examines citizen access to government under constitutional, statutory and common law, especially state sunshine laws, emphasizing the function of the news media. Covers current FOI legal issues, including legislative trends and processes, as well as policy issues, such as personal privacy, national security, and the challenges of electronic records.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Regulation of Information
Description: Study of the latest academic thinking and doctrinal development of the regulation of knowledge through information controls. From privacy to insider trading to state secrets, our law regulates information to prevent the harms arising from undesirable distributions of knowledge.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Federal Taxation of Estates, Gifts, and Trusts
Description: Focuses on federal tax law and policy affecting the transfer of wealth, including the gift tax, the estate tax, and the generation-skipping transfer tax. Statutes, regulations, and interpretative materials and their application to hypothetical problems are addressed to lay the groundwork for the study of estate planning.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Tax
Description: The taxation of corporations and their shareholders. Major topics include contributions of property to corporations, distributions and redemptions by corporations, and taxable and tax-free mergers and acquisitions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Georgia Practice and Procedure
Description: Advanced course in Civil Procedure. Explores Georgia Civil Practice Act and Long-Arm Statute as interpreted by Georgia appellate court decisions, along with selected constitutional and statutory provisions allocating jurisdiction among trial courts, venue, and validity of judgments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Solo and Small Firm Practice
Description: Provides a roadmap for the new lawyer to establish a solo law practice or to join with other lawyers in creating or expanding a small law firm.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Innovation in the Practice of Law
Description: Introduces students to innovations necessary to keep pace with a rapidly changing legal industry and that will ensure that those in need of representation have equal access to justice, including, among others: AI, predictive analytics, process management, alternative pricing models, and collaborative workspace platforms.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Insurance Law
Description: The law relating to one entity's (the insurer's) promises to pay for losses incurred by another (the insured).

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Public International Law
Description: Foundation for students interested in international dimensions of law. International law concerns not only matters of intergovernmental and international organizational relations, but also many matters which the private practitioner deals with in daily work with transnational operations and transactions for national and transnational enterprises.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law of War
Description: The laws and customs intended to regulate war – not only when and whether law permits resort to armed conflict, but also national and international legal rules and regimes governing how war is to be waged and when actors may be sanctioned for violating those rules.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Law II
Description: Areas of international law in which important changes have occurred since 1945. Particular studies include: international conflicts in which the United Nations has played an important role; the United Nations' lawmaking activities in peace-making, peace-keeping, and human rights; and arms control and reciprocal reduction of armaments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Human Rights
Description: Study of international human rights law and international and regional organizations, states, and private actors in the field. Examines instruments and institutions forming sources of human rights law (UN system, including Charter and treaties, European, African and Inter-American human rights regimes), the role of NGOs, and interaction between domestic and international law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Business Transactions
Description: Examination of the legal regime governing a variety of international business transactions. Topics include international sales, international finance, and anti-corruption legislation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Business Transactions
Description: Examination of the legal regime governing a variety of international business transactions. Topics include international sales, international finance, and anti-corruption legislation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Legal Transactions
Description: Prepares lawyers to advise companies engaged in transnational transactions. Economic and legal natures of transnational enterprises and their legal consequences; national rules and international conventions on basic aspects of litigation, including comparisons of rules on jurisdiction and enforcement of judgments, and transnational arbitration.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law of Transnational Investments
Description: Trade and investment in the economies of other countries are more than ever essential components of the prosperity sought in all parts of the world. This course will examine the major actors involved in investment and financing across national boundaries.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Taxation
Description: The role of the American lawyer acting as tax planner in context of transnational business transactions; United States income taxation consequences of foreign corporations and individuals doing business and investing in the United States; similar tax consequences of American companies and individuals doing business and investing in foreign countries.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Commercial Arbitration
Description: Examination of the legal regime governing international commercial arbitration. Topics will include the enforcement of arbitration agreements, arbitral procedure and the enforcement of arbitral awards. The course also will cover how to draft arbitral clauses.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Children and International Law
Description: Explores developments at the intersection of international, family, labor, and criminal law. The Children’s Rights Convention as well as other treaties, many of which are enforceable in United States courts, will be examined. These treaties cover issues like adoption and abduction, child labor and trafficking, and child soldiers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Children and the Law
Description: Examination of the status of children in society and how the law treats their relationships with their parents and the state. Includes study of issues relating to child custody and dependency, neglect, abuse, medical care, abortion, foster care, adoption, illegitimacy, curfews, child pornography, pedophilia (including internet predators), and the juvenile justice system.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lawyering for Children
Description: Explores the responsibilities of lawyers for children and the factors that influence their interactions with child clients and lawyering decisions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Labor Law
Description: National Labor Relations Act, focusing on history and evolution of labor relations laws, union organizational activity, collective bargaining, economic weapons, the duty of fair representation, and federalism and labor relations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Responsibility
Description: Examination of the recent increase in corporate reorganization/restructuring which created focus on decisions by managers which have an impact on employee jobs, such as closure or sales of plants/businesses, subcontracting or outsourcing of work and layoffs. Focus on federal/state laws (NLRA; WARN Act) which impose obligations on employers in such situations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Responsibility
Description: Examination of the recent increase in corporate reorganization/restructuring which created focus on decisions by managers which have an impact on employee jobs, such as closure or sales of plants/businesses, subcontracting or outsourcing of work, and layoffs. Focus on federal/state laws (NLRA; WARN Act) which impose obligations on employers in such situations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Labor Arbitration
Description: Simulation course in which students will take on roles of union counsel, management counsel, and arbitrators.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Real Estate Transactions
Description: Basic components of conveyancing with emphasis on finance, acquisition, and development of real property. Financing techniques and default and foreclosure; review of issues raised by contemporary innovations in financing and ownership of real property.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Real Estate Transactions
Description: Basic components of conveyancing with emphasis on finance, acquisition, and development of real property. Financing techniques and default and foreclosure, and review of issues raised by contemporary innovations in financing and ownership of real property.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Land Use Planning
Description: Analysis of the legal and administrative aspects of the regulation of land use for development and the problems and techniques of urban planning. Particular attention is given to zoning, subdivision controls, public acquisition of land, and urban redevelopment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Land Conservation Clinic
Description: The legal foundations of private land conservation, as well as the policy and environmental basis for this work. Students will explore conservation easements, the role of land trusts, the ecological and public benefits of protected land, and ways to enhance the impact of private conservation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Land Conservation Clinic Hours
Description: Law and graduate students from other disciplines will provide advice and drafting assistance to nonprofits, government agencies, and others on land conservation issues, with an emphasis on supporting private land conservation. Students will research, analyze, and draft transactional documents, reports, and guidebooks; counsel clients; and address policy and ecological challenges.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Natural Resources Law
Description: Statutory, case law, and regulations concerning resource conservation, allocation, and development. Modern, systems-sensitive regulatory programs affecting natural resources administration analyzed. Examination of the division and nature of the functions of the judicial and executive branches of government.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Natural Resources Law
Description: Statutory, case law, and regulations concerning resource conservation, allocation, and development. Modern, systems-sensitive regulatory programs affecting natural resources administration analyzed. Examination of the division and nature of the functions of the judicial and executive branches of government.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Georgia Election Law
Description: Examination of Georgia law regulating the political process and how it shapes policy outcomes. Covers election law within Georgia.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sociology of Law
Description: Empirical patterns of legal behavior, such as initiation and winning of lawsuits, origins and content of rules, and development of legal institutions. Lectures and readings invoke social characteristics of participants (e.g., social ties, status, marginality, reputation, and organizational affiliations) to predict and explain case outcomes. Sociological techniques by which social differentials might be minimized.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Race and Law
Description: Exploration of the definition of race, as well as its historical role in American society. In particular, the course will look at how the law has been used to both support and suppress racism. The course will look at historical and current illustrations of the intersection of race and law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sexual Orientation and Gender Law
Description: Examines legal regulation relating to sexual orientation and identity and the impact of such laws on sexual minorities. Focuses on relevant constitutional, family, property, immigration law and state and local laws protecting or discriminating against sexual minorities. Course will examine interaction between legal developments and social mores.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sexual Orientation and Gender Law
Description: Examines legal regulation relating to sexual orientation and identity and the impact of such laws on sexual minorities. Focuses on relevant constitutional, family, property, immigration laws, and state and local laws protecting or discriminating against sexual minorities. Course will examine the interaction between legal developments and social mores.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law, Medicine, and Culture
Description: Examination of medical-legal issues in a religious and cross-cultural context. Topics discussed include euthanasia, assisted suicide, abortion, surrogacy, informed consent, and cultural conflicts between immigrants/minorities and the American medical community. Reading material includes court cases from various countries and discussions from medical, legal, and anthropological journals/books.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Law and Politics
Description: The role of lawyers in lawmaking and public policy, and the political aspects of various policy issues.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Election Law
Description: Examination of the law regulating our political process, and consideration of how those regulatory choices shape substantive policy outcomes. The course covers campaign finance regulation, redistricting, voting rights, and the regulation of political party primaries.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Renewable Energy Law and Policy
Description: Examination of development and use of various energy sources, including traditional areas such as oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear. Particular emphasis will be placed on development of alternative sources of energy, including solar, geothermal, wind and biomass, and the role of government in encouraging development.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Animal Law
Description: Exploration of the legal treatment of animals. Topics include: ethical approaches to animals; regulatory schemes for wildlife (e.g., hunting regimes, endangered species); regulation of domesticated animals for food, research, and entertainment; regulation of veterinary practices; and animal issues in traditional areas of law, including property, torts, and criminal law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Water Law
Description: The allocation, management, and protection of water resources. Water law is more substantially developed in arid Western states, but is increasingly important in Eastern states that are facing water scarcity. Water law focuses on allocation, access, and use.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Intelligence Law and National Security Policy
Description: Survey of intelligence and related national security law and policy issues. The focus will be on how United States intelligence activities are affected by Constitutional separation of powers, the law of covert action, the criminal law system, the Bill of Rights, issues in counter-terrorist policy, and other federal laws.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Women and the Law
Description: The historical and current legal status of women and, by comparison, of men in the United States, with emphasis on recent changes in constitutional and statutory law; the role the courts have played in that change; remedies (administrative, legislative, and judicial) for challenging legal classifications based on sex stereotypes.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Critical Race Feminism
Description: Critical race feminism is part of an evolving tradition that originated with critical legal studies and its off-shoots of feminist critical theory and critical race theory. Critical race feminism's core mission is an anti-essentialist exploration of the historical and contemporary issues in the law that affect primarily women of color law as well as others who fall into the gaps of traditional conceptualizations in the law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Regulation of the Human Body
Description: Examination of the ways in which we regulate the human body and its uses, treatment, and materials. As we study these regulations, we will also examine the underlying cultural assumptions embodied in the laws. The exact topics covered will vary by semester.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Religion
Description: The history and judicial construction of the Establishment and Free Exercise Clauses of the First Amendment. The course will also include a section exploring how several religious traditions approach the relationship between religion and law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Election Law Reform: Selected Issues
Description: In-depth look at various proposals to reform or change the way we run elections. Topics covered will include electronic and internet voting, voter registration and identification laws, and the "Democracy Index," as well as more fundamental changes, such as mandatory voting and proportional representations systems.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law in the Gospels
Description: Comparative legal history, involving "law in action" in the life of one man. This is not a class about religion or religious faith. It is about the stance of Jesus on legal issues and the authorities' response.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Sustainability
Description: Examination of legal structures aimed at promoting environmental, social, and economic sustainability of corporate activities, with particular emphasis placed on how publicly traded companies are governed and regulated in some of the world's leading commercial and financial jurisdictions. The seminar further considers the intersection of corporate law with other legal fields and disciplines that impact corporate sustainability.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Document Drafting: Survey
Description: An overview of drafting non-litigation documents. Develops the skills required to draft statutes, will, and contracts. The course also focuses on gathering information to provide a factual basis for the preparation of such documents and drafting such documents within the existing legal framework.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Document Drafting: Survey
Description: An overview of drafting non-litigation documents. Develops the skills required to draft statutes, wills, and contracts. The course also focuses on gathering information to provide a factual basis for the preparation of such documents and drafting such documents within the existing legal framework.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: English Legal History
Description: The evolution of English law and legal institutions, with emphasis on constitutional law, development of the court systems, and nineteenth-century legal reforms. American legal history will also be examined when time permits.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: American Legal History
Description: Examination of the role that law and legal institutions have played in American history from Reconstruction until the 1980s. We will examine the Civil War Amendments and federalism, laissez-faire formalism and economic regulation, the growth of legal liberalism, and the rights revolution.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Georgia History for Lawyers
Description: A survey of the people, places, and events that form the history of the State of Georgia from prehistoric times to the present, including the ways in which that history has intersected with Georgia and U.S. law. Students will be expected to produce a paper examining in depth an issue of legal importance in Georgia history.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Topics in Legal History
Description: Examination of the role of law and legal institutions in shaping politics, society, and economics. The course will cover time periods from the colonial period and its European and Native American antecedents to the twentieth century.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Statutory Interpretation and the Legislative Process
Description: Exploration of how legislatures make statutes and how courts interpret them. Rather than focusing on a single statute, the class will familiarize students with general procedural and interpretive principles that are relevant in a variety of practice settings.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Statutory Interpretation and the Legislative Process
Description: Exploration of how legislatures make statutes and how courts interpret them. Rather than focusing on a single statute, the class will familiarize students with general procedural and interpretive principles that are relevant in a variety of practice settings.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legislation and Regulation
Description: Our legal system comprises many institutions, all tasked with making and interpreting various kinds of laws. This course ventures beyond common law courts to examine legislatures, executive agencies, and other kinds of lawmakers. It will ask why and how we regulate and how lawmaking institutions are related to one another.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legislation and Regulation
Description: Our legal system comprises many institutions, all tasked with making and interpreting various kinds of laws. This course ventures beyond common law courts to examine legislatures, executive agencies, and other kinds of lawmakers. It will ask why and how we regulate and how lawmaking institutions are related to one another.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: How a Bill Becomes a Law: Legislative Process and Drafting
Description: Learn the inner workings of how a bill becomes a law, with an emphasis on the Georgia legislative process.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legislative Interpretation Seminar
Description: Exploration of contemporary theories of, and debates in, statutory and constitutional interpretation. Use of commentaries and, to a much smaller extent, Supreme Court cases from the last term or two. Each student will complete a semester-long writing project on an interpretation question chosen in consultation with the professor.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: State and Local Governments
Description: Examination of the relationships among local governments, states, and the Federal government. Issues to be addressed include the role of local government, the source of local government power, and the advantages and disadvantages of decentralized decision making. These questions will be explored in both general and specific subject areas.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Georgia State and Local Government
Description: Exploration of the principles of state and local government in Georgia. Issues include organizational structures of local governments and the authority granted by the U.S. and Georgia Constitutions. Writing and research associated with practice in this area and reflection on professional roles and responsibilities are elements of the course.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Natural Resources
Description: The law governing the acquisition and use of natural resources, with particular regard to natural resources on publicly-owned lands.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Patent Law
Description: Patents are federal exclusionary rights for inventions, and a few are worth billions of dollars. Their complexity, high value, and intangibility have led to extensive litigation and judicial ingenuity at the Federal Circuit and Supreme Court. Survey of the law and policy of validity, transactions, and enforcement for patents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Patent Prosecution and Procedure
Description: Study of how to write and prosecute a United States patent application. The course both introduces students to common issues arising during patent prosecution and equips students with basic strategies to deal with those issues. The course also explores patent infringement analysis and opinion letter work in which patent lawyers routinely engage.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Patent Management
Description: An overview of practical patent management and corresponding legal issues in four venues: operations, transactions (including finance), competition, and litigation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Trademark Law
Description: Acquisition of trademark rights, registration, infringement, false advertising, dilution, remedies, and international aspects of trademark law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Franchise Law
Description: Provides overview of the legal aspects of franchising as a distribution system.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Secured Transactions
Description: Basic commercial law course dealing with secured financing when the collateral consists of personal property, including goods, fixtures, intangibles, and intellectual property. Focus is on Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code. The course should help students to develop their skills in statutory analysis and in understanding and planning business transactions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Securities Regulation
Description: Examination of controls relevant to the sale and distribution of securities by corporations, underwriters, and others, including such matters as scope of the securities laws, the public offering, exempt transactions, disclosure obligations, express and implied civil liability, and secondary distributions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Disability and Education Law
Description: Students with disabilities are entitled to specific educational services and accommodations in public schools in the United States. This course will introduce undergraduate and graduate students to federal and state laws and regulations that apply to the provision of educational services for students with disabilities from birth through age 21.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Disability and Education Law
Description: Students with disabilities are entitled to specific educational services and accommodations in public schools in the United States. This course will introduce undergraduate and graduate students to federal and state laws and regulations that apply to the provision of educational services for students with disabilities from birth through age 21.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Employment Discrimination
Description: Law regulating distinctions in the employment relationship. The emphasis is on federal statutory law regulating race, sex, religion, national origin, age, and disability discrimination in employment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: State and Local Taxation
Description: A study of principles and problems of state and local taxation in our federal system. Examines ad valorem property taxes, corporate and personal income taxes, sales and use taxes, and Federal constitutional limitations on state tax power.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Georgia Law Review
Description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Georgia Law Review

Description: A two-student team practices oral arguments under the supervision of a faculty advisor in preparation for a competition against the University of Florida before a panel of state and federal judges. A student registering for this course must be selected as a competing advocate who will attend the competition in the semester in which the student registers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: Student teams prepare civil or criminal jury trials under the supervision of a faculty advisor by preparing and presenting pretrial evidentiary motions, opening statements, direct and cross examinations of witnesses, and closing arguments. A student must be selected as a competing advocate who will attend a competition in the semester in which the student registers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: Through this simulation course, students will learn about the child welfare system, trauma-informed lawyering, and interdisciplinary collaboration through classroom instruction and participation in a mock termination of parental rights trial. Guest faculty will include attorneys, judges, and social workers.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Child Welfare Law and Practice

Description: An introduction to researching intellectual property, including copyrights, patents, and trademarks. In addition to reviewing administrative regulation research, this course will explore a variety of free and fee-based tools. Topics include classification and search techniques and intellectual property searching in business research and competitive intelligence.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Workers' Compensation
Description: The historical evolution and current operation of modern workers' compensation systems. Exploration of the extent to which the no-fault workers' compensation model could serve as an alternative to tort litigation in other areas of personal injury, such as medical malpractice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Planning and Drafting for the Closely Held Business
Description: Introduction to the issues which are important in planning, negotiation, execution of agreements, and documents which affect formation, operation, and disposition of small closely- held businesses. Emphasis is placed on drafting sample agreements such as limited liability operating agreements, buy- sell shareholder agreements, stock or asset sale agreements, and employment agreements.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Special emphasis on practical illustrations of Theory of the Firm, powers of Federal Reserve Board, and consequences of diverse governmental fiscal and monetary policies. Analysis of legal frameworks for major components of the financial services sector.

Students will also learn about the search warrant requirement and its “well- recognized exceptions,” identification of suspects, Confrontation Clause, and Right to Counsel.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

title: Prosecution III Hours
Description: Students will continue the process of learning the proper role of a prosecutor as a “minister of justice” in our criminal justice system. This portion encompasses working with professionals in this area.

Description: Presentations of substantial works-in-progress on a variety of international law topics by prominent scholars from other law schools.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Lawyers, Kings, Despots, and Revolutionaries: How Lawyers Create and Destroy Political Freedom
Description: This course examines the role that lawyers across time and space have played in creating and defending democratic government that respects the rule of law. We will examine the role that lawyers played in insulating the rule of law from the arbitrary exercise of monarchical power, the role lawyers have played since 1900 in defending democracy and the rule of law from authoritarian governments, and evaluate the performance of lawyers in defending these institutions in the United States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Wilderness Law and Policy
Description: Provides an in-depth look at the federal lands managed under the Wilderness Act of 1964 and subsequent enactments, as well as the regulations that the federal land management agencies employ in governing these lands. In addition, systems of state, private, and international wilderness protection will be discussed.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Wildlife Law
Description: Overview of how the legal system deals with wildlife issues. Federal law is considered, with the primary focus on the 50- state law level, as the state fish and wildlife agencies have primary responsibility for managing wildlife. Students will review wildlife-related laws from a variety of perspectives, including sustainable use, regulated hunting, and sound wildlife management.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Boot Camp in Animal Welfare Skills
Description: This is an intensive-learning class focused on the skills necessary for an animal welfare law practice. It will cover the legal regulation of animals in Georgia and the means of enforcing the various governing statutes. Students will learn to prepare the basic forms used in an animal welfare practice.
