Description: This is a practicum in which students will learn to identify, investigate, and prosecute animal welfare crimes and ordinance violations. In some semesters, it may include drafting ordinances and state laws, providing an analysis of laws presented for adoption by others, and other related tasks.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: A case study approach to cover the types and purposes of writing found in an environmental law practice. Students will study and draft a number of the typical documents used in environmental rulemaking, public comments and rulemaking responses, transactional agreements, and environmental litigation. Students will be working from the perspectives of the variety of stakeholders found in environmental law, including property owners, industry, and the general public.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: A survey of many different topics: adaptation and resilience, climate and energy, water supply and reuse, and land management and transportation. Overarching themes explored across all content areas include legal constraints of city authority, governance, and the roles of various types of institutions in developing, advancing, and advocating for local policy change.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Climate Change Seminar
Description: The law of climate change in the United States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Policy and Ecological Implications of Climate Change in Georgia
Description: A look at climate change worldwide, with a focus on Georgia, looking at consequences on human health and safety, water availability, weather patterns, agriculture, infrastructure, biodiversity, environmental justice, and other issues.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Environmental Practice Seminar
Description: This seminar will expose the students to practical questions presented in handling environmental litigation. The material is presented through case studies, mock depositions, mock penalty negotiations, class presentations, and guest lectures.

Description: Advanced research in legal control of environmental problems, with primary attention given to water and biodiversity issues. Law students work with graduate students from other disciplines, including ecology, forestry, agriculture, and environmental design, to address problems identified by watershed stakeholders.

Description: Many controversial and fascinating issues face the modern family and the legal system. This seminar provides the opportunity to explore some of these issues in depth. While the primary focus will be on American family law, use will be made of comparative material.

Description: Overlapping regulation of employment by the National Labor Relations Act, Title VII, the Americans with Disabilities Act, and state common law claims.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Communications Law Seminar
Description: Fundamental goals and policies served by our First Amendment, focusing on state torts of defamation and privacy, as limited by First Amendment concerns. The course will also cover the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, and the federal regulations of broadcasting and cable.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Trade Laws
Description: National and international policies and laws relating to international trade and investment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

title: International Legal Research
Description: Selected area of international and comparative law. Topics may include a particular field of law in another country, a comparative study of a particular field of law in two or more countries, or other topics selected by the professor.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Special International Law Studies II
Description: Selected topics focusing on the legal institutions of another legal system, including the legislative, judicial, and administrative structures used to operate the legal system. Topics may include separation of powers, judicial review, federalism, social welfare institutions, and the criminal justice system.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Arbitration Seminar
Description: Exploration of the arbitration process in context of labor and employment disputes in nonunion and union settings. Students prepare and present an arbitration case and also write an arbitration award. No formal prerequisites, but either Employment Discrimination, Employment Law, or Labor Law are helpful.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Interviewing, Counseling, Negotiating
Description: Focuses upon theories of psychology, sociology, and conflict resolution, as applied to three of the most fundamental skills for litigators — interviewing, counseling, and negotiating. Students then have the opportunity to hone these skills through hands-on, practice-based simulations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: Current topics in securities litigation, such as RICO, fraud on the market, the international reach of rule 10b-5, and SEC actions.

Description: This course focuses on moving disputing parties from an agreement in principle to an enforceable settlement document. Students learn the elements that make agreements complete and binding, the drafting skills that make them clear, and common issues that undermine enforceability. Students discuss contested agreements and complete written assignments.

Students learn the elements that make agreements complete and binding, the drafting skills that make them clear, and common issues that undermine enforceability. Students discuss contested agreements and complete written assignments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Description: The written motion is a litigator’s basic tool for seeking and obtaining court rulings in a variety of contexts during the course of litigation. This course provides an overview of, and practice in applying, the legal principles applicable to drafting motions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Students gain experience in writing the types of documents commonly required in this context, such as employment agreements, employment policies, advice memorandum, and other related documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence

Students gain experience in writing the types of documents commonly required in this context, such as employment agreements, employment policies, advice memorandum, and other related documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Regulation of Pensions and Employee Benefits
Description: The non-tax aspects of employee benefit law, with primary emphasis upon the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), including the policies behind the federal regulation of pensions and benefits; preemption of state law; spousal interests in pensions; fiduciary law; and plan termination.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Poverty and Financial Law
Description: Examination of the history and current regulatory structure of financial services to the poor. Examines the legal framework around the fringe banking sector, the credit union and savings and loan movements, postal banking, and other poverty-related financial initiatives.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Banking Law
Description: Case and problem study of American banking system. Focuses on federal and state regulation of financial institutions and includes analysis of bank formations, bank mergers, bank holding companies, and the FDIC.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Real Estate Development
Description: Selected issues in real estate development law, including financing, securities, tax, and business planning considerations. Coursework will include negotiation and drafting of documentation for real estate project and preparation of memoranda.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Indian Law
Description: Cases and materials on the relation between Indian nations, the United States, and the States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Independent Project
Description: Independent projects provide flexible opportunity to explore independently legal issues or questions sometimes not found in any course or seminar and without following format of a formal research paper. Projects must involve significant legal, social, or empirical research or experience.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Law and Economic Development
Description: Impact on content of international law of increased concern of states with economic and social matters, both internally and at international level. Effects of enlarged international community and emergence of important new actors (international organizations and transnational corporations) examined in light of new sources of international law.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Design and Construction Law
Description: Examines the legal framework of the design and construction process. The course focuses on application of tort and contract law to contract formation and performance issues, and will examine legal remedies available to construction project participants.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Housing Law Seminar
Description: Selected issues in housing law and policy. The course typically covers affordable housing, environmental aspects of housing, fair housing, homelessness, homeowners' associations, housing products including condominiums, housing quality and standards, landlord-tenant law, mortgage financing, public housing, residential development, taxation, zoning and other land-use controls.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sports Law
Description: Basic theoretical and contractual premises of sports law, including areas of labor, antitrust, and contract law related to representation of athletic talent and sports businesses.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sports Law
Description: Basic theoretical and contractual premises of sports law, including areas of labor, antitrust, and contract law related to representation of athletic talent and sports businesses.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Complex Litigation
Description: Advanced civil procedure, including class actions, large case discovery, and judicial management of multi-party, multi-district litigation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Entertainment Law
Description: Basic theoretical and contractual underpinnings of entertainment law and areas of intellectual property and contracts law related to representation of artistic talent.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Visual Arts and the Law
Description: Legal issues in the visual arts world, including controversial art/censorship, moral rights, intersection of First Amendment and intellectual property laws, lost/stolen art, looting of cultural antiquities, artist-gallery partnership, auction houses, agents, museums and art dealers, consignment of art, and developments about public funding of the arts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Media Law
Description: Examination of a variety of legal issues affecting the news media. Discussion of traditional constitutional issues and exploration of how these traditional principles are balanced against competing interests not only in constitutional law but also in common law and statutory regulations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Media Law
Description: Examination of a variety of legal issues affecting the news media. Discussion of traditional constitutional issues and exploration of how these traditional principles are balanced against competing interests not only in constitutional law but also in common law and statutory regulations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Student Press Law Seminar
Description: Issues in the law of media and free expression facing students specifically within contexts of K-12 schools and institutions of higher education. Issues include censorship, tort, intellectual property, information, and juvenile law. Students will be exposed to principles of journalism practice, ethics, and education. A paper is required.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Science Seminar
Description: Emerging technologies present an intrinsic challenge as new discoveries frequently extend beyond the reality anticipated by existing laws and regulations. The use of science in the courtroom or legislation (e.g., climate change) is often problematic as parties put forth competing claims as to what the law should regard as valid scientific evidence.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law, Science, and Technology
Description: Legal issues relating to science and technology, including governmental regulation of commercial application of scientific research, impact of technological developments on law, and constitutional concerns raised by modern science, technology, and medicine.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and the Information Age
Description: Examines many points of intersection between the internet and associated technologies and the legal landscape. Course begins with a series of 'public law' problems - freedom of expression and information privacy. Explores a number of intellectual property issues specific to information technologies and issues of jurisdiction and taxation of e-commerce.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Electronic Discovery
Description: Exploration of the legal issues that have arisen with the migration of business and personal transactions to the internet. Discussion of approaches to regulating internet transactions, statutes enacted to govern internet activity, and the emerging case law adapting existing statutory and case law to internet business.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Internet Law
Description: The legal and policy issues raised by computers and the internet. This course will explore how the internet’s digital and networked environment changes the nature of regulation, facilitates innovation, and refashions the relationships among public and private actors. Topics include jurisdiction, speech, privacy, intellectual property, e-commerce, and internet governance.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Cybercrime
Description: Exploration of how changes in technology challenge the law's traditional approaches to combating criminal activity, enforcing criminal law, and balancing the rights of the public against the demands of justice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Bioethics
Description: Examination of the legal, ethical, and social problems generated by advances in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Some of the issues covered include human cloning and stem cell research, gene-based therapies, death and dying, reproductive technologies, experimentation with human subjects, and societal limits on scientific developments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Bioethics
Description: Examination of the legal, ethical, and social problems generated by advances in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Some of the issues covered include human cloning and stem cell research, gene-based therapies, death and dying, reproductive technologies, experimentation with human subjects, and societal limits on scientific developments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: From Contraband to Commodity: Regulating the New Marijuana Markets
Description: Even a few years ago, marijuana was uniformly made contraband by both federal and state law. The legal status of marijuana is now in flux, among and between state and federal governments. This course explores regulation of these new marijuana markets, using economic analysis and other regulatory law-and-policy tools.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Regulating Digital Abuse
Description: Digital abuse is on the rise. People are increasingly using networked technologies to engage in harassment, stalking, privacy invasions, and surveillance. The law will often adapt to deal with harmful technologies, and one of the pressing challenges of our time is deciding whether and how to regulate digital abuse. This seminar will consider responses to the harms enabled by networked technologies, exploring issues related to civil rights, consumer protection, cybercrime, free speech, privacy, and private self-governance.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 0.5-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Special Legal Studies
Description: Selected areas of general law too narrow to occupy a full-semester course. Topics may include such areas as the trial of a medical malpractice case, negotiation strategies in contract law, representation of an immigrant in deportation proceedings, etc.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 0.5-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Special Legal Studies
Description: Selected areas of general law too narrow to occupy a full-semester course. Topics may include such areas as the trial of a medical malpractice case, negotiation strategies in contract law, representation of an immigrant in deportation proceedings, etc.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Legal Topics Seminar
Description: Study of current legal topics and contemporary legal issues usually not considered in traditional legal courses. Faculty members will include visitors who have unique experiences and offer knowledge to enhance law student learning.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Legal Topics Seminar
Description: Study of current legal topics and contemporary legal issues usually not considered in traditional legal courses. Faculty members will include visitors who have unique experiences and offer knowledge to enhance law student learning.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Political Leadership and the Law
Description: Examines the intersection of law and politics, with a special focus on leadership and how leadership qualities in the Executive and Legislative branches impact how federal laws ultimately affect the American public.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Multidistrict Litigation: Law, Practice, and Strategy
Description: This course dissects the legal problems and issues associated with aggregate litigation in federal multidistrict litigation by examining various court decisions, decisions by the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation, scholarly articles, empirical data, and litigation filings. It likewise considers strategic and ethical considerations.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Civil Tax Practice
Description: Study of practice before Internal Revenue Service and various tax forums, including audit process, procedures relating to determination of tax liability and tax collection, and extraordinary procedures, such as jeopardy and termination assessment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Criminal Tax Practice and Procedure
Description: Criminal tax investigations and prosecutions; constitutional defenses to the compulsory production of evidence; attorney-client privilege, confidentiality and other defenses available to taxpayers and third parties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Health Law Organization and Finance
Description: Focuses on the health care enterprises, such as hospitals and managed care systems, their organization, and the legal system's handling of fraud and abuse claims. Examination of the policy context of health care costs and access, including the obligation to provide care and regulation of insurance and managed care.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Health Care Fraud and Abuse
Description: Examination of federal and state laws imposing civil and criminal penalties on health care providers, with special emphasis on the federal False Claims Act, the Anti-Kickback Statute, and the Physician Self-Referral (Stark) Law. Ample experiential learning opportunities will be provided through use of drafting assignments, mock client advising problems, and guest lectures.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Public Health Law
Description: Public health law with historic, contemporary, and international comparative law-policy perspectives, discusses the government entities most involved in public health domestically and internationally, and then surveys a range of applications. Coverage encompasses reproductive health, vaccination, biodefense, integration of genomics (study of gene function) and population genetics into public health policy and practice, and international public health.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Medicine
Description: Focuses on the relationship between health care providers and patients. Topics include: the treatment relationship, professional liability, licensing, access to care (including EMTALA), quality of care, privacy and confidentiality (including HIPAA), and informed consent.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Health Law Seminar
Description: The course will explore various topics in health law, health policy, and bioethics, focusing on recurring themes of rationing scarce resources, balancing individual rights against community needs, and improving social welfare.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law of American Health Care
Description: Examination of the United States health care delivery system as a regulated industry. A survey of a variety of legal issues affecting health care providers and their interactions with commercial insurers, government health care programs, and state and federal regulators.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Mental Health Law
Description: The legal issues relating to mental health and illness, including competency, disability, confidentiality (HIPAA), duty to warn, civil commitment, criminal defenses, discrimination, and similar issues. Recommended for students planning careers in the helping professions, including social work, therapy, psychology, education, and criminal justice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Community Health Law Partnership
Description: The Community Health Law Partnership will partner with health care professionals to tackle a variety of legal needs that impact patients, including immigration, disability rights, benefits, and family law. Students will have direct responsibility for all aspects of client representation in cases undertaken by the clinic.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Community Health Law Partnership Clinic Hours
Description: Course engages students in three primary learning experiences: direct exposure to the skills and methods of legal practice; focused application of legal concepts to real conflicts; and reflective appraisal of their own abilities, values, and professional goals.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Health Law Survey
Description: An introduction to the United States health care system. Comparative discussion of health care systems in industrialized economies with a focus on distinguishing features of the United States system. The course covers a range of topics in the areas of liability, regulation, and bioethics.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and the Mind
Description: Examines how law is affected by both the traditional field of psychology and the emerging field of neuroscience. Broad topics include judge and jury decision-making, the psychological basis of criminal culpability, the psychological justifications for various legal rules and doctrines, and much more.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Food and Drug Law
Description: An overview of laws and regulations governing development, manufacturing, and commercial distribution of drugs, biologic, medical device products, and animal health products and how they relate to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industry. This includes domestic regulatory requirements and various regulatory agencies and their jurisdiction.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Timing in Federal Tax
Description: An in-depth investigation into the timing concepts of Federal Income Taxation. Examination of when items of income should be included and a deduction taken. Includes integrity of taxable year, tax accounting methods, inventory, depreciation, installment sales provision, net operating losses, tax benefit rule, claim of right doctrine, and equity compensation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Compliance: Controls and Breakdowns
Description: Examines the legal underpinnings and structural components of the compliance function in corporations. It reviews the key compliance issues for public companies, banks, and accounting firms, among other organizations, and deconstructs past compliance failures. The course also analyzes the role of attorneys working with, and as, compliance professionals.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Whistleblower Litigation Seminar
Description: This seminar focuses on the major Federal whistleblower statute, the civil False Claims Act, and its role in driving Government investigations and large recoveries in recent years. We examine liability theories and strategies for the Government, whistleblowers and defendants, as well as emerging new whistleblower programs.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Internal Investigations
Description: Examines how corporations and their personnel investigate their own conduct. Course will develop students’ understanding of the roles of management, the board of directors, and their respective counsel in corporate investigations and their interplay with government regulators, such as the Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Employment Law
Description: Legal aspects of employment relationship, excluding union/management and statutory discrimination issues. Primarily focuses on erosion of employment-at-will doctrine through various tort and contract theories. Unemployment compensation, OSHA and wage/hour laws are also covered.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: The Law of Business Crime
Description: The mens rea elements of federal crimes and the law of conspiracy and attempt. The course also addresses federal "white collar" crime statutes covering a variety of offenses, including fraud, bribery, racketeering and extortion, and cases interpreting these statutes.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: White Collar Prosecution
Description: An introduction to economic and political crimes (Georgia focus) under the label of “white collar crime,” including conspiracy, theft, fraud, racketeer-influenced and corrupt organizations (RICO), money laundering, computer and cyber-crimes, perjury and false statements, securities fraud, fraud upon financial institutions, and parallel non-criminal procedures associated with white collar crimes.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Business Ethics Seminar
Description: Corporate scandals make the headlines, but businesses face ethical challenges every day, even in situations that are legally compliant. This course will examine ethical issues confronted by businesses in a variety of contexts, from legal activities to those on the "slippery slope" to outright corruption. Students will consider different approaches to ethical decision-making and the lawyer's role in advising business clients.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Ethics Seminar II
Description: Continuation of Business Ethics Seminar. Continue to examine ethical issues confronted by businesses in a variety of contexts, from legal activities to those on the "slippery slope" to outright corruption. Students will consider different approaches to ethical decision-making and the lawyer's role in advising business clients.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Sustainable Business: Transactions and Strategy
Description: Introduces students to the concept of environmental sustainability, the legal challenges facing businesses in attaining environmental sustainability, the incentives for business to achieve sustainable commerce, and possible means that governments may have to encourage or stimulate environmentally sustainable commerce.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Commercial Law Seminar
Description: Advanced work on specific commercial law problems, including interrelationships between negotiability and security. Students research, write, and defend a paper addressed to a specific problem area.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Corporate Law Appellate Litigation
Description: Advanced course in corporate law appellate litigation in which students learn through experiencing the roles of both oral advocate and Delaware Supreme Court Justice in connection with two currently pending Delaware Supreme Court cases and the actual briefs filed therein.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Public Interest Practicum
Description: How to discover peoples' needs, how to summon community's resources for meeting those needs, and how to determine what lawyers can do to insure community's services are functioning. Students are required to work with both service institutions and individuals who are clients of those institutions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Public Interest Practicum Hours
Description: As part of the practicum, students are required to work with both service institutions and individuals who are clients of those institutions. This section is for the student's work.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Trial Practice
Description: Trials of advanced or multi-party cases, such as adverse possession, commercial litigation, conspiracy and product liability actions; some expanded problems in evidence and trial procedure. Drafting projects include pre-trial documents, motions in limine, and post-trial motions.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Literature
Description: Literature and literary theory relevant to legal issues such as procedural problems in death penalty cases, criminal responsibility and plea bargaining, rape, obscenity, modern tort law and parole evidence rule. Works covered include selections from: Euripides, Koestler, Kierkegaard, Frisch, Eco, Fish, Nussbaum, Posner, Foucault, and Nietzche.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law, Literature, and Business
Description: A survey of different methods of approaching law and literature. Exploration of how law and literature applies to the world of business entities, transactions, corporate disclosure, and the role of the business attorney.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. 1 hours lecture and 1-2 hours lab per week.
title: Law, Public Policy, and the Elderly
Description: Federal and state elderly programs and problems; special risk populations; significance of older population of elderly clients; guardianship; significance of older population growth; representation of elderly clients, guardianship; lifetime estate management; testamentary estate disposition; living and "right to die" debate; health and long-term care; housing, transportation, and employment policies; public assistance.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Dispute Resolution and Systems Design
Description: In a world of settlement, this course prepares students to effectively represent clients through an understanding of the design and strategic election between ADR processes, and development of best practices as counsel in each process. Both private processes (arbitration, negotiation, mediation) and public tribunals (domestic and international) are studied.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Dispute Resolution Systems Design
Description: The systemic analysis and design of dispute resolution processes, with a focus on large-scale and complex settings. Participants will survey various approaches to disputes, including facilitative, evaluative, transformative, and restorative practices. Topics will include problems of scale and methods for scaling the role of neutral parties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Dispute Resolution Systems Design
Description: The systemic analysis and design of dispute resolution processes, with a focus on large-scale and complex settings. Participants will survey various approaches to disputes, including facilitative, evaluative, transformative, and restorative practices. Topics will include problems of scale and methods for scaling the role of neutral parties.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Dispute Resolution in the 21st Century
Description: Students explore the modern ADR movement and its applications in law, government, business, community, and other spheres. Surveys the history of dispute resolution, various DR processes, and the work of practitioners who utilize them. Processes covered include mediation, arbitration, facilitation, case evaluation, restorative justice, mini-trials, online dispute resolution, and others.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Dispute Resolution in the 21st Century
Description: Students explore the modern ADR movement and its applications in law, government, business, community, and other spheres. Surveys the history of dispute resolution, various DR processes, and the work of practitioners who utilize them. Processes covered include mediation, arbitration, facilitation, case evaluation, restorative justice, mini-trials, online dispute resolution, and others.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Alternative Dispute Resolution Seminar
Description: Introduces the law and practices of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration through in-class discussions and role-playing exercises that simulate the work of lawyers in these contexts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Alternative Dispute Resolution Seminar
Description: Introduces the law and practices of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration through in-class discussions and role-playing exercises that simulate the work of lawyers in these contexts.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: ADR in the Workplace
Description: Skills and systems for conflict management in the workplace will prepare participants to use dispute resolution skills and design dispute resolution systems within the workplace. Participants will learn how to prevent conflict when appropriate, manage conflict when it arises, and empower stakeholders.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: ADR in the Workplace
Description: Skills and systems for conflict management in the workplace will prepare participants to use dispute resolution skills and design dispute resolution systems within the workplace. Participants will learn how to prevent conflict when appropriate, manage conflict when it arises, and empower stakeholders.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Comparative Labor and Employment Law
Description: Regulation of employment relationship by European Community and by national legal systems outside United States, as compared to United States labor and employment law. This is a writing seminar.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Environmental Law
Description: Introduction to international environmental law and policy, focusing on how international environmental regimes emerge, develop, and influence behavior. Selected case studies on topics such as acid rain, global warming, whaling, deforestation, and trade in endangered species.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Legal Malpractice
Description: The law of malpractice and the context in which it arises with a view to developing a framework for analyzing problems the lawyer faces in order to avoid malpractice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation
Description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation - Service Learning
Description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation Clinic Hours
Description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Corporate Counsel Externship Summer
Description: Exploration of the practice of law from the perspective of an in-house counsel. Covers legal and practical issues typically encountered in an in-house practice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Corporate Counsel Externship Summer - Service Learning
Description: Exploration of the practice of law from the perspective of an in-house counsel. Covers legal and practical issues typically encountered in an in-house practice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Corporate Counsel Externship Summer
Description: Students will work in a legal department under the supervision of an in-house attorney and will gain first-hand knowledge about an in-house practice.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Advanced Copyright
Description: Issues of copyright created by modern communications technology; the historical and constitutional context of copyright and its relevance to the proposed National Information Infrastructure.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Education Law
Description: Examination of a variety of issues affecting educational institutions. Discussion of the constitutional rights afforded students and teachers and exploration of how various federal and state statutes affect the community of learning in schools in the United States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Education Law
Description: Examination of a variety of issues affecting educational institutions. Discussion of the constitutional rights afforded students and teachers and exploration of how various federal and state statutes affect the community of learning in schools in the United States.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Higher Education Law
Description: Examines the constitutional, statutory, administrative, and common-law principles that shape the structure, identity, and character of American public and private colleges and universities, including academic freedom, the rights and responsibilities of students and faculty, issues of identity and access, shared governance, accreditation and regulation.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Mass Torts Seminar
Description: Exploration of the overriding question of whether the courts can dispense individual justice in cases involving thousands of litigants. Course requirements will include writing a substantial research paper as well as actively participating in class discussion.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Western Legal Tradition
Description: Development of law in the western world -- continental Europe, the British Isles, North America and Latin America -- focusing on factors that cause law to change and that determine the nature and shape of the legal change.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Civil Litigation
Description: Globalization has increased frequency of transboundary disputes, whether between companies like Microsoft and Sony or business dealings with sovereigns like China. The next generation of lawyers need to know the law governing personal jurisdiction over foreign companies, forum nonconveniens, discovery in international disputes, forum selection clauses, and foreign judgments.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Law and Institutions of the European Union
Description: History of the European Union, law-making and administrative institutions and processes, economic sectoral policies, including competition and state aids, transport and agriculture; internal market, freedoms (movement of goods, workers, capital, services); harmonization of national laws; external economic trade policy; impact of Single European Act and Treaty on European Union.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Capital Punishment
Description: Legal and social issues surrounding capital punishment. Surveys legal issues in areas of criminal law and procedure, constitutional law and ethics which confront attorneys in capital cases. Encourages students to synthesize social and legal facets to objectively evaluate complex issues involved in capital punishment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Capital Punishment
Description: Legal and social issues surrounding capital punishment. Surveys legal issues in areas of criminal law, and procedure, constitutional law and ethics which confront attorneys in capital cases. Encourages students to synthesize social and legal facets to objectively evaluate complex issues involved in capital punishment.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Document Drafting: Contracts
Description: Provides opportunity to apply legal principles acquired in substantive courses to drafting of non-litigation documents. Provides fundamental skills necessary to draft documents such as contracts and wills. Also focuses on eliciting information from clients to provide factual basis for preparation of such documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Document Drafting: Contracts
Description: Provides opportunity to apply legal principles acquired in substantive courses to drafting of non-litigation documents. Provides fundamental skills necessary to draft documents such as contracts and wills. Also focuses on eliciting information from clients to provide factual basis for preparation of such documents.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: International Finance
Description: Analytical review of regulatory structures and procedures associated with international financial transactions. Special emphasis is given to national and international markets that underlie these transactions. Concept and financial instruments examined include capital adequacy, securitization, privatization, derivatives and swaps.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Environmental Dispute Resolution
Description: Conflict management, anatomy of negotiation, planning and conduct of negotiations, and resolving multiparty environmental disputes.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Anti-Terrorism and Criminal Enforcement
Description: This course will deal with the difficult but important issue of how we protect the American homeland from terrorism in a way that is consistent with the constitution and criminal laws.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Mediation Clinic
Description: Students are required to participate in weekly two-hour classes and to be available at court for mediations for an average of five hours per week.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Mediation Clinic
Description: Students are required to participate in weekly two-hour classes and to be available at court for mediations for an average of five hours per week.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Global Governance
Description: In a globalizing world, the range of issues with cross-border implications only expands, from finance to trade, environment to human rights, food safety to sports. This course in International Law examines how and why different legal regimes have developed to govern these issues and when they succeed or fail.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Telecommunications Law and Policy
Description: Explores the rules and standards of U.S. telecommunications law. We examine market structures and regulatory treatment of a number of related electronic communications technologies—from wireline and wireless telephony to T.V. to the Internet backbone—whose convergence and recombination continue to challenge frameworks first established decades ago.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Global Governance Summer School: Independent Project
Description: During the Global Governance Summer School, students will engage with guest speakers and visit sites of historic and contemporary significance. This course will allow students to deepen their understanding of important issues in global governance and the context in which international legal institutions function. Students will critically reflect on these experiences through reflective papers and group projects.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Global Governance Summer School: Special Topics
Description: Examination of selected topics in global governance. Introduces actors and legal institutions that are involved in addressing issues of transnational or global significance and critically evaluates the role of various actors, legal regimes, and institutions in responding to those issues. The particular focus of the Global Governance Summer School will vary from year to year based on the Supervising Faculty Member’s area of expertise.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: International Law Hackathon
Description: Introduces students to a contemporary challenge in the field of international law and prompts them to design and present a solution as part of a group. Students will learn about the historical context, institutional, legal, and theoretical frameworks, as well as the relevant law and policy frameworks, of the selected hackathon challenge through readings, lectures, recorded interviews, and more. Small groups will present their “hacks” or proposed solutions to a panel of judges at the end of the semester.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Immigration Law
Description: Examination of American immigration law and policy.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Crimmigration
Description: Crimmigration refers to the convergence of the criminal and immigration systems. Students in this course will learn to analyze the constitutional, statutory, and regulatory provisions implicated by noncitizens' interactions with the criminal justice system. They will also develop the foundation to debate the policies that animate crimmigration.

subject: JURI - Jurisprudence
title: Business Immigration Law

Our primary purpose is to better understand the role lawyers have played in shaping social, political, and economic change.

Students will then examine what the criminal justice system can do to prevent wrongful convictions in the future and present a paper detailing a proposed solution to one of the issues discussed. Description: With its roots in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, copyright is an essential part of U.S. Law. This course will explore the fundamentals of U.S. copyright law, from securing protection, to copyright duration, fair use, and the tension between copyright and First Amendment freedom of expression.

subject: KINS - Kinesiology
title: Information Literacy and the Law
Description: Teaches students to research effectively and introduces them to information literacy concepts like verifying news, online resources, and other publications. Civics concepts needed to understand American government and legal documents and how to find those documents for free or at low cost.

subject: KINS - Kinesiology
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.

subject: KINS - Kinesiology
title: Studies in Law in Other Times and Places

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Elementary Korean I
Description: Pronunciation, grammar, particles, basic sentence construction, and sentence patterns. Reading and writing in Hangul, the national writing system. Not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Elementary Korean II
Description: As a continuation of Elementary Korean I, this course focuses on pronunciation, grammar, particles, basic sentence construction, and sentence patterns. Reading and writing in Hangul, the national writing system. This course is not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Intermediate Korean I
Description: Pronunciation, grammar, particles, sentence construction, and sentence patterns. Declarative, interrogative, propositive, and imperative speech styles. Reading and writing in Hangul, the national writing system. This course is not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Intermediate Korean II
Description: As a continuation of Intermediate Korean I, this course focuses on pronunciation, grammar, particles, sentence construction, and sentence patterns. Declarative, interrogative, propositive, and imperative speech styles. Reading and writing in Hangul, the national writing system. This course is not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Enhanced Intermediate Korean I
Description: Enhanced course with comprehensive grammar review; readings of intermediate texts; composition, conversation, and presentation. Not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean

Description: A continuation of Enhanced Intermediate Korean I, with comprehensive grammar review; readings of intermediate texts; composition, conversation, and presentation. Not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Advanced Korean I
Description: This course focuses on building an advanced-level vocabulary and grammar knowledge in Korean for a variety of verbal and written communications. This course is not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Advanced Korean II
Description: As a continuation of Advanced Korean I, this course focuses on building an advanced-level vocabulary and grammar knowledge in Korean for a variety of verbal and written communications. This course is not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Enhanced Advanced Korean I
Description: Enhanced course with comprehensive grammar review; readings of advanced texts; composition, conversation, and presentation. Not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Enhanced Advanced Korean II
Description: A continuation of Enhanced Advanced Korean I, with comprehensive grammar review; readings of advanced texts; composition, conversation, and presentation. Not open to native speakers.

subject: KREN - Korean
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Directed Study in Korean Language, Literature, and Culture
Description: The student undertakes an in-depth study of Korean language, literature, and culture in consultation with a faculty member.

subject: KREN - Korean
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Internship in Korea
Description: Students will intern at a secondary school or university in Korea. They will teach conversational English in class or through extracurricular activities at a host school. Students will also learn spoken Korean by engaging in various activities with Korean students on and off campus.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Business Korean
Description: Students will be able to speak, comprehend, read, and write business Korean and will also be able to understand Korean business culture through classroom activities, field trips, and homework assignments based on authentic material.

subject: KREN - Korean
title: Business Korean II
Description: A continuation of Business Korean.

subject: KREN - Korean
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Special Topics in Korean Film
Description: Students will enhance their understanding and knowledge of Korean society, culture, and history by studying fictional and documentary films from Korea. Representative topics examined in this class include colonialism, post-colonialism, war, the national division, family, women’s lives, shamanism, Confucianism, Buddhism, modernization, and the impact of Globalization.

subject: KREN - Korean
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Modern Korean Fiction
Description: Survey of representative works of fiction in modern Korean literature. Western-style novels, emerging in the early twentieth century, have served as main vehicles for chronicling dramatic changes in Korean society. Students will study the development of this novelistic genre from aesthetic, historical, socio-cultural, and comparative perspectives.
