subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Introduction to Latin America and the Caribbean
Description: The interdisciplinary study of Latin America and the Caribbean. Examination of ethnic and cultural diversity and issues of gender, race, class, and culture within Latin American and Caribbean society. Consideration will also be given to the historical, political, economic, geographic, and social experiences of Latin American and Caribbean ethnic and cultural groups with special attention to their diversity and unity.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Introduction to Latin America and the Caribbean (Honors)
Description: The interdisciplinary study of Latin America and the Caribbean, with a focus on student-directed learning. Examination of ethnic and cultural diversity and issues of gender, race, class, and culture within Latin American and Caribbean society. Consideration will also be given to the historical, political, economic, geographic, and social experiences of Latin American and Caribbean ethnic and cultural groups, with special attention to their diversity and unity.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Introduction to Latin America and the Caribbean
Description: The interdisciplinary study of Latin America and the Caribbean. Examination of ethnic and cultural diversity and issues of gender, race, class, and culture within Latin American and Caribbean society. Consideration will also be given to the historical, political, economic, geographic, and social experiences of Latin American and Caribbean ethnic and cultural groups with special attention to their diversity and unity.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Introduction to Latin American and Caribbean Studies II
Description: This continuation of Introduction to Latin American and Caribbean Studies I serves as a basic introduction to Latin American and Caribbean Studies. Faculty from various disciplines deliver weekly lectures introducing students to issues related to the cultures, languages, ecology, geography, history, linguistics, political science, and the societies of Latin America and the Caribbean. Advanced readings and discussions following the weekly lectures.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Latino/a Studies
Description: Multidisciplinary study of the history, culture, and politics of Latino/as in the United States. Topics include, but are not limited to, barrio life, precarious labor, border policing, citizenship, exile, Latinidad, stereotypes, the American Dream, and empowerment.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Caribbean Studies
Description: Multidisciplinary study of the history, culture, and politics of the Caribbean and its diaspora in the U.S. Topics include, but are not limited to, colonialism and slavery, revolution and empowerment, color and caste, gender and sexuality, Afro- Caribbean religions and music, national identity, and the tourist economy.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Brazilian Studies
Description: Introduction to the real Brazil today, focusing on key issues of contemporary relevance. Rather than emphasizing Brazil’s problems, it explores the innovative ways Brazilians are solving them.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Brazilian Studies
Description: Introduction to the real Brazil today, focusing on key issues of contemporary relevance. Rather than emphasizing Brazil’s problems, it explores the innovative ways Brazilians are solving them.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Mexican Studies: A Transnational Perspective
Description: Multidisciplinary study of the history, culture, and politics of Mexico. Though the focus is on understanding Mexico, the course incorporates a transnational perspective through an appreciation of the politics and effects of globalization and Mexico-U.S. relations. Materials include scholarly texts and traditional and new media.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Multidisciplinary Mexican Studies: A Transnational Perspective
Description: Multidisciplinary study of the history, culture, and politics of Mexico. Though the focus is on understanding Mexico, the course incorporates a transnational perspective through an appreciation of the politics and effects of globalization and Mexico-U.S. relations. Materials include scholarly texts and traditional and new media.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Indigenous Peoples in the Americas
Description: An overview of the histories, struggles, and current conditions of indigenous peoples in the Americas from pre-Columbian times to the present. Emphasis on the political, technological, and social organization and achievements of indigenous cultures and struggles over territories, rights, and resources during the Colonial period and after.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American Civilization to 1800
Description: Amerindian, Iberoamerican, and Caribbean history and culture from pre-encounter times to 1800.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American Civilization Since 1800
Description: Latin American and Caribbean history and culture from 1800 to the present.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: The Other Americans: U.S. Hispanic/Latinx History from 1565 to the Present
Description: A survey of the history of the Hispanic/Latinx people of the United States from the Spanish conquest to the present, examining the U.S. occupation of the Southwest and the successive waves of Hispanic immigration through issues of segregation, integration, gender equality, and identity formation.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: The Other Americans: U.S. Hispanic/Latinx History from 1565 to the Present (Honors)
Description: A survey of the history of the Hispanic/Latinx people of the United States from the Spanish conquest to the present, examining the U.S. occupation of the Southwest and the successive waves of Hispanic immigration through issues of segregation, integration, gender equality, and identity formation.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Race and Slavery in the Americas
Description: Examination of the history of race and slavery in the Americas from the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries. We analyze the enslaved experience, with an emphasis on outlining similarities and differences among slavery in North American, Caribbean, and Latin American societies, and how slavery influenced post- abolition racial inequalities.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Women, Gender, and Sexuality in Latin America
Description: Examination of the history of women, gender relations, and sexuality in Latin America. It pays particular attention to how gender, race, and class intersected in the formation of historical trends from pre-Colombian societies to the present day. Approximately one-half of the course will focus on pre-1800 society.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: History of Mexico
Description: Mexican history and culture from pre-Columbian times to the present.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: History of Mexico (Honors)
Description: Mexican history from pre-Aztec times to the modern era. Pre- Columbian Mexico, the era of Spain's colonial rule (1519-1810), the struggle for independence, and the turbulent years of post- independence chaos will be covered. Also, the Juárez years (1855-1872), the long reign of Porfírio Díaz, and the epic Mexican Revolution, its effects and aftermath leading up to the present day.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: History of Brazil
Description: Brazilian history and culture from pre-Columbian times to the present.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: History of Brazil
Description: Brazilian history and culture from pre-Columbian times to the present. How Brazil and its people have been shaped by colonialism, economic cycles of boom and bust, slavery, regional cleavages, shifts from monarchical to republican to dictatorial to democratic forms of government, and incomplete attempts to expand access to prosperity and political power.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Andean History: From Inka Empire to Plurinational State
Description: Exploration of the central nodes of Andean history: the foundation of the Inka empire, the Spanish Conquest, process of modern state formation and the indigenous rights movement in Ecuador, Bolivia, and Perú, analyzing how the Andean village adapted to outside exactions and demands without betraying its defining character.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latinx Literature
Description: A survey of Latinx literature and key topics in Latinx literary studies. Students will explore how Latino/as have imaginatively dramatized issues such as barrio life, exilic nostalgia, internal colonialism, historic traumas, border crossings, Spanglish, mestizaje, machismo, and new notions of the American Dream.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: New World Archaeology
Description: Cultural variation in the Americas from the end of the Pleistocene to the time of intensive European contact, with emphasis on human/environmental interactions.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American Ethnobotanical Garden Internship
Description: Field-based course held at the Latin American and Caribbean Studies Institute (LACSI) Latin American Ethnobotanical Garden (LAEG) on UGA’s north campus. Students will carry out garden and/or greenhouse work under the supervision of the garden’s part-time curator and work on occasion with garden volunteers.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Women in the Caribbean
Description: This course covers a range of issues affecting women in the various parts of the Caribbean region. It examines the meaning of feminism within the Caribbean context. It considers the ways in which race, gender, class, ethnicity, language, sexuality, and other factors affect the formation of Caribbean women's identities in the modern world.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Women in the Caribbean
Description: Examination of the meaning of feminism within the Caribbean context. The ways in which race, gender, class, ethnicity, language, sexuality, and other factors affect the formation of Caribbean women's identities in the modern world.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Pandemic! Infectious Disease in Global History
Description: Centers the lived experiences of different individuals and cultures during infectious disease epidemics in modern global history, particularly in Latin America, Africa, and Asia. Based on the history of medicine, the course emphasizes both historical context and anthropological, epidemiological, sociological, and cultural issues surrounding infectious disease both past and present.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Reflections on Fighting Hunger
Description: Exploration of world hunger using an interdisciplinary approach. Analysis of natural resource-related, political, and cultural causes of hunger; its health and socioeconomic effects; and current proposed solutions, with an emphasis on education. Group discussions will be emphasized in this course.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Reflections on Fighting Hunger
Description: Exploration of world hunger using an interdisciplinary approach. Analysis of natural resource-related, political, and cultural causes of hunger; its health and socioeconomic effects; and current proposed solutions, with an emphasis on education. Group discussions will be emphasized in this course.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Latin American Indigenous Languages I
Description: Students will study a less-commonly taught Latin American indigenous language either in the country of origin or at UGA. The course will focus on developing students' cultural and linguistic knowledge of the target language.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Latin American Indigenous Languages II
Description: Students will continue studing a less-commonly taught Latin American indigenous language either in the country of origin or at UGA. The course will focus on developing students' cultural and linguistic knowledge of the target language.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Topics in Cinema, Culture, and Literature in the Portuguese-Speaking World
Description: Specific aspects of cinema, culture, and literature of the Portuguese-speaking world. Topics to be selected according to the needs and interests of the students. Taught in seminar fashion with extensive outside readings of primary and secondary sources. Given in English.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Current Topics in Latin American Research
Description: Topics of current interest in Latin American Studies based on individual study, readings, or projects under the supervision of a project director. Students will develop a paper or project based upon a specific aspect of the region.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Social Policy Storytelling: In and Around Athens
Description: Examination of local and national politics through the lived experience of local Athens area residents, social policymaking processes, and the role of research and storytelling for policy. Students will conduct fieldwork and create policy-relevant digital stories. Students will present their findings to community stakeholders in the Athens area.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Practicum in Service Learning
Description: Practical use of language skills and cultural awareness through community involvement. Students will work directly with approved study abroad providers or the Latino community of Athens in planned and systematic activities coordinated with a variety of community organizations. Each student will organize, manage, and track his/her community service.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Practicum in Latin American and Caribbean Studies
Description: Practical use of sociopolitical, geographical, and cultural knowledge of Latin America will be put to use through community involvement or with a locally relevant LACSI project. Students will work on planned and systematic activities coordinated by the instructor of record.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Citizenship and Social Movements in Latin America and the Caribbean
Description: An overview of contemporary social movements of the region, its historical roots, and the economic/political causes that motivate the protests of the powerless. Special attention will be given to the relationship between social movements, political parties, and the state in different historical moments and countries.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Topics in Spanish-American Studies
Description: Designed for students who participate in UGA Study Abroad programs. Students will attend a class in Spanish offered by the host university. Given in Spanish.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Francophone Film, Literature, and Culture
Description: Introduction to various Francophone regions of the world through the study of film and literature.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Studies in Latin American History
Description: Special issues or topics in Latin American history not covered in a regular history course. Topics, methodology, and instructor vary from semester to semester. Representative topics include the Latin American revolutionary tradition, the wars of independence in the Americas, and Latin American wars.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Environmental Justice in Latin America and the Caribbean
Description: An introduction to environmental issues in Latin America and the Caribbean, with an emphasis on how capitalist expansion, patriarchal structures, and white supremacist ideologies are linked to environmental degradation. We will review theories on environmental issues and apply them to the analysis of environmental problems in specific ecosystems.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Mexican Civilization: Cultural Identity of Mexican People
Description: Examination of ethnic and cultural diversity, and issues of gender, race, class, and culture within Mexican society. Consideration will also be given to the historical, political, economic, and social experiences of Mexican ethnic and cultural groups with special attention to their diversity and unity.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Mexican Civilization: Cultural Identity of Mexican People (Spanish)
Description: Examination of ethnic and cultural diversity and issues of gender, race, class, and culture within Mexican society. Consideration will also be given to the historical, political, economic, and social experiences of Mexican ethnic and cultural groups, with special attention to their diversity and unity. Designed to offer students the opportunity to develop further their skills in the Spanish language. Students in this course will receive some course material in Spanish.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Supernatural Latin America: Readings on Witchcraft, Shamanism, and Popular Religion
Description: Exploration of the history of popular religions in Latin America since Pre-Columbian times. Readings include issues such as religion in the Andes, witchcraft and cult of the saints, African religions in Brazil, and shamanism in the Amazon. Analysis of the social, political, and gender dimensions of the religious experience.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Citizenship and Social Movements in Latin America and the Caribbean
Description: Examination of struggles surrounding assertions of citizenship rights in Latin America and the Caribbean since the eighteenth century. The readings trace moments in which women, migrants, and indigenous and colonized peoples transformed dominant understandings of the nation-state and political agency.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Race, Nation, and Popular Culture in Latin America
Description: Exploration of how Latin Americans see themselves through the lens of popular culture. Studying festivals, dances, theater, and a variety of forms of public performance serves the purpose of reflecting on the specific way Latin Americans have constructed race, gender, class, and nation. In addition, the course pursues the goal of introducing the students to different concepts and methodologies developed in the humanities and social sciences and applying them to specific Latin American cases.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: The Black and Green Atlantic: Crosscurrents of the African and Irish Diasporas
Description: An exploration of the comparative dimensions of Black and Irish experiences in the Atlantic world through the study of cultural production from the United States, Africa, Britain, the Caribbean, and Ireland. Special emphasis will be placed on the relevance of the texts under discussion to contemporary society around the world.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Inter-American Relations
Description: Introduction to and analysis of changes in Latin American and United States foreign policy.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Global Perspectives on Gender
Description: The diverse social and cultural manifestations of gender located within an economic, social, and political context. Case studies drawn from Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and the Caribbean.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Global Perspectives on Gender
Description: The diverse social and cultural manifestations of gender located within an economic, social, and political context. Case studies drawn from Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and the Caribbean.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Sociology of Latin America
Description: Exploration of the social history and contemporary questions of race, class, gender, and nation in Latin America. Case studies drawn from throughout the region. Topics may include socioeconomic development, poverty and inequality, social movements, institutions, and change. Latin America in transnational context.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Critical Concepts in Latin American and Caribbean Studies
Description: Covers a range of theories and perspectives instrumental to Latin American and Caribbean Studies across disciplines and over time. Examples include dependency theory, liberation theology, subaltern studies, the decolonial turn, indigenous epistemologies, and Latin American feminisms. Concepts addressed may include colonialism, imperialism, coloniality, criollismo, indigenismo, mestizaje, hybridity, testimonio, and lo popular.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Comparative Democracy, Democratization, and Civil Society
Description: Democracy and democratization focused on the political, cultural, and socioeconomic bases of democratization, its practice in the United States, Europe, Russia, Eastern Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and/or Latin America and the prospects for democracy spreading in presently non-democratic countries. Emphasis on the distinct meanings of democracy, its variety of forms, and the distinct priorities that different societies give to democracy.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American Politics
Description: The factors leading to democratic transitions in the region and the problems associated with the consolidation of democratic rule.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: The Aztecs and the Maya
Description: Two indigenous urban societies of the Americas, from farming village beginnings to the Spanish conquest, and their lasting impact on modern middle American culture. Topics include ecology, economy, political organization, urbanism, militarism, beliefs, art, architecture, and literature.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Archaeology of the Caribbean
Description: This history of archaeology in the Caribbean islands focuses on theories of migration, settlement patterns, subsistence strategies, and emergence of complex polities encountered by the first Europeans. The Caribbean region will be compared to adjacent areas along the Gulf Coast to explore the roots and limits of Caribbean traditions.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American and Caribbean Theatre and Performance
Description: Theatre and performance from several Latin American and Caribbean countries. Study of the history of theatre and performance in the region and a selection of plays by some of the best artists. Emphasis will be placed on theatre’s cultural influences and its sociopolitical role.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latina Studies
Description: The study of Latina lives from a feminist perspective. Examination of research and writing about the lives of Latina women with a particular focus on the dynamics of communities in the United States, immigration, cultural values regarding gender, and effects of poverty and violence.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Comparative Postcolonial Studies
Description: Embracing a comparative approach that begins by excavating the foundations of post colonial theory, this course analyzes cultural production emanating from or relating to three distinct geographic areas: Latin America and the Caribbean, Africa, and Asia. The course will explore the changing nature of the relationship between the periphery and the core of an increasingly globalized economy.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: African Religion in Diaspora
Description: Diasporic movement, sustainability, modifications, syncretic tendencies of African Derived Religions in the Americas, especially Brazil, Cuba, Haiti, and North America.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American Film and Media
Description: A historical survey of cinema and related audio(visual) media, including radio, television, and digital media, in Latin America. The course traces the role played by cinema and media in nation-building in Latin American countries as well as the relationship between film aesthetics, politics, and globalization.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Latin American Film and Media
Description: A historical survey of cinema and related audio(visual) media, including radio, television, and digital media, in Latin America. The course traces the role played by cinema and media in nation-building in Latin American countries as well as the relationship between film aesthetics, politics, and globalization.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: U.S. Latino/a Mental Health: An Introduction
Description: An overview of Latino/a mental health issues in the United States from the perspective of well-being, cultural strengths, and empowerment. Students will examine the strengths and resiliency of U.S. Latinos/as and critically examine structural and societal barriers in the U.S. that result in stress and mental illness in this population.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Special Topics in Latin American and Caribbean Transnational Comparative Studies
Description: Focuses on two or more Latin American and/or Caribbean countries (e.g., Peru and Bolivia) or at least one Latin American county and another country outside of Latin America (e.g., Brazil and Angola). The approach could be discipline- specific (e.g., literature) or interdisciplinary (e.g., anthropology and linguistics).

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: International Agricultural Development
Description: Analysis of international development programs, stressing the developing world's perspective. Study of issues affecting international cooperation, agricultural development and sustainability, technology transfer, and extension education.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: International Agricultural Development
Description: Analysis of international development programs, stressing the developing world's perspective. Study of issues affecting international cooperation, agricultural development and sustainability, technology transfer, and extension education.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Geography of Latin America
Description: The geography of Latin America, including physical, cultural, and economic characteristics of different regions. Prospects for expansion of settlement, development of resources, and growth of industries.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American and Caribbean Studies Internship
Description: Students are permitted to enter an organization to obtain practical and applied experience. Work is conducted in a Latin American or Caribbean language. A scholarly research paper relating this experience to academic work is required.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Special Topics in Latin American and Caribbean Studies
Description: Current topics in Latin America and/or the Caribbean.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Latin American and Caribbean Studies Senior Capstone Seminar
Description: To enhance the knowledge gained and deepen the appreciation of Latin American and Caribbean Studies. Students will demonstrate proficiency in the major regional language of choice.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Telenovelas, Culture, and Society
Description: Examination of the connections between media, culture, and society as participants study the world's most watched television genre: the Latin American telenovela. The class focuses on the genre's contexts of production, consumption, regulation, and globalization, and analyzes telenovelas as a public forum for the negotiation of sociocultural issues.

subject: LACS - Latin American and Caribbean Studies
title: Issues in Latino Education
Description: An overview of important patterns and issues in education relating to Hispanic/Latino students K-12 and post-secondary, statewide and nationally. Includes history, cultural context, policy issues and trends, challenges faced by Latinos in school, implications for practice, and current research.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Studying for Success
Description: An introduction to three learning strategies proven to enhance long-term retention of new material. Rather than relying on techniques that promote short-term memorization of facts for exams and result in little to no retention afterwards, students will complete three modules, each of which focuses on a proven study strategy. Students will have opportunities to practice each strategy within the course and will receive advice about how best to use them going forward.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Preparing for Healthcare
Description: Introduces concepts students will encounter in prerequisite courses for medical, physician assistant, dental, or veterinary school. Illustrations, animations, and interactive models will reinforce the role each concept plays in a disease encountered in healthcare, thereby allowing students to see the impact of these concepts on their chosen profession.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Foundations of Clinical Medicine I
Description: This course is designed like Foundations of Clinical Medicine II and Foundations of Clinical Medicine III, neither of which is required to take this course. Students will complete three modules that address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Foundations of Clinical Medicine II
Description: This course is designed like Foundations of Clinical Medicine I and Foundations of Clinical Medicine III, neither of which is required to take this course. Students will complete three modules that address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Foundations of Clinical Medicine III
Description: This course is designed like Foundations of Clinical Medicine I and Foundations of Clinical Medicine II, neither of which is required to take this course. Students will complete three modules that address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.6 hours credit.
title: Physical Diagnosis
Description: Veterinary clinical diagnostic procedures. Techniques and procedures necessary to perform physical diagnosis on the animal are practiced in the clinic on normal and abnormal animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Large Animal Infectious Diseases
Description: A review of the principles of infectious diseases of large animals, the mechanisms by which microorganisms infect and cause disease, how the immune response contributes to disease, the principles of infectious disease epidemiology, and how antimicrobials and vaccines can be used rationally to control these diseases.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Advanced Clinical Dermatology
Description: Practical application of the course material/knowledge base acquired in the Dermatology core course. The course is based on problem/symptom-oriented, case-based discussions.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.1 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.2 hours credit.
title: Principles of Anesthesia
Description: Principles and application of anesthesia to large and small animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. 1 hours lecture and 1 hours lab per week.
title: Comparative Clinical Dermatology
Description: Basic morphologic reactions of skin to disease processes, diagnostic techniques, important skin diseases in small and large animals, and current therapy.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit. 1 hours lecture and 1 hours lab per week.
title: Equine Dentistry
Description: An introduction to equine dentistry. Topics to be covered include: instrumentation, sedation, handling, floating with hand and power tools. Extraction of deciduous and permanent teeth via intraoral extraction and various surgical techniques. The labs will involve both cadaver skulls and live horses.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Large Animal Advanced Anesthesia
Description: Lectures, case-based discussions, and one two-hour laboratory covering anesthesia of large animals, including the impact of anatomic and physiologic features, selection of anesthetic drugs and techniques, modification of equipment for large animals, considerations of specific diseases, and recognition and treatment of common anesthetic complications.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.6 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Medicine I: Urology, Hematology, Endocrinology
Description: Medical aspects of the urinary tract, hematology, and endocrinology of large domestic animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Problems in Large Animal Medicine
Description: A problem-based course using cases submitted to the DDI service. Students (in a small group of 3-4 along with a facilitator) will develop their learning objectives, and using the resources of the CVM, accomplish their learning objectives and provide a solution to the questions posed by practitioners.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinical Techniques in Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
Description: Introduction to procedures commonly performed during diagnosis and treatment of large animal cases. The course consists of lectures describing the procedures and their clinical use and interactive case discussions illustrating the application of these concepts.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinical Techniques in Large Animal Medicine and Surgery Laboratory
Description: An introduction to procedures commonly performed during diagnosis and treatment of large animal cases. The course is the laboratory companion to Clinical Techniques in Large Animal Medicine and Surgery, and laboratories will be timed to demonstrate the techniques described during lectures.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 2 hours. 16 hours lecture and 14 hours lab per week.
title: Principles of Surgery and General Surgery Practicum
Description: Application of surgical and anesthetic techniques to domestic animals. Principles of surgical asepsis, wound healing, and instrument handling.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Veterinary Obstetrics
Description: Pregnancy and its abnormalities. Parturition, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of dystocia in cow, mare, ewe/doe, sow, dog, and cat. Cesarean section and fetotomy. Postparturient problems.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Ruminant Internal Medicine: Respiratory Diseases
Description: Pathophysiology, etiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cardiopulmonary diseases of ruminants will be covered.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.4 hours credit.
title: Neurology
Description: This course will provide a systematic approach to localizing a lesion in the nervous system. While the main emphasis will be understanding and identifying lesion location, common diseases of both small and large animals will be discussed.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Theriogenology Selective
Description: This is a comprehensive course that encompasses the didactic aspects of large animal theriogenology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Equine Respiratory Diseases
Description: The study of etiology, pathophysiology, clinical signs, diagnosis, therapy, and prevention of common equine respiratory diseases and cardiac diseases.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Neurology
Description: The etiology, pathophysiology, clinical signs and localization, diagnosis, therapy, and prevention of large animal neurologic diseases will be covered.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 3.2 hours credit.
title: Equine Clinical Diagnostic Imaging
Description: Radiographic and ultrasonographic imaging of osseous and soft tissue disorders of the musculoskeletal, abdominal, and thoracic systems.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 3.5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7 hours credit.
title: Veterinary Radiology
Description: This course is a study of the fundamentals of x-ray production, the production of quality radiographs, radiobiology, normal radiographic anatomy, and interpretation paradigms. The normal and diseased appearances of large and small animals will be discussed. Fundamentals of advanced diagnostic imaging will be presented.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Large Animal Cardiology
Description: Review and discussion of clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment of the most common cardiac diseases of large animals. Lectures will review "core" cardiology, sound recordings and ECG used to simulate normal and abnormal cardiac findings, and consist of audience participation (keypad interaction) case presentations.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.6 hours credit.
title: Respiratory Diseases
Description: The diagnosis and treatment of respiratory diseases in horses, food animals, and small animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Large Animal Digestive Diseases
Description: The diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of diseases of the equine and food animal digestive systems.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Digestive Diseases
Description: Continuation of the material presented in the Digestive Diseases of Large Animals core course. Focus is on the presenting complaint of equine abdominal pain. The material presented is suitable for students interested in a mixed animal, equine, or large animal exclusive track.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Lameness and the Foot
Description: Significant lameness as a clinical problem, identification of the lame limb, and diagnostic techniques used to identify the cause. The equine foot is discussed in terms of its form and function in relation to disease with emphasis on relating the symptoms, diagnosis and treatment to basic principles. Individual diseases and cases are discussed.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Cardiology
Description: Fundamentals of the cardiac evaluation, diagnostic testing, pathophysiology of CHF, recognition of common cardiac disorders, and clinical pharmacology of heart diseases. Emphasis is on auscultation and treatment of cardiomyopathies and valvular disease.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Musculoskeletal Diseases
Description: Fundamental information about musculoskeletal pathophysiology focusing on bone, joint, and tendon/ligament biology. The course will form the basis for future species specific elective courses.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-7.8 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Emergency Medicine and Surgery
Description: Clinical rotation in large animal emergency medicine and surgery. Students will participate in the admission, work-up, and treatment of large animal emergencies after hours. Additionally, participants will help with treatments on critical patients in the hospital and take part in topic and case-based rounds.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 2.6 hours credit.
title: Small Animal Basic Surgical Techniques
Description: Anesthetic and surgical techniques as applied to small animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Surgery I: Musculoskeletal
Description: Diseases of the musculoskeletal system in which surgery may be a treatment. Emphasis on diagnostic techniques, surgical decision making, surgical techniques, and postoperative care. This course emphasizes orthopedic problems.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Surgery II: Soft Tissue Surgery
Description: Diseases of the digestive, respiratory, integumental, and reproductive systems in which surgery may be a treatment. Emphasis on diagnostic techniques, surgical decision making, surgical techniques, and postoperative care.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Large Animal Advanced Surgical Techniques
Description: Advanced surgical techniques to equine and production animals.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Bovine Surgery
Description: The course discusses diseases of the digestive, musculoskeletal, reproductive systems in which surgery may be a treatment. Emphasis is placed on diagnostic techniques, surgical decision making, surgical techniques, and post-operative care.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Artificial Insemination, Embryo Transfer, and Advanced Reproductive Technologies
Description: A combination of lectures and labs will introduce students to Artificial Insemination (AI), Embryo Transfer (ET) in large animals, and other Advanced Reproductive Aechnologies (ART). Students will perform AI and actively participate in the practical management and performance of an ET program.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit. 2.6-7.8 hours lab per week.
title: Large Animal Advanced Clinical Anesthesia
Description: Clinical training in large animal anesthesiology. Students will examine, evaluate, and provide anesthesia and analgesia for clinical patients in the large animal hospital. Practical skills and knowledge of problem-solving techniques will be emphasized.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 15.6 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Internal Medicine
Description: A three-week clinical rotation in the large animal internal medicine of horses, ruminants, and pigs.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 15.6 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Surgery
Description: Clinical training in general large animal surgery with emphasis on equine soft tissue, musculoskeletal, soft tissue disease, food animal lameness, alimentary surgery, diagnosis and pathophysiology of disease.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Farm Practice
Description: Clinical training in farm animal medicine. Pathophysiological mechanisms of disease in the individual animal. Examination, evaluation, and treatment of domesticated animals in the farm environment.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinical Focus on Small Ruminants and Camelids
Description: Provides students the opportunity to experience and discuss management issues and diseases of small ruminants and camelids and to perform common procedures on these species.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Advanced Farm Animal Husbandry and Clinical Medicine
Description: Clinical training in farm animal medicine. Pathophysiological mechanisms of disease in the individual animal. Examination, evaluation, and treatment of domesticated animals in the farm environment. Medical and surgical principles of Farm Practice will be studied and practiced. Students will be exposed to farm/exotic animals and honey bees in a clinical situation which has inherent dangers.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: General Theriogenology
Description: The didactic and clinical aspects of animal reproduction in bovine, canine, equine, and other species. Content includes the management of normal and abnormal reproductive cases and assigned reviews for clinical rounds.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Small Animal Theriogenology
Description: This is a comprehensive clinical rotation that encompasses the didactic and clinical aspects of small animal theriogenology. Emphasis is on the practical implementation of the specialty. The course is only available to fourth-year students.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: Clinical Radiology
Description: The production and recognition of diagnostic quality radiographs of both small and large animals as well as radiographic interpretation.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 3.9-7.8 hours. Repeatable for maximum 15.6 hours credit.
title: Advanced Equine Theriogenology
Description: A comprehensive course encompassing the didactic and clinical aspects of equine theriogenology. The emphasis is on practical implementation of the specialty. The course is only available to fourth year students during the equine breeding season.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Emergency and Critical Care
Description: Clinical rotation in large animal emergency medicine and surgery. Students will participate in the admission, work-up, and treatment of large animal emergencies after hours. Additionally, participants will help with treatments on critical patients in the hospital and take part in topic and case based rounds.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 5.2 hours credit.
title: Equine Diagnostic Imaging and Lameness
Description: The object of this course is to provide students with an in-depth understanding of equine lameness, and the diagnostic imaging techniques used and their interpretation.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Clinical Nutrition
Description: Discussion of equine nutrition concepts and journal articles regarding equine nutrition.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1.3-3.9 hours. Repeatable for maximum 7.8 hours credit.
title: Equine Ophthalmology
Description: Provides students with a strong foundation in equine ophthalmology by providing in-depth experience performing equine ophthalmic examinations, common medical and surgical procedures, and diagnosing and treating common diseases affecting the equine eye.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Equine Sports Medicine, Rehabilitation, and Podiatry
Description: Clinical rotation in equine sports medicine and podiatry. Students will predominantly see cases related to equine sports medicine and podiatry. Assigned responsibilities include case involvement, record keeping, and primary case care for patients hospitalized through the service (may include weekend treatments). This rotation is appropriate for students pursuing equine practice.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-4 hours. Repeatable for maximum 40 hours credit.
title: Seminar in Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
Description: Seminar is presented by the student under the direction of a faculty member. The seminar can consist of a literature review or a review of clinical cases. After the presentation, the group asks questions of the student, who then leads the discussion.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 0.7-8 hours. Repeatable for maximum 20 hours credit.
title: Studies in Clinical Large Animal Medicine
Description: Studies involving different areas of large animal medicine, surgery, population medicine, or theriogenology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinically-Based Concepts I
Description: This is the first of a series of three courses that are designed to achieve two goals. First, to apply foundational basic science concepts from cell biology, chemistry, anatomy, and physiology in a clinical context to better prepare students for careers in healthcare. In addition, this course will introduce strategies for studying and learning that have been proven to reinforce long-term recall. Students will complete three modules, two of which will address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions. The third module will describe the neuroanatomy behind memory and learning techniques that target and strengthen these pathways and provide the students opportunities to use these techniques during the course.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinically-Based Concepts II
Description: This is the second of a series of three courses that are designed to achieve two goals. First, to apply foundational basic science concepts from cell biology, chemistry, anatomy, and physiology in a clinical context to better prepare students for careers in healthcare. In addition, this course will introduce strategies for studying and learning that have been proven to reinforce long-term recall. Students will complete three modules, two of which will address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions. The third module will introduce the students to specific strategies proven to enhance long-term learning and mastery of the learned concepts.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
title: Clinically-Based Concepts III
Description: This is the third of a series of three courses that are designed to achieve two goals. First, to apply foundational basic science concepts from cell biology, chemistry, anatomy, and physiology in a clinical context to better prepare students for careers in healthcare. In addition, this course will introduce strategies for studying and learning that have been proven to reinforce long-term recall. Students will complete three modules, two of which will address biomedical concepts encountered by healthcare professionals. These modules will be presented in a clinical context and will use four learning modalities to address them: reading text, viewing animations and illustrations, watching videos, and answering questions. The third module will introduce the students to specific strategies proven to enhance long-term learning and mastery of the learned concepts.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 45 hours credit.
title: Graduate Student Seminar
Description: Advanced supervised experience in an applied setting. This course may not be used to satisfy a student's approved program of study.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 5-17 hours. Repeatable for maximum 68 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Internship
Description: Clinical training for the graduate veterinarian desiring in-depth knowledge and skills relative to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases affecting food animals and horses.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 5-18 hours. Repeatable for maximum 51 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Residency I
Description: This course provides clinical training during year one of a residency for graduate veterinarians desiring to specialize in large animal medicine, surgery, theriogenology, or anesthesiology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 5-18 hours. Repeatable for maximum 51 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Residency II
Description: This course provides clinical training during year two of a residency for graduate veterinarians in large animal medicine, surgery, theriogenology, or anesthesiology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 5-18 hours. Repeatable for maximum 51 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Residency III
Description: This course provides clinical training during year three of a residency for graduate veterinarians in large animal medicine, surgery, theriogenology, or anesthesiology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 5-18 hours. Repeatable for maximum 60 hours credit.
title: Large Animal Residency IV
Description: This course provides clinical training for graduate veterinarians in the fourth year of a large animal residency in animal medicine, surgery, theriogenology, or anesthesiology.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-5 hours. Repeatable for maximum 10 hours credit.
title: Problems in Large Animal Pathophysiology
Description: Designed to allow graduate students the opportunity to explore, under supervision, problems pertaining to the pathophysiology of large animals. These may be, but are not limited to, the areas of large animal surgery and medicine. Open to graduate students in the biological sciences meeting the course prerequisites.

subject: LAMS - Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
credits: 1-12 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Instructional Challenges in Large Animal Medicine and Surgery
Description: Designed to provide opportunities for students in the Comparative Medical Illustration Certificate Program to explore, under faculty supervision, challenges that occur in the use of scientific visualizations to instruct veterinary students about conditions that occur in large animal species. Open to graduate students in the Comparative Medical Illustration Certificate Program.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Design and the Environment
Description: The built environment and its effects on natural systems. Focus is on the design of the built environment as an ongoing activity integrating ecological, social, and cultural values. Topics include land use patterns and policies, development and resource management, community design issues, and strategies for improving environmental integrity and quality of life.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Design and the Environment
Description: The built environment and its effects on natural systems. Focus is on the design of the built environment as an ongoing activity integrating ecological, social, and cultural values. Topics include land use patterns and policies, development and resource management, community design issues, and strategies for improving environmental integrity and quality of life.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Reading the Landscape
Description: Approaches to perceiving and interpreting the landscape. Topics include the landscape in art and literature, visual assessment techniques, use of maps, field sketching, and photography.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio I
Description: The elements, principles, and processes of visual design as a foundation for landscape architecture. Emphasis is on the development of creativity and design skills through the application of theory and techniques in a series of two- and three-dimensional design projects.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio II
Description: A continuation of Landscape Architecture Design Studio I, with continued emphasis on the development of creativity and design skills through the application of theory and techniques in a series of two- and three-dimensional design projects. Further exploration of the design process.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Design Communication I
Description: Manual drafting and design drawing skills with an emphasis on the development of basic drafting convention and graphic presentation literacy.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Design Communication II
Description: A continuation of Design Communication I, with emphasis on computerized drafting skills and basic understanding of computer- aided graphic presentation literacy.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Introduction to Sustainability
Description: Introduction to the issues and practices related to sustaining functioning economic, social, cultural, and political systems as well as a supportive and healthy physical and biological environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Introduction to Sustainability
Description: Introduction to the issues and practices related to sustaining functioning economic, social, cultural, and political systems as well as a supportive and healthy physical and biological environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Introduction to Sustainability
Description: Lab designed to apply the concepts presented in Introduction to Sustainability. Methods include site observation and measurement, digital modeling, and in-person simulations. Introduction to the tools available to support sustainability planning, and preparation for students to make informed decisions that help to sustain functioning environmental, economic, and cultural systems.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
credits: 2 hours. 1 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Landscape Construction Processes and Materials
Description: The range of materials used in the built environment by landscape architects: metals, concrete masonry, glass, plastics, wood. Emphasis on understanding the properties of these materials and the implications for design.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Place, Society, and Design
Description: An investigation of relationships between the physical environment, social structures, and the design, planning, and management of places. Topics include the influence of physical environment on human behavior and well-being, cultural meanings and place attachment, and how social forces (including design and planning) shape places.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: History of the Built Environment I: Landscape
Description: Landscape architecture from ancient times to the present. Emphasizes the relationship between landscape architecture and culture, aesthetics, and the environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: History of the Built Environment I: Landscape
Description: Landscape architecture from ancient times to the present. Emphasizes the relationship between landscape architecture and culture, aesthetics, and the environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: History of the Built Environment II: Architecture
Description: Architecture from ancient times to the present. Emphasizes the relationship between architecture and culture, aesthetics, and the environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: History of the Built Environment II: Architecture
Description: Architecture from ancient times to the present. Emphasizes the relationship between architecture and culture, aesthetics, and the environment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio III
Description: Analysis of plant elements and form. Emphasis on plant function in the landscape composition. Basic problems in planting design of small scale areas with emphasis on orientation, arrangement, and human needs. Course will include one project that involves inventory and analysis.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio III
Description: Analysis of plant elements and form. Emphasis on plant function in the landscape composition. Basic problems in planting design of small scale areas with emphasis on orientation, arrangement, and human needs. Course will include one project that involves inventory and analysis.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio IV
Description: The design of housing and mixed-use projects which focus on the issues of community and privacy at a variety of scales from single family dwellings to new towns.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio IV
Description: The design of housing and mixed-use projects which focus on the issues of community and privacy at a variety of scales from single family dwellings to new towns.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Engineering Processes and Materials
Description: The forming and building of landscapes with emphasis on the values of "sustainability." Includes introduction to landscape engineering: grading, drainage, and roadway alignment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
credits: 2 hours. 1 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Applied Landscape Engineering
Description: Applied grading, drainage, and road alignment.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Plants of the South
Description: Plant materials of the southern United States with an emphasis upon the ornamental attributes, cultural requirements and tolerances, historical origins, and ecological characteristics of plants used in landscape architecture. The course will cover both native and introduced species.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Plants of the South
Description: Plant materials of the southern United States with an emphasis upon the ornamental attributes, cultural requirements and tolerances, historical origins, and ecological characteristics of plants used in landscape architecture. The course will cover both native and introduced species.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
credits: 3 hours. 1 hours lecture and 4 hours lab per week.
title: Edible Landscape Design
Description: The design and implementation of edible and educational landscapes where food production, soil health, water use, and human needs support each other. Students will work on a community project that emphasizes selecting plants for multiple functions: food production, soil health, comfort and beauty, and pest management.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Residential Design
Description: Use and selection of plants for environmental design.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
credits: 3 hours. 2 hours lecture and 2 hours lab per week.
title: Planning, Design, and Analysis
Description: Approaches to planning, design, and analysis techniques in landscape architecture. The relationship between applied theories and methods and the environmental, social, and cultural context of projects.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio V
Description: Master planning and site design at a variety of scales, with emphasis on the role of regional culture and ecosystems. Though the context for sites may be urban or rural, emphasis will be on inventory, analysis, and appropriate sustainable design practices.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio V
Description: Master planning and site design at a variety of scales, with emphasis on the role of regional culture and ecosystems. Though the context for sites may be urban or rural, emphasis will be on inventory, analysis, and appropriate sustainable design practices.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture
title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio VI
Description: Urban design and architecture. Projects will be developed through master plan and site specific scales focusing on the relationship between landscape architecture, architecture, and urban design.

subject: LAND - Landscape Architecture

Description: The nature and composition of the English vocabulary, with particular attention to Greek and Latin elements, and its development among diverse cultures and societies; techniques of morphological analysis, allomorphy, derivational morphology, formal and semantic change, and Indo-European etymology.

subject: LING - Linguistics

subject: LING - Linguistics
