title: Introduction to Music Education
Description: Provides an introduction to the music education profession. It will examine practices and principles of music teaching and learning, historical foundations of American music education, and sociological, political, and curricular influences that have shaped its development. It will provide an opportunity for students to take a panoramic view of the profession and critically reflect upon issues of school music teaching and their role as music educators. Field experience in the schools will be required.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Sophomore Applied Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the sophomore year.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Introduction to Composition
Description: Applied instruction for music composition and theory majors in for the first semester of the sophomore year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Sophomore Applied Instruction and Recital
Description: Applied instruction and recital for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the sophomore year. Required for BM-Music Performance majors and AB-Music majors but optional for all other undergraduate music degrees.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Introduction to Composition II
Description: Applied instruction for composition majors for the second semester of the sophomore year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: African Music Ensemble
Description: An ensemble performing choral, dance, and instrumental music from Africa including sacred, secular, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: African American Percussive Music: From Africa to the Americas
Description: Traditional and contemporary African American percussion music beginning with its African heritage and tracking its development throughout the Americas, with particular emphasis on the United States. Teaching/learning strategies include in-class performance, demonstrations, audiovisuals, and lectures. No previous music performance background is required.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: World Music Survey: Africa, Europe, and the Americas
Description: Surveys music cultures of Africa, Europe, and the Americas excluding western art music. An exploration of their structures, forms, instruments, performance practices, contexts, and roles in social, cultural, and global systems.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: World Music, the West, and the East
Description: Interrogates the East-West divide in music and allied fields. Drawing on anthropological, ethnomusicological, feminist, and postcolonial forms of analysis, participants will explore practices of representation and the structures, forms, instruments, performance practices, contexts, and aestheticization of the East-West binary in social, cultural, and political systems.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Music Therapy Practicum III
Description: Intermediate level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Music Therapy Practicum IV
Description: Continuation of intermediate level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the United States
Description: Music-making and composition in the United States from the colonial period through the twenty-first century. The genres and styles covered include folk, popular, theatre, band, and art music traditions.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Skills and Fundamentals for Elementary School Teachers
Description: The basic skills and fundamentals of music for the elementary and early childhood classroom teacher.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Creativity in Music
Description: Where does music come from? When, why, and how did people first start making music? What forms does creativity take in music? How do music creators turn raw inspiration into finished pieces? How do improvisers create music on the spot? How do composers create notes for many instruments playing at once? Can anyone create music, or is that something only for composers? This course will provide many and varied answers to these questions and more.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Techniques and Experiences for Children
Description: Methods and field experience for music education majors. Course consists of a survey of effective teaching techniques, research in learning, and materials, including use of technology and multicultural materials.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Composition Lab
Description: Elementary exercises and study of composition for non-music majors and music majors not majoring in composition.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the Western Tradition Pre-1750
Description: History of western music from its beginnings through the Baroque era.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the Western Tradition Post-1750
Description: The history of western music from the Classical style period to the present day.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Instrumentation and Arranging
Description: Instrumentation and Arranging is the first course in orchestration. Instrument ranges and colors will be learned and discussed. After learning ranges, colors, and uses, students learn to arrange for the orchestra. Common doublings up to three- and four-part arrangements are learned and discussed. Other compositional techniques will be discussed.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Guitar Techniques
Description: Basic principles and methods of guitar performance and pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Guitar Skills for Therapists
Description: Functional guitar skills and repertoire appropriate for use in therapeutic work.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Jazz Pedagogy
Description: An overview of jazz curriculum development, rehearsal techniques, and performance for secondary school teachers and prospective teachers.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Percussion Techniques for Music Therapists
Description: Percussion methods course for music therapy majors that will cover the following topics: introduction of African percussion instruments, tone production techniques, the djembe drum, the Afro-Cuban conga and quinto. In addition, the course covers an introduction to the drumset, drumset improvisation, and performance techniques.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy
Description: Presents structure and function of the singing mechanism, current research in physical development, maturation, learning and skill acquisition and the application of these to vocal instruction for individuals and groups; research and class presentations utilizing electronic media; and service-learning vocal instruction experience with area community partners.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy II
Description: A historical overview of vocal instruction from primary and secondary resources, examination of methods and materials relevant to group and individual settings; research and class presentations. Students enrolled in this course are recommended to obtain membership in professional organizations (MTNA, NATS, MENC).

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Pedagogy I
Description: Piano teaching, surveying elementary methods and materials for teaching beginners.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Keyboard Musicianship
Description: Functional keyboard skills for piano performance majors and music theory majors.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Technique and Repertoire
Description: Class piano elective for undergraduate music majors who have successfully completed Piano Class III. Students will develop their keyboard technique and reading through etudes and piano repertoire of various genres (classical, contemporary, sacred).

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Introduction to Conducting
Description: Basic principles, techniques, and methods of conducting and interpretation.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Choral Conducting
Description: Rehearsal, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for choral organizations.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Band Conducting
Description: Rehearsals, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for band organizations.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Orchestra Conducting
Description: Rehearsal, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for orchestra.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Accompanying
Description: Practical experience in chamber music, piano duets, and accompanying.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Introduction to Songwriting
Description: The components of American popular song from the perspective of the developing songwriter. Following successful examples, techniques to improve studentsʼ expressive and artistic songwriting potential will be applied, culminating in performance of a finished song. Relevant aspects of music production and music business will also be addressed.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Theory for Non-Majors
Description: The fundamentals of music and their application in composition and analysis.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music and Media
Description: An overview study of music in film, television, games, videos, and multimedia. Music for film and other media is about “helping tell the story” of the film, show, or game play. We will be critically analyzing the underscore (and songs) for various genres to help gain an understanding of how underscore works to help tell the story.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Applied Music Instruction for the Non-Music Major
Description: Applied music instruction (instrumental or vocal) offered at all levels through enrollment in the University of Georgia Community Music School.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 16 hours credit.
title: Applied Music Instruction for Music Minors
Description: Applied instruction for music minors in a musical instrument or voice.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Junior Applied Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the junior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Junior Composition Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the junior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Junior Applied Instruction and Recital
Description: Applied instruction and recital for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the junior year and performance of a junior recital.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Applied Composition Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the second semester of the junior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: String Pedagogy
Description: Instruction in pedagogy for all bowed string instruments. Class and studio teaching methods will be explored.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Instrumental Pedagogy
Description: Principles of teaching and learning appropriate for applied instrumental music in brass, woodwinds, strings, guitar, piano, and percussion.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Applied Instruction for the Musical Theatre Certificate Program
Description: Applied instruction in voice for students enrolled in the Musical Theatre Certificate Program.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Junior Recital in Music
Description: Required recital for music majors in a musical instrument, voice, or composition.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Directed Independent Study in Music
Description: Independent research topics in any field of music directed by a faculty member.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Introduction to Music Technology
Description: Provides an overview of technologies essential to professional musicians in the 21st century. Meeting in the MuTec lab, this course offers hands-on instruction in a variety of relevant music software. Coursework is primarily creative projects, with some written examination on fundamentals.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Music Therapy Practicum V
Description: Senior level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes more in-depth assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Music Therapy Practicum VI
Description: Continuation of senior level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes more in-depth assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Summer Music Therapy Practicum
Description: Practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients at beginner, intermediate, and advanced student levels. Includes observation, assisting, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Music Therapy Internship
Description: In-depth experience of clinical training in a professional setting. Experience in all aspects of music therapy practice in preparation for Board Certification.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Double Reed Making Seminar
Description: Oboe and bassoon players will learn how to create and finish reeds for their instruments. The course will cover the fundamentals of making a blank, exploring different reed scrapes and styles, and focus on detailed finishing techniques.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: A Technician's Guide for the Pianist
Description: Covers piano nomenclature, how pianos work, what to consider when buying a new or used piano, how to care for your piano, an in-depth look at the services that piano technicians provide, and communicating with your piano technician.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Music in the City
Description: In New York City, students will attend jazz performances and Broadway shows, tour recording facilities used for soundtracks, attend a seminar on the American Federation of Musicians, learn about union function, spend individual time with working musicians, and keep a small book on experiences to share with the class.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Filmscoring in LA Intensive Field Study
Description: Field study course designed to provide first-hand exposure to Filmscore professionals in LA. Students will visit composers' studios, scoring stages with an orchestral recording session, studio music heads, music supervisors, and music editors, as well as be introduced to the professional practices of these areas through these meetings.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Music Theory Review
Description: Visual and aural skills for entering graduate students in need of remediation.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the Real World
Description: Music graduates face new challenges in today's professional landscape, including fewer traditional jobs. Students will build relevant skills and tools that emphasize versatility and flexibility to better prepare them for career success in this evolving landscape.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Alexander Technique
Description: Introduction to the practice and principles of the Alexander Technique, which enables musicians to practice and perform their instrument with less tension and a greater freedom of movement.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Music Recording Practicum
Description: Audio techniques, technologies, and critical listening will be applied towards recording, mixing, editing, and mastering live and archived recordings for the UGA HHSOM. Working in a professional studio environment equips students with skills needed to succeed in audio recording, while also empowering them in their performance, teaching, and research endeavors.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Diction Methods
Description: Students will demonstrate pedagogical application of IPA and diction principles suitable for error detection and correction in a choral or solo vocal teaching setting.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Interpreting Popular Music
Description: Exploration of analytical methodologies for interpreting and understanding various forms of what one might describe as “popular music.” Readings from music theory guide analyses, student-led discussions, and projects. Students are evaluated on presentations, concert reviews (with an emphasis on Athens music), and a capstone final project/presentation that entails a conference proposal suitable for submission to music theory conferences.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Modal Counterpoint
Description: The study of counterpoint of the Renaissance, with emphasis on model composition and analysis of the vocal music of Lassus, Josquin, Morley, and Palestrina.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Form and Analysis
Description: Analysis of form focusing on music from the seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth centuries.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Tonal Counterpoint
Description: The study of counterpoint of the Baroque, with emphasis on model composition and analysis of the keyboard works of J.S. Bach.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Twentieth-Century Counterpoint
Description: An investigation of the extension of contrapuntal techniques based on 20th-century repertory. Classes will focus on practical techniques and repertory, including student discussion and analysis of examined works.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Analysis of Non-Tonal Music
Description: Introduces basic concepts for the analysis of non-tonal music from the twentieth- and twenty-first centuries, focusing on theories and analysis of pitch, rhythm, form, and other elements in works from this time period. Content for the course will vary depending on the instructor, and aural skills and listening strategies are part of the course’s evaluation.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Analysis of Texted Music
Description: Detailed analytical exploration of texted music. The course begins with a preliminary section that reviews harmony and small form and considers analytical methods for interpreting texts. After that preparatory unit, the course progresses into an in-depth study of how composers and musicians use a text to convey an array of meanings. To facilitate delivery, the course’s contents are organized according to genre and/or conceptual area.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Dissolution of Tonality
Description: Poses the questions “What do we mean by tonality?” and “How can we describe music when it challenges the norms of tonality?” Through diverse repertory (much of it from the 19th and early 20th centuries), techniques designed for tonal, chromatic, and post-tonal music are synthesized and expanded to explore answers to those questions.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Exploring Math and Music
Description: Provides opportunities for students to survey the rich intersections of mathematics and music. Classes will be organized around broad topics (such as proportions, modular arithmetic, networks, and geometry) and will involve equal parts discussion and exploration. Assessment will include small homework exercises and open-ended, student-proposed projects. (The class requires no specific mathematical knowledge, beyond what is typical for a music major.)

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Special Topics in Composition and Music Technology
Description: Changing series of topics in composition and music technology that are not covered in other courses.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Special Topics in Music Theory and Analysis
Description: Changing series of topics in music theory and analysis that are not covered in other courses.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Ancient, Medieval, and Renaissance Music
Description: Music from Greek and Roman society to the death of Josquin (c. 1520).

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Late Renaissance and Baroque Music
Description: Musical styles and genres from the 16th century through Bach and Handel.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the Classic Period
Description: Chamber, orchestral, keyboard, and operatic works from the middle and late eighteenth century.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music in the Romantic Period
Description: Emphasis on the development of song, symphony, chamber music, and opera.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Modern Music
Description: Modern trends in music from Schoenberg, Stravinsky, Hindemith, and Bartok to the present.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Women and Music
Description: Roles of women in music, including the history of women musicians in western art music, world cultures, and popular music; gender studies in music.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: History of Opera
Description: Examination of representative operas of each period in historical context. It analyses the roles played in the creation and production of operas by the patron/audience, librettist, composer, singers, conductor, director, machinist, and (when appropriate) film director.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Topics in Musical Cultures of the World
Description: In-depth study of the music of a select culture, area, topic, or genre. Investigates historical aspects, social functions, aesthetic preferences, the musician, musical instruments, structures and forms, performance contexts, and practices.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Instrumental/Vocal/Choral Literature
Description: Solo, sonata, and ensemble music composed for winds, brass, strings, piano and harpsichord, organ or voice, dating from the earliest appropriate period to the present.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Selected Studies in Musicology
Description: Investigation of a special topic not otherwise covered in the curriculum. Topics and instructors vary from one semester to the next.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Seminar in Musicology-Ethnomusicology
Description: Investigation of a special topic not otherwise covered in the curriculum. Topics and instructors vary from semester to semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: African Music
Description: History, styles, and forms of African music. Investigation of historical, cultural and social aspects, contexts and functions, music structures, instruments, genres, structures and indigenous societies, nation-states, and global industry.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Gender and Music Video
Description: Examination of music videos from the 1980s until the present. Music videos will be treated as texts from which we can glean cultural understanding as well as explore new ways of analyzing aesthetic communication and musical meaning.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Gender and Music Video
Description: Examination of music videos from the 1980s until the present. Music videos will be treated as texts from which we can glean cultural understanding as well as explore new ways of analyzing aesthetic communication and musical meaning.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Women and Music
Description: Roles of women in music, including the history of women musicians in Western art music, world cultures, and popular music; gender studies in music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: String Instrumental Techniques
Description: Basic principles and methods of string performance and pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Woodwind Instrumental Techniques
Description: Basic principles and methods of woodwind performance and pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Brass Instrumental Techniques
Description: Basic principles and methods of brass instrument performance and pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 2 hours credit.
title: Percussion Techniques for Music Educators
Description: Basic principles and methods of percussion performance and pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Pre-College Music Theory Pedagogy
Description: Designed primarily to prepare you to teach topics that are typically described as “music theory” to pre-college students. Such topics include several different areas of musicianship including fundamentals, harmony and voice leading, sight-singing, contextual listening, transcription/dictation, and analysis. Designed to be a practical course that places an emphasis on how to teach pre-college music theory topics through effective lesson planning and model teaching.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Melody Harmonization
Description: Course is intended for music therapy majors and explores theoretical and analytical approaches to harmonizing diatonic and chromatic melodies on guitar, piano, and other instruments. Course begins with a review of diatonic and chromatic harmony before moving into alternate forms of harmonic representation that include lead-sheet notation, Nashville numbers, tablature, and chord box reading. The goal of the course is fluency in harmonization, as demonstrated through skills-based assessments, performances, and projects.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Performance and Racialization
Description: Drawing from work in anthropology, sociology, performance studies, and legal theory, this course explores how modern discourses of racialization and performance in the U.S. context emerge from a long history of travel writing, colonial and postcolonial encounters, and other circulations of people and goods throughout the world.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Bollywood and Its Others: Cinema in South Asia
Description: Examination of the ways in which various kinds of identities are constructed and negotiated through the film industries of South Asia. Exploration of narratives of place and their expression through performance underscore processes of social identification across the South Asian subcontinent. Through our study, we will explore mediums and topics such as: religion and myth; colonialism and postcolonialism; gender and sexuality; language and ethnic identity; caste and other forms of discrimination; and the politics of national and subnational identity.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Country Music, Race, and the Idea of America
Description: This interdisciplinary music history course is built around a few basic questions: What is Country Music? Is it a genre? Is it American? If so, why? In this class we’ll explore the complex construction of country music as a 20th-century modern American musical practice.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: History of American Music
Description: A survey of art and vernacular music traditions of the United States.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Pedagogy II
Description: Survey of supplementary teaching materials for elementary and intermediate level piano students.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: English Lyric Diction
Description: Introductory lyric diction course for singers. Fundamentals for singing in English, including symbols and sounds of the International Phonetic Alphabet as applied to English classical song. Applied elements included.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Italian Lyric Diction
Description: Fundamentals for singing in Italian, including symbols and sounds of the International Phonetic Alphabet. Applied elements included with special focus on Italian art song and operatic repertoire.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: French Lyric Diction
Description: Fundamentals for singing in French, including symbols and sounds of the International Phonetic Alphabet, rudimentary grammar, translations for musical terms, and words commonly found in song texts. Applied elements included.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: German Lyric Diction
Description: Fundamentals for singing in German, including symbols and sounds of the International Phonetic Alphabet. Applied elements included with special focus on the Lieder and opera.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Acting for Singers
Description: Students will apply basic theatrical performance techniques to enhance their music performance training, including song interpretation, intentions, objectives, emotional connectivity, movement, active listening, and responding while utilizing their existing vocal technique to achieve a deeper sense of truth and the creation of a more realistic, natural, and nuanced performance.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Performance Anxiety and Focus
Description: Students will learn about the issues regarding performance anxiety and discover solutions to work through these issues. The course will also cover strategies for improving focus, resilience, courage, and perspective. Includes readings from a variety of texts, videos, writing assignments, in-class discussions, and in-class exercises and performances. In-class performances by each student are a required part of the course. These can be in music, theatre, dance, and comedy.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Techniques and Experiences for Children
Description: Methods and field experience for music education majors. Course consists of a survey of effective teaching techniques, research in learning, and materials, including use of technology and multicultural materials.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Choral Techniques and Field Experience
Description: Methods and field experience for music education majors with specialization in choral music. Course involves effective teaching techniques, research in teaching/learning, and materials, including technology and multicultural materials.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Instrumental Techniques and Field Experience
Description: Methods and field experience for instrumental music education majors. Course involves effective teaching techniques, research in teaching/learning, and materials, including technology and multicultural materials.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: World Music Pedagogy
Description: Designed principally for prospective K-12 music teachers as an introduction to the content and context of music in a multiethnic American society. Also, an introduction to a wide array of musics, along with a developing understanding for how to incorporate them in K-12 music classrooms.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Suzuki Violin and Viola Pedagogy I
Description: Course includes the Suzuki Association of the Americas (SAA) Every Child Can!, Violin Book 1, and Viola Book 1, and Group Class Strategies courses. Provides students with skills and resources needed to teach beginning violin and viola to students using the Suzuki method.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Suzuki Violin and Viola Pedagogy II
Description: A continuation of Suzuki Violin and Viola Pedagogy I; provides students with further skills and resources for teaching violin and viola students using the Suzuki method at the Book 2 and 3 levels. Students will be required to provide recorded teaching segments and will include live teaching experiences and feedback.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Suzuki Violin Pedagogy III
Description: A continuation of Suzuki Pedagogy I and II. Will provide students with further skills and resources needed to teach violin students using the Suzuki Association of the Americas Violin Books 4 and 5 levels.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Suzuki Violin Pedagogy IV
Description: The Suzuki Association of the Americas (SAA) Violin Books 6, 7, and 8 courses. It is a continuation of Suzuki Pedagogy I, II, and III and will provide students with further skills and resources needed to teach violin students using the Suzuki Method at the Books 6 through 8 levels.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Media Composition and Production I
Description: An in-depth look at the composition process for media. Both linear (film, tv) and non-linear (game) composing processes will be studied. How does underscore “help tell the story”? How, as composers, do we use themes, harmony, instrumentation, rhythm, and tempo to accomplish these goals? In film scoring, how do we address these ideas as the picture changes? In game scoring, how are these ideas accomplished?

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Media Composition and Production II
Description: A continuation of the concepts of Media Composition and Production I, moving forward into the process of recording live instruments with scores. Students will continue to compose pieces to picture, as well as the continued study of other film scores through score reading and analysis. Different instruments and instrument groups will be studied and recorded with their compositions to picture over the course of the semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Orchestration for Film
Description: A review of instrument ranges and techniques, traditional orchestration in practice, and an in-depth discussion and application of orchestration techniques used in film scores, including practical applications of MIDI and notation software packages.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Game Composition and Production
Description: Students learn to compose and produce tracks or a series of layered tracks to accommodate game scoring or non-linear scoring. Game composers will ask how their music “Helps Tell the Story” of the game, but also how to accommodate non-linear scoring and functions.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Men's Glee Club
Description: Concentration on choral literature for men's voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Women's Glee Club
Description: Concentration on choral literature for women's voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: African American Choral Ensemble
Description: Performance of traditional and contemporary black gospel, spiritual, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2-3 hours lab per week.
title: University Philharmonia
Description: Designed to give students an opportunity to participate in a symphonic ensemble.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 5 hours lab per week.
title: University Symphony Orchestra
Description: Performance of orchestral literature of various styles and genres.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: University Sinfonia
Description: Orchestral ensemble open to music majors and non-majors. Audition required for all players. Ensemble will perform standard orchestral repertoire and accompany opera productions as appropriate.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: University Chorus
Description: Performance of choral literature for mixed voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Guitar Ensemble
Description: This is a performance course open to all guitar majors. Designed to give guitar students experience performing in a large conducted ensemble. Repertoire includes music from a variety of stylistic periods. Open to non-majors; requires ability to read standard notation and a classical guitar. One public performance per semester.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 4 hours lab per week.
title: UGA Hodgson Singers
Description: Performance of choral literature for mixed voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Ensemble
Description: Class piano elective for undergraduate music majors who have completed Piano Class III. Students develop ensemble and reading skills through the study and performance of literature written for piano-four hands, piano-six hands, two pianos, and multi-keyboard ensembles.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Studio Orchestra
Description: Provides an opportunity for students to perform in a unique ensemble setting that combines the instrumentations of a traditional jazz ensemble with a chamber orchestra. This type of ensemble has been historically used in movie soundtracks, Broadway show orchestras, recording, and concert settings.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Jazz Ensemble I
Description: Advanced level big band. This ensemble is made up of traditional instrumentation of saxophones, trombones, trumpets, piano, bass, drums, and guitar. This ensemble performs a difficult level of music from a variety of jazz styles, including swing, be-bop, Latin jazz, and contemporary.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Jazz History
Description: Aural identification of factual stylistic knowledge of the major works, stylistic trends, and performance practices in twentieth-century jazz. Awareness of the major composers and geographical areas of influence in jazz from the late nineteenth century to the present. Development of a vocabulary for discussing jazz compositions, jazz performance, and improvisation. Demonstrable ability to process and write about music heard in concerts and in the class.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Jazz Improvisation I
Description: The study of chords and corresponding scales and how they are used in jazz context. Students will practice the skill of creating melodies on all chord/scales qualities. Students will study a variety of song forms used in the jazz style, 12-bar major blues, 12-bar minor blues, 32-AABA song form.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Jazz Ensemble II
Description: Introductory level jazz big band. Instrumentation is saxophones, trombones, trumpets, plus rhythm section, including piano, bass, drums, and guitar. This ensemble rehearses music from all eras of big band jazz from Duke Ellington through contemporary composers. Students are accepted by audition.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit. 4 hours lab per week.
title: Jazz Improvisation II
Description: Introduction to 12-bar blues form and rhythm changes. Compositional styles from Louis Armstrong, the Swing Era, Be-bop, and modern jazz will be studied and performed. The concept of rhythm in each of these styles will be studied.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Jazz Private Applied
Description: Study of jazz theory with in-depth analysis of chord/scale relationships based on standard period compositions. Study of performance and compositional styles.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Chamber Music Ensemble
Description: Directed chamber music experiences in variable instrumental and vocal catagories (percussion, clarinet, trombone, etc.).

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit. 1-2 hours lab per week.
title: Jazz Improvisation
Description: The study and performance of jazz improvisation styles from the 1930's to the present through listening, analysis, practical application (applied study), and performance.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Viola Orchestral Excerpts: Literature and Training
Description: A study of the orchestral excerpt literature, with training in performance and auditioning. The goal is to develop the student's familiarity with standard orchestral audition excerpts and give the student opportunity to learn and perform these excerpts, practice style, and prepare for auditions through mock audition and video audition practice.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Contemporary Chamber Ensemble
Description: Performance of post-1950 literature and commissioned works for small and large ensembles. Guided rehearsal time is limited. Major 20th- and 21st-century work will be presented each fall semester. The spring semester is a "lab" environment for composers, performers, and conductors as each prepares and performs commissioned works by UGA composers.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Senior Applied Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the senior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Senior Composition Instruction
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the senior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Senior Applied Instruction and Recital
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the senior year and performance of a senior recital.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Senior Composition Instruction and Recital
Description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the senior year and performance of a senior recital.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Collegium Musicum
Description: Performance of early music through the Baroque.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Redcoat Marching Band
Description: Ensemble performance of a wide variety of music and movement designed for athletic and other University events.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: University Band
Description: An ensemble open to all University students interested in performing a wide variety of quality band literature.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Concert Band
Description: A concert band open to all students who have had significant previous experience in instrumental music.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 4 hours lab per week.
title: Symphonic Band
Description: Performance of a wide variety of original compositions and transcriptions written for band.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Wind Symphony
Description: Performance of new and standard wind compositions with concentration on advanced scores.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit. 6 hours lab per week.
title: Wind Ensemble
Description: Performance of large ensemble and chamber compositions with concentration on advanced scores and contemporary repertoire. Professional level experience.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Orchestral Percussion and Timpani Repertoire Class
Description: Delves deeply into the standard orchestral repertoire most commonly seen at percussion and timpani auditions, thus exposing students to a study of the orchestral literature in a deep and thorough manner. Students will be expected to study and familiarize themselves with the works prior to each meeting.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3 hours lab per week.
title: Opera Ensemble
Description: Study and performance of operatic literature including, as appropriate, large fully-staged works, one-act operas, and concert presentations of arias, duets, and ensembles.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 3-6 hours lab per week.
title: Opera Theater
Description: Designed for students assigned to major roles in opera productions. Includes general principles of opera production, as well as coaching in singing and acting appropriate to the selected production.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Applied Ethnomusicology: African Music
Description: Performance of African music, including styles, techniques, and movement in instrumental and vocal music. Repertoire for study and performance drawn from various regions and cultures on a rotating basis.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Asian Music Ensemble
Description: An ensemble performing folk, classical, and contemporary music of China, Japan, Korea, Indonesia, or India.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Latin American Music Ensemble
Description: An ensemble performing folk, classical, popular, nationalistic, and contemporary music and dance of Latin America including countries in North, Central, and South America as well as the Caribbean.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Near East Music Ensemble
Description: An ensemble performing folk, classical, nationalistic, and contemporary music of the Middle East, Eastern Europe, and the Mediterranean region.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 10 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: British Brass Band
Description: The British Brass Band ensemble trains brass players for the musical, technical, and physical demands of their instrument. Playing in the band will enhance finger and tongue dexterity, improve reading skills, benefit embouchure endurance, and increase musical awareness and unit cohesion as sections and a full band.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Chamber Orchestra
Description: Chamber orchestra for strings. Preparation and performance of chamber music from the Baroque period to the present.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Opera Orchestra
Description: Orchestra created specifically for presentation of UGA opera. Preparation and performance of operatic literature.

subject: MUSI - Music

Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

Description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Undergraduate Theory Thesis
Description: Independent research in music carried out under the direction of an area faculty member.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Advanced Steel Drum Band
Description: The Steel Pan Ensemble provides students with the opportunity not only to study the traditional music of Trinidad, but also to experience this music through performance. Students will also learn about the history and evolution of the steel pan.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Jazz Combos
Description: Performance of works in a variety of styles from swing to modern jazz in a small group setting.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music for Childhood
Description: Literature, techniques, and methodologies for teaching children music in a diverse society; a study of children's musical development.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Early Childhood Musical Development
Description: Musical development of children from birth through age eight years emphasizing auditory perception, auditory discrimination, responses of children to music, modes of learning music, and children's acquisition of musical performance skills, and understandings.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Computer-Assisted Instruction in Music
Description: Programming and testing CAI music lessons.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Jazz in New York and London
Description: Students will spend semesters studying the evolution of jazz in New York City. This historical perspective covers the 1920's to the present. Students will examine recordings, important musicians, composers, as well as jazz venues and recordings done in the UK. Students will accompany instructor to live performances in London.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 9 hours credit.
title: Jazz Studies in Europe
Description: In Europe, students will attend professional jazz rehearsals, performances, and recording sessions. Students will have discussion time with professionals. There will be interaction with conservatory students in Germany and Amsterdam. Students will keep a daily journal to be shared with the group upon return.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Violin Orchestral Repertoire Class
Description: Preparation and performance of standard orchestral audition repertoire excerpts for violin, as well as mock audition experience. Students are expected to familiarize and prepare the assigned repertoire prior to each meeting.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: Repertory Singers
Description: Repertory Singers is a small choral ensemble geared to provide a real-world, laboratory, and recital conducting experience for graduate conducting students, while offering the singers in the ensemble unique insights into conducting gesture, rehearsal techniques, group motivational dynamics, and other topics relevant to choral music education and the choral art.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit. 2 hours lab per week.
title: UGA Choral Project
Description: UGA Choral Project is a highly select chamber choir designed to emulate the model and standards of a professional chamber choir. The number of singers will vary depending on the particular project. Auditions are open to everyone and will be advertised in advance of the first rehearsal. UGA Choral Project will rehearse and perform on a condensed timeline, and attendance at all rehearsals and performances is required. Full self-preparation of repertoire is expected.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Marching Band Techniques
Description: Methods and techniques for organizing and training marching bands; planning music, drills, formations, and shows.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Advanced Conducting
Description: Choral and instrumental conducting methods and techniques with application in laboratory situations.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Choral Literature and Performance Practice
Description: Choral music, including multicultural materials, suitable for all levels and voices.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Principles of Music Therapy
Description: Music as human behavior and its uses as therapeutic intervention with various populations.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Psychology of Music
Description: Acoustical and psychological aspects of music with emphasis upon problems of perception, experimental aesthetics, musical function, measurement and diagnosis of musical ability.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Influence of Music on Behavior
Description: Physiological effects of music, the relation of music to health, and the place of music in the habilitative and rehabilitative process.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Therapy Assessment
Description: Practical application of music therapy in an assigned clinic, along with seminars to analyze effectiveness, in-depth interactions, intervention strategies, and accountability measures.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music Skills for Therapists
Description: Skill development in voice and on social instruments for use in the therapeutic treatment of various age groups. Includes improvisation, transposition, and self-accompanied performance of a variety of repertoire.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music for Exceptional Children
Description: Trends in special education, characteristics and needs of those classified as exceptional, curriculum development, and intervention strategies. Mainstreamed and self-contained settings will be discussed.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Internship in Music Teaching
Description: This service-learning, practicum-based course will provide supervised teaching experience in public school and/or community musical settings. The course will emphasize practical teaching skills, including lesson planning, sequencing, communication, motivation, and assessment. Seminar discussions and faculty observation and feedback will build on the weekly practicum.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 8 hours credit.
title: Media Composition Instruction
Description: Applied instruction in media composition.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Electroacoustic Composition
Description: Electronic music composition techniques, focusing on composing stereo and quadraphonic fixed-media works, music for fixed-media and instrument, and the study of electroacoustic music circa 1948 to today.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Interactive Composition
Description: Electronic music composition techniques, focusing on interactive systems, live electronic music, and multimedia applications, and current trends in music utilizing interactive technologies. Semester also includes recording studio workshops.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Audio Foundations
Description: Overview of the theory and practice of audio recording. Topics include analog audio, digital audio, transducers, recording techniques, editing, signal processing, mixing, and acoustics.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Critical Listening
Description: Learning to listen critically to classical music recordings allows recording engineers to formulate educated opinions and make good decisions when capturing new recordings. Topics include musical balance, sound quality, stereo imaging, depth of image, signal processing, artifacts, acoustic signatures, and other qualities.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Classical Recording
Description: Hands-on introduction to the equipment and training in the process which comprises a typical classical (acoustic performance) recording project. Topics include venue assessment, positioning of performers, mic techniques, use of spot mics, recording “takes,” the roles of the engineer and producer, creating an Edit Decision List (EDL), editing, and mixing/mastering.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Overdub Recording
Description: Hands-on introduction to the equipment and training in the process which comprises a recording project in which additional performances are “overdubbed” onto a base track. Topics include venue assessment, positioning of performers, mic techniques, use of spot mics, isolation, recording "overdubs,” the roles of the engineer and producer, punching in/out, comping, and mixing/mastering.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Album Recording
Description: As a class, record an album for commercial release for a Hugh Hodgson School of Music ensemble. Topics include pre-production, venue assessment, positioning of performers, mic techniques, use of spot mics, recording “takes,” the roles of the engineer and producer, creating an Edit Decision List (EDL), editing, and mixing/mastering.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 5 hours credit.
title: DMA Recording
Description: Taking all of the previously learned skills from the Classical Recording curriculum, students in this course will create a capstone recording project for a student in DMA performance.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music and Media Internship
Description: An in-depth experience of working in music and media or media composition in a professional setting. This includes a media composer’s or other music and media professional’s studio or a music editor’s professional studio.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 6 hours credit.
title: Senior Recital in Music
Description: Required recital for music majors in a musical instrument, voice, or composition, normally taken during the first or second semester of the senior year.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-3 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Directed Independent Study
Description: Independent research topics directed by a faculty member at the masters level.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Trends and Issues in Music Education
Description: Current trends and issues in music education, the historical and social foundations of American music education, music education bibliography, and the role of research in music education.

subject: MUSI - Music

Description: Current trends and issues in music education, the historical and social foundations of American music education, music education bibliography, and the role of research in music education.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Elements of Music Theory
Description: Focusing on repertoire from 1685 to 1900, this course will both reinforce and deepen students' understanding of the principles that govern tonal music. Begins with a review of fundamental concepts and proceeds to a study of species counterpoint, diatonic harmony, chromatic harmony, small-scale and large-scale forms, recent analytical methods, and theory pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music

Begins with a review of fundamental concepts and proceeds to a study of species counterpoint, diatonic harmony, chromatic harmony, small-scale and large-scale forms, recent analytical methods, and theory pedagogy.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Theory Pedagogy for Music Educators
Description: Prepares students to teach topics that are typically described as “music theory” to pre-college students. Such topics include several different areas of musicianship — most notably fundamentals, harmony and voice leading, sight singing, dictation, and analysis.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Music History Problems
Description: Western music literature, styles, genres, and composers from the medieval period to the present day.

subject: MUSI - Music

subject: MUSI - Music

Description: Library research, documentation, and writing.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Performance and Ethnography
Description: Designed to equip graduate students with methodological and epistemological tools for doing ethnographic and archival fieldwork in expressive cultural contexts. Students will consider writing, transcription, notation, archiving practices, and audio/visual recording as ethnographic modes within shifting disciplinary and ethical contexts.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Woodwind Pedagogy
Description: Designed to cover the various teaching techniques and resources available for woodwind pedagogy. Students will research different teaching styles, observe applied lessons, and practice applied teaching in various settings. Topics covered are: basics of pedagogy, teaching fundamentals, phrasing and interpretation, setting up and running a studio.

Description: Course allows students to set and maintain writing goals, create methodologies, conduct research, and receive extra writing help from faculty and colleagues.

Description: Basic concepts, types, and techniques of research as they apply to music education. Students plan and conduct individual research projects.

subject: MUSI - Music

Description: Advanced principles, techniques, and methods of conducting and interpretation.

Description: Thesis writing under the direction of the major professor.

subject: MUSI - Music

subject: MUSI - Music

Description: Philosophy, design, implementation, and supervision of curriculum for music programs in the public schools.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 2 hours. Repeatable for maximum 4 hours credit.
title: Instrumental Literature and Performance Practice
Description: Instrumental music, including multicultural materials, suitable for all levels of instruction for band, orchestra, and chamber music.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Trends and Issues in Music Therapy
Description: In-depth study of foundations and principles of music therapy and current developments in music therapy theory and practice. Review of current clinical and research literature in music therapy and related fields. Discussion of emerging models and trends in music therapy practice.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Research in Music Therapy
Description: A course designed to acquaint students with the techniques, tools, and methodologies used in music therapy research.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Seminar in Professional Music Therapy Practice
Description: Survey of music therapy applications with various populations, conducted in seminar format. Each student will choose a specific population to research and will facilitate presentations and class discussions of characteristics, indications and contraindications for music therapy, assessment and evaluation tools, treatment models, and interventions for each population chosen.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1 hour. Repeatable for maximum 3 hours credit.
title: Advanced Music Therapy Practicum
Description: This course focuses on the development of advanced competence in clinical music therapy practice, particularly in the areas of clinical supervision, clinical administration, clinical skills, and personal development and professional role.

subject: MUSI - Music
credits: 1-6 hours. Repeatable for maximum 12 hours credit.
title: Graduate Professional Project in Music Therapy
Description: Research study or clinical program development. Student will make an original scholarly/clinical contribution to the field of music therapy through applied research, which will be expressed through a written document and an oral presentation in a professional public venue.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy
Description: Presents structure and function of the singing mechanism, current research in physical development, maturation, learning and skill acquisition and their application to vocal instruction in group and individual settings; research and class presentation utilizing electronic media; and service- learning vocal instruction experience with area community partners.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy II
Description: Vocal instruction from primary and secondary resources, examination of methods and materials relevant to group and individual settings; research and class presentations. Students enrolled in this course are recommended to obtain membership in professional organizations (MTNA, NATS, NAfME).

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Pedagogy I
Description: Learning theories, methodologies, and materials.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Piano Pedagogy II
Description: Repertoire, motivation, and related issues of personalities/learning styles.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Group Piano Pedagogy
Description: Explores group piano teaching methods and strategies, materials, and technologies. Course material is delivered through lectures, discussions, readings, and observation of students in pre-college, college, and adult (Recreational Music Making) class settings, as well as through a peer-teaching practicum.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Directed Observations in Piano Pedagogy
Description: Observational field experience in off-campus private piano teaching studios.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Final Project in Piano Pedagogy
Description: The following options are available for the Final Project in Piano Pedagogy: written document, public lecture, lecture recital, or workshop. The Final Project is under the direction of the major professor.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy III
Description: Supervised experience in P-adult instruction in school and community-based educational settings. Includes a weekly seminar and participation in service projects. Seminars include discussions with local educators and UGA faculty on current topics in vocal instruction. Students are encouraged to obtain membership in professional organizations (MTNA, NATS, NAfME).

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Current Topics in Music Pedagogy
Description: An overview of teaching practices, theories, research, and ideas relating to the instruction of music in a variety of settings. Open to all graduate music majors, this course will include coverage of studio teaching as well as group and class instruction.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Vocal Pedagogy for the Choral Conductor
Description: Study of voice science and pedagogy topics with special emphasis on the effective teaching of singing in choral settings.

subject: MUSI - Music
title: Community Engagement for Performers
Description: Students will explore the idea of an Artist as Citizen and the concept of the "teaching artist," an increasingly common description for performers who are reaching out to the community to make meaningful connections between the music we perform and a diverse audience.

Description: Applied lessons at the masters level.

Description: A study of piano accompanying repertoire (instrumental duo, concerto, art song, opera) through the lens of essential skills for the aspiring collaborative pianist. The repertoire for a specific elective under the umbrella of this course may be limited to either vocal or instrumental repertoire.

Examples include (but are not limited to) a recital tour, national audition, commissioning project, or cross-disciplinary project.

Description: Professional development for careers in nutritional sciences, including culinary science, nutrition, and dietetics. subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

Students will engage in self-reflection and build competency in the promotion of equity, diversity, and inclusion in health and nutrition.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

Description: The role of energy intake, macronutrients, and micronutrients in obesity prevention and management throughout life, including during the preconceptual period, pregnancy, lactation, infancy, childhood, adolescence, middle-age, and the older adult years. Emphasis on evidence-based strategies for the general public and health practitioners to improve nutrition and prevent and manage obesity.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

Description: Provides an overview of community and public health nutrition topics for graduate students enrolled in the Community Nutrition Online M.S. degree program to gain knowledge, skills, and research methodology in identifying and addressing nutrition and health problems in communities through community-based nutrition interventions and policies.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences
title: Global Health and Food Systems
Description: Explores complex relationships among food, culture, and disease through a food systems approach. Examines food policies at local, national, and global levels assessing their impact on health through phenomena such as child malnutrition, obesity, globalization of the Western Diet, food insecurity, food safety, food marketing, and the rise of diet-related noncommunicable diseases.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences
title: Trending Topics in Nutrition
Description: Current trending topics in nutrition. Specific course topics will depend on current newsworthy nutrition-related events, stories, etc. An overlying theme across all topics includes focusing on critical thinking, triangulation of resources, and translating nutrition messages to the public. Students will explore current hot topics across various aspects of nutrition and practice critiquing and interpreting trending topics with peer-reviewed, published research.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

Description: Literature of human nutrition related to macronutrients; includes metabolism, genetics, physiology, biochemistry, endocrinology, and epidemiology.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

A major focus will be on developing a comprehensive nutrition intervention program for a selected target group.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences

Description: Role of health professionals in supporting health and performance of competitive athletes, recreational athletes, and others engaged in physical activity and exercise through interpretation and application of evidence-based recommendations for food, nutrient, fluid, and supplement intakes, nutritional assessment, body composition, and weight management, and understanding the scope of professional practice.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences
title: Nutrition and Neuroscience
Description: How do we know when it is time to eat and when we should stop? How does diet impact thoughts, memories, and behavior? How nutrition affects the brain and cognitive functions along with the role of the central nervous system in regulating eating behavior and body weight.

subject: NUTR - Nutritional Sciences
title: Child Growth, Diet, and Disease
Description: Diet and disease considerations in the setting of child and adolescent health. Intended for current and future researchers and providers of children and adolescents. subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Policy Process
Description: An introduction to roles of governmental structures and policy-making procedures in the policy process. In addition, the course covers an array of policy areas and topics, including both cost-benefit analysis and ethical analysis. The core focus is on policymaking in the United States.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Program Evaluation
Description: Provides a broad training in policy evaluation concepts and methods and provides the tools needed to apply quantitative techniques to the assessment of policy decisions.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Bureaucracy and the Law
Description: Basic introduction to administrative law and the role of regulatory and other administrative agencies in the governing process. The primary focus will be on United States administrative law, but systems in other countries will be discussed as well.

Description: The legal principles and practical doctrines involved in the work of administrative agencies, vested with quasi-legislative or quasi-judicial powers.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Public Administration and Democracy
Description: Administrative organization, relations, and controls facing the contemporary public management in the United States. The institutional, political, and normative environment of the public manager in democratic society. Among the questions considered is the problem of reconciling bureaucratic government and democratic principles.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Public Personnel Administration
Description: Procedures and problems of governmental personnel administration. Included in the topics are classification, performance appraisal, hiring practices, affirmative action, and pay equity. Studies of governmental agencies are employed to give the students first-hand knowledge of governmental personnel administration.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Public Financial Administration
Description: Activities involved in the collection, custody and expenditure of public revenue, such as the assessment and collection of taxes, public borrowing and debt administration, the preparation and enactment of the budget, financial accountability and the audit. In addition, the course covers politics of the budgetary process.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Economic Foundations in Policy Analysis
Description: Introduction to the basic tools and analytical techniques needed for the analysis of public policies. Emphasis is placed on the application of principles of microeconomic theory as applied to policy analysis.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Public Management
Description: Major concepts and theories associated with the modern public organization. Organizational environments, goals and effectiveness, strategy and decision-making, structure and design, communication, leadership, individual work behaviors, and other topics. The implications of the public sector context and political environments for these topics.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Socialization Seminar in Public Administration
Description: An introduction to the profession of public administration for incoming MPA students, with emphasis on law, ethics, communications, professionalism, and cohort building.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
title: Capstone Paper and Portfolio
Description: This culminating experience requires students to demonstrate mastery of MPA degree program competencies through a written paper demonstrating critical reflection upon a sample of work from the MPA program.

subject: PADP - Public Administration and Policy
